(These readers do not lengthen the vowel of the question particle ʾa- before hamzah, ʾa-ʾantum(ū) → ha-ʾantum(ū); since they read it with a long vowel, it can only be interpreted as demonstrative hā + ʾantum(ū).) Whoever takes it as a demonstrative and makes a distinction between (applying overlength to) long vowels depending on whether (the following hamzah) occurs within or without a word boundary, must not add overlength to the ʾalif, regardless of whether the hamzah after it is pronounced hard or pronounced soft (i.e., there is no overlength for Qālūn or ʾAbū ʿAmr hā .antum or al-Bazzī’s hā ʾantumū, because hā is considered a separate word if it is understood as a demonstrative and those readers do not have overlong vowels before hamz across word boundaries). Those who take it as an interrogative among those who pronounce the ʾalif overlong only within word boundaries must add length to it regardless of whether the hamzah is pronounced hard or soft (i.e., ʾAbū ʿAmr, Qālūn when taking it as an interrogative pronounce it hâ.antum, and al-Bazzī as hâʾantum(ū)). All of this is based on general principles and happens because of those manners.[24]

footnotes.text: Al-Dānī’s description is somewhat imprecise and unclear here. Ibn al-Ǧazarī understands the description as indicating ha.antum (Ibn al-Ǧazarī 2018, §1512). However, since al-Dānī interprets the

The words hā ʾantumū are seen as having a word-boundary between them. As Ibn Kaṯīr does not have an overlong vowel with long vowels before hamzah between two words, this is not lengthened (see U.11.2.).
This refers to a recognised possibility by grammarians to replace the hamzah of the interrogative particle ʾa- with a hāʾ (Saeed 2023, 83).
See U.11.1. for the insertion of an ʾalif with the question particle ʾa- before hamz.

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads ʾa-.an yuʾtā with length[25] as a question, while the rest have it without length as a non-interrogative statement (i.e., ʾan).

footnotes.text: Note that al-Dānī refers to a hamzah followed by another hamzah pronounced bayna bayn as madd ‘length’. This is ambiguous because he also calls a hamzah followed by ā madd. The wording therefore also allows the reading ʾān. Al-Dānī is explicit that the intended reading is ʾa-.an in his Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 970).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥamzah read yuʾaddih ʾilayka, lā yuʾaddih ʾilayka and nuʾ/ūtih minhā in two places (here and in Q3:145) and in al-Nisāʾ nuwallih and nuṣlih (Q4:115), and in ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf[26] nuʾ/ūtih minhā (Q42:20) without a vowel on the hāʾ in all seven. Qālūn reads it with a shortened[27] kasrah on the hāʾ (i.e., yuʾaddihi, etc.), and al-Ḥulwānī[28] transmits it like that from Hišām for all that is mentioned in this entry. The rest read it with full pronunciation of the kasrah (i.e., yuʾaddihī, etc.). In pause all of them pronounce them without a final vowel (i.e., yuʾaddih#, etc.).

footnotes.text: An alternate name for Sūrat al-Šūrā (Kandil 1992, 51).

Iḫtilās normally means ‘ultrashort’, but it is technically a relative term, i.e., shorter than its ʾaṣl ‘base’. As the base is yuʾaddihī, iḫtilās should be simply understood here to mean a normal-length kasrah, -hi. See I.4.2.
The Taysīr only has ʾisnāds for Hišām that go through al-Ḥulwānī. The Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān has other paths, but few seem to have explicit information on this topic (al-Dānī 2007, 980–81).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir reads tuʿallimūna l-kitāba with ḍammah on the tāʾ, fatḥah on the ʿayn and kasrah on the geminate lām. The rest read it with fatḥah of the tāʾ, an ungeminated lām and no vowel on the ʿayn (taʿlamūna).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah and Ibn ʿĀmir read wa-lā yaʾmurakum with naṣb of the rāʾ and the rest read it with rafʿ (i.e., yaʾ/āmurukum(ū)). ʾAbū ʿAmr reads it according to his principle with an ultrashort vowel or no vowel (i.e., yaʾ/āmurŭkum, yaʾ/āmurkum).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads an-nabiyyīna limā with kasrah of the lām and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., lamā). Nāfiʿ reads ʾātaynākum with nūn and ʾalif according to the plural. The rest read it with a tāʾ carrying a ḍammah according to the singular (ʾātaytukum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ḥafṣ and ʾAbū ʿAmr read yabġūna with yāʾ and Ḥafṣ reads wa-ʾilayhi yurǧaʿūna with yāʾ. The rest read both with tāʾ (i.e., tabġūna and turǧaʿūna; ʾAbū ʿAmr has yabġūna but turǧaʿūna).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ḥiǧǧu l-bayti with kasrah on the ḥāʾ and the rest read it with fatḥah (ḥaǧǧu).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-mā yafʿalū min ḫayrin fa-lan yukfarūhu with yāʾ for both and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tafʿalū … tukfarūhu).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read lā yaḍurrukum with ḍammah of the ḍād and rafʿ in the rāʾ with gemination (of the rāʾ). The rest read it with kasrah of the rāʾ and with apocopation of the rāʾ (i.e., yaḍirkum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads munazzalīna and in al-ʿAnkabūt ʾinnā munazzilūna (Q29:34) with gemination in both. The rest read it without gemination (i.e., munzalīna, munzilūna).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim read musawwimīna with kasrah on the wāw and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., musawwamīna).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read sāriʿū without wāw before the sīn and the rest with wāw (i.e., wa-sāriʿū).[29]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 140).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read qurḥun in both places (in this verse) and al-qurḥu (Q3:172) with ḍammah on the qāf for all three places. The rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., qarḥun, al-qarḥu).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads wa-kâʾin whenever it occurs with an overlong ʾalif and after it a hamzah that carries a kasrah. The rest read it with a hamzah that carries a fatḥah after the kāf and a geminate yāʾ that carries a kasrah, and after that no vowel at all on the nūn (i.e., ka-ʾayyin). We have already mentioned it in the chapter on pausing on what is written in the script.[30] The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read qātala maʿahū with ʾalif and fatḥah of the qāf and tāʾ. The rest read it with ḍammah of the qāf and kasrah on the tāʾ and without ʾalif (i.e., qutila).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read ar-ruʿub and ruʿuban with an extra vowel whenever they occur. The rest read it without extra vowel (i.e., ar-ruʿb and ruʿban).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read taġšē ṭāʾifatan with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaġšā/ǟ). ʾAbū ʿAmr reads kulluhū li-llāhi with rafʿ and the rest with naṣb (i.e., kullahū).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-ḷḷāhu bi-mā yaʿlamūna baṣīrun with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taʿlamūna).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū Bakr read muttum, muttu and mutnā with ḍammah on the mīm whenever they occur. Ḥafṣ follows them with ḍammah in the two words that occur in this sūrah only (i.e., Q3:157 muttum and Q3:158 muttum). The rest read it with kasrah on the mīm (i.e., mittum, mittu, mitnā). Ḥafṣ reads ḫayrun mimmā yaǧmaʿūna with yāʾ and the rest read it with tāʾ (i.e., taǧmaʿūna).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim read ʾan yaġulla with fatḥah on the yāʾ and ḍammah on the ġayn. The rest read it with ḍammah on the yāʾ and fatḥah on the ġayn (i.e., yuġalla).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Hišām reads mā quttilū with gemination of the tāʾ and the rest read it ungeminated (i.e., qutilū).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads allaḏīna quttilū, and in al-Ḥaǧǧ ṯumma quttilū (Q22:58) with gemination of the tāʾ in both. The rest read it without gemination (i.e., qutilū). Hišām, according to my recitation to ʾAbū al-Fatḥ, reads wa-lā yaḥsabanna llaḏīna quttilū with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taḥsa/ibanna).[31]

footnotes.text: Hišām is only transmitted through tilāwah by ʾAbū al-Fatḥ in the Taysīr (see U.4.4.2.), but the specific mention of ʾAbū al-Fatḥ implies that al-Dānī knows other tilāwah transmission from Hišām that has taḥsabanna. This is indeed the case, as he points it out in the Ǧamiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 994).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads wa-ʾinna ḷḷāha lā yuḍīʿu with kasrah on the hamzah, and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., wa-ʾanna).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads wa-lā yuḥzinka, la-yuḥzinunī (Q12:13) and li-yuḥzina llaḏīna (Q58:10) with ḍammah on the yāʾ and kasrah on the zāy whenever it occurs, except for His speech in al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ (Q21:103) lā yaḥzunuhum, where he applies a fatḥah on the yāʾ and a ḍammah on the zāy. The rest does it like that for all of them (i.e., wa-lā yaḥzunka etc.).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads wa-lā taḥsabanna llaḏīna kafarū and wa-lā taḥsabanna llaḏīna yabḫalūna (Q3:180) with tāʾ in both. The Kufans read lā taḥsa/ibanna llaḏīna yafraḥūna (Q3:188) with tāʾ. The rest read yāʾ in all three (i.e., yaḥsa/ibanna).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ḥattā yumayyiza here and in al-ʾAnfāl (Q8:38) with ḍammah on the yāʾ, fatḥah on the mīm and kasrah on the geminate yāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ, kasrah on the mīm and no vowel on the yāʾ (i.e., yamīza).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read bimā yaʿlamūna ḫabīrun with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taʿlamūna).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads sa-yuktabu with a yāʾ carrying ḍammah and with fatḥah on the tāʾ, qatluhum with rafʿ of the lām and wa-yaqūlu with yāʾ. The rest read it with a nūn carrying fatḥah, ḍammah on the tāʾ, naṣb of the lām and nūn on yaqūlu (i.e., sa-naktubu … wa-qatlahum(ū) … wa-naqūlu).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Hišām reads wa-bi-z-zuburi wa-bi-l-kitābi with the addition of bāʾ to both. [And like this Hišām wrote it in his book from his teachers from Ibn ʿĀmir and he told that the rasm was like this in his muṣḥafs].[32] Farīs b. ʾAḥmad reported to me, and he said: ʿAbd al-Bāqī b. al-Ḥasan reported to us and said: al-Ḥulwānī was doubtful about this, so he wrote to Hišām about it, and he answered that the bāʾ is present on both words (i.e., wa-bi-z-zuburi wa-bi-l-kitābi). Ibn Ḏakwān reads it with the addition of bāʾ to az-zuburi only (i.e., wa-bizuburi wa-l-kitābi), and the rest without the bāʾ on both (i.e., wa-z-zuburi wa-l-kitābi).[33]

footnotes.text: This is an addition in one of the manuscripts that Pretzl consulted. Al-Ḍāmin includes it without making mention of manuscripts that lack it. I have found it in both the Berlin and Paris manuscripts, and in one of the four Princeton manuscripts (Islamic Manuscripts, Garrett no. 213Y). It is unlikely to be an addition of later copyists; it has either been dropped out, or it points to a later recension of al-Taysīr with this added by al-Dānī. Hišām indeed appears to have had a book describing Ibn ʿĀmir’s reading, and al-Dānī had access to it, as he cites it several times in his Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān as well (Hamdan 2018, 55, fn. 4).
This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 140).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and ʾAbū Bakr read li-yubayyinunnahū and wa-lā yaktumūnahū with yāʾ on both, and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., li-tubayyinunnahū and wa-lā taktumūnahū).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read fa-lā yaḥsibunnahum(ū) with yāʾ and ḍammah on the bāʾ. The rest read with tāʾ and fatḥah on the bāʾ (i.e., taḥsa/ibannahum).

statements.heading: F.3. Sūrat ʾĀl ʿImrān
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and Ibn ʿAmīr read quttilū here[34] and in al-ʾAnʿām allaḏīna qattalū (Q6:140) with gemination of the tāʾ in both words. The rest read it without gemination for both (i.e., qutilū, qatalū). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read qutilū wa-qātalū and in al-Tawbah (Q9:111) fa-yuqtalūna wa-yaqtulūna, so they begin with the passive before the active in both. The rest begins with the active before the passive (i.e., qātalū wa-qutilū/quttilū, fa-yaqtulūna wa-yuqtalūna).

footnotes.text: The word hunā is missing in Pretzl (al-Dānī 2008a, 36).

statements.heading: F.3.1. [Yāʾs of Q3]
statements.text: There are six yāʾs: 1. wa-waǧhiya li-llāhi (Q3:20) is read with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ. 2. minniya ʾinnaka (Q3:35) and 3. ʾaǧʿal liya ʾāyatan (Q3:41) are read with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 4. Nāfiʿ reads with fatḥah both ʾinniya ʾuʿīḏuhā (Q3:36) 5. and man ʾanṣāriya ʾilà ḷḷāhi (Q3:52). 6. The two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr read ʾanniya ʾaḫluqu with fatḥah.

statements.heading: F.3.2. [Removed yāʾs of Q3]
statements.text: There are two removed ones: 1. Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr retain [the yāʾ] in connected speech of wa-man ittabaʿanī (Q3:20). 2. ʾAbū ʿAmr retains [the yāʾ] in connected speech of wa-ḫāfūnī ʾin kuntum (Q3:175).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: The Kufans read tasāʾalūna without gemination of the sīn and the rest read it with gemination (i.e., tassāʾalūna). Ḥamzah reads wa-l-ʾarḥāmi with ḫafḍ of the mīm and the rest with naṣb (i.e., wa-l-(ʾ)arḥāma).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read qiyaman without ʾalif and the rest with ʾalif (i.e., qiyāman).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: ḍiʿē/āfan ḫē/āfū has already been mentioned.[35]

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr and Ibn ʿĀmir read sa-yuṣlawna with ḍammah on the yāʾ and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., sa-yaṣlawna).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads wa-ʾin kānat wāḥidatun with rafʿ and the rest with naṣb (i.e., wāḥidatan). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read fa-li-ʾimmihī in the two words (in this verse), in al-Qaṣaṣ fī ʾimmihā (Q28:59) and in Zuḫruf fī ʾimmi l-kitābi (Q43:4), with kasrah on the hamzah in all four when pronounced in connected speech. The rest pronounce it with ḍammah in both contexts (in connected speech and when starting on the word) (i.e., fa-li-ʾummihī, fī ʾummihā and fī ʾummi l-kitābi). When al-ʾumm is made plural and there is kasrah next to its hamzah—this altogether occurs in four places: in al-Naḥl min buṭūni ʾimma/ihātikum (Q16:78), and like that in al-Nūr (Q24:61), in al-Zumar (Q39:5) and al-Naǧm (Q53:32)—Ḥamzah applies the kasrah to the hamzah and the mīm (i.e., ʾimmihātikum) in connected speech, whereas al-Kisāʾī applies the kasrah to the hamzah in connected speech but fatḥah to the mīm (i.e., ʾimmahātikum). The rest applies ḍammah to the hamzah and fatḥah to the mīm (i.e., ʾummahātikum) in both contexts (connected speech and starting on the word). When starting on the word, everybody reads all these places with ḍammah on the hamzah in the singular (i.e., ʾummihī etc.), and ḍammah on (the hamzah) and fatḥah on the mīm in the plural (i.e., ʾummahātikum(ū)). Ibn Kaṯīr, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū Bakr read yūṣā bihā in both places (Q4:11, 12) with fatḥah on the ṣād and Ḥafṣ follows them only in the second case. The rest read it with kasrah on the ṣād on both (i.e., yūṣī bihā).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read nudḫilhu in both instances of the word (Q4:13, 14) with nūn and the rest with a yāʾ (i.e., yudḫilhū̆).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads wa-llaḏânni [here], in Ṭāhā hāḏânni (Q20:63), in al-Ḥaǧǧ hāḏânni (Q19:22), in al-Qaṣaṣ hātayyyynni (Q28:27) and in Fuṣṣilat ʾarnā llaḏayyyynni (Q41:29) with gemination of the nūn and making the ʾalif and yāʾ overlong before it in these five cases. The rest read it without gemination, without making the ʾalif and the yāʾ overlong (i.e., wa-llaḏāni, hāḏāni, hātayni).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read kurhan here and in al-Tawbah (Q9:53) with ḍammah on the kāf and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., karhan). Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū Bakr read bi-fāḥišatin mubayyanatin here, in al-ʾAḥzāb (Q33:30) and in al-Ṭalāq (Q56:1) with fatḥah on the yāʾ. The rest read it with kasrah for all of them (i.e., mubayyinatin).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads al-muḥṣināt and muḥṣināt with kasrah on the ṣād whenever it occurs, except for the first occurrence in this sūrah, al-muḥṣanāt min an-nisāʾi (i.e., Q4:24). The rest read them with fatḥah on the ṣād (i.e., al-muḥsanāt, muḥṣanāt). Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-ʾuḥilla lakum with ḍammah on the hamzah and kasrah on the ḥāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on both (i.e., ʾaḥalla).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read fa-ʾiḏā ʾaḥṣanna with fatḥah on the hamzah and the ṣād. The rest read it with ḍammah on the hamzah and kasrah on the ṣād (i.e., ʾuḥṣinna).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: The Kufans read tiǧāratan with naṣb and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., tiǧāratun).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads madḫalan here and in al-Ḥaǧǧ (Q22:59) with fatḥah on the mīm. The rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., mudḫalan).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and al-Kisāʾī read wa-salù ḷḷāha min faḍlihī, wa-salhū̆ and fa-sal illaḏīna and what is like it without hamzah when it is an imperative and before the sīn there is a wāw or a fāʾ. Ḥamzah does the same according to his regular principle in pause.[36] The rest read it with hamzah (i.e., wa-sʾal, wa-sʾalū, wa-sʾal-hu, fa-sʾal).

footnotes.text: See U.11.6.1. The phrase ‘in pause’ is missing in the Pretzl edition. This must be a mistake (al-Dānī 2008a, 263).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: The Kufans read wa-llaḏīna ʿaqadat without ʾalif and the rest read it with ʾalif (i.e., ʿāqadat).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read al-baḫal here and in al-Ḥadīd (Q54:24) with fatḥah on the bāʾ and ḫāʾ. The rest read it with ḍammah on the bāʾ and no vowel on the ḫāʾ (i.e., al-buḫl).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: The two of the holy cities read wa-ʾin taku ḥasanatun with rafʿ and the rest with naṣb (i.e., ḥasanatan).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read law tassawwā/ǟ with fatḥah on the tāʾ and gemination of the sīn. Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read it with fatḥah on the tāʾ but no gemination of the sīn (i.e., tasawwē). The rest read it with ḍammah of the tāʾ and no gemination of the sīn (i.e., tusawwā).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾa-wa-lamastum here and in al-Māʾidah (Q5:6) without ʾalif. The rest read it with ʾalif (i.e., ʾa-wa-lāmastum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: fatīlan // i/unḏ̣ur,[37] ʾinna ḷḷāha ni/aʿ(i/ĭ)mmā (Q4:58),[38] in i/uqtulū (Q4:66)[39] and ʾaw i/uḫruǧū[40] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads ʾillā qalīlan minhum with naṣb and with an ʾalif when pausing (i.e., qalīlā#). The rest read it with rafʿ (i.e., qalīlun) and pause on it without ʾalif (i.e., qalīl#).[41]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 140).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and Ḥafṣ read ka-ʾan lam takun with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yakun).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-lā yuḏ̣lamūna fatīlan, that is the second one (to occur in this sūrah, the first being Q4:49), with yāʾ. The rest read it with tāʾ (i.e., tuḏ̣lamūna). There is no disagreement with the first in that it is with yāʾ.

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥamzah read bayyaṭ⸗ṭāʾifatun minhum with assimilation of the tāʾ to the ṭāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the tāʾ and without assimilation (i.e., bayyata ṭāʾifatun).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-man ʾaẓdaqu, yaẓdifūna,[42] taẓdiyah, yuẓdira/yaẓduru, qaẓd and what is like it, whenever an unvowelled ṣād occurs with a dāl afterwards, with ʾišmām of the zāy to the ṣād (i.e., ẓ [zˁ]). The rest pronounced it with pure ṣād (i.e., ʾaṣdaqu, etc.).

footnotes.text: Pretzl has يصْ دقون. This does not occur in the Qurʾān (al-Dānī 2008a, 36).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read fa-taṯabbatū in both places, here and in al-Ḥuǧurāt (Q49:6), with tāʾ and ṯāʾ of (the verb) al-taṯabbut. The rest read it with yāʾ and nūn (i.e., fa-tabayyanū). Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾilaykumu s-salama lasta muʾ/ūminan, and it is the last one (treated this way, the other cases of ʾilaykumu s-salama [Q4:90, 91] are read this way by all) without the ʾalif. The rest read it with ʾalif (i.e., as-salāma).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read ġayra ʾulì ḍ-ḍarari with naṣb of the rāʾ and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., ġayru).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and ʾAbū ʿAmr read fa-sawfa yuʾ/ūtīhi ʾaǧran with yāʾ and the rest with nūn (i.e., nuʾ/ūtīhi).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and ʾAbū Bakr read yudḫalūna l-ǧannata here, in Maryam (Q19:60) and Ġāfir (Q40:40) with ḍammah on the yāʾ and fatḥah on the ḫāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ and ḍammah on the ḫāʾ (i.e., yadḫulūna).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: The Kufans read ʾan yuṣliḥā with ḍammah on the yāʾ, without a vowel on the ṣād and kasrah on the lām. The rest read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ, ṣād and lām, with gemination of the ṣād and retention of the ʾalif after it (i.e., yaṣṣālaḥā).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamzah read wa-ʾin talū with ḍammah on the lām and no vowel on the wāw. The rest read it without a vowel on the lām and after it two wāws, the first of which carries a ḍammah and the second carries no vowel (i.e., talwū).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: The Kufans and Nāfiʿ read allaḏī nazzala and allaḏī ʾanzala with fatḥah on the nūn, hamzah and zāy. The rest read it with ḍammah on the nūn [and hamzah], and with kasrah on the zāy (i.e., nuzzila, ʾunzila).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: ʿĀṣim reads wa-qad nazzala with fatḥah on the nūn and zāy. The rest read it with ḍammah on the nūn and kasrah on the zāy (i.e., nuzzila).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: The Kufans read fì d-darki without a vowel on the rāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., ad-daraki).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads sawfa yuʾtīhim ʾuǧūrahum with yāʾ and the rest with nūn (i.e., nuʾ/ūtīhim(ū)).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Warš reads lā taʿaddū with fatḥah on the ʿayn and gemination of the dāl. Qālūn reads it with an ultrashort vowel on the ʿayn (bi-ʾiḫfāʾi ḥarakati l-ʿayn) and gemination of the dāl (taʿăddū) but texts transmitted from him have it without a vowel (i.e., taʿddū).[43] The rest read it with no vowel on the ʿayn and no gemination on the dāl (taʿdū).

footnotes.text: Qālūn had a book that described his recitation of Nāfiʿ (Hamdan 2018, 37). It appears that this early work lacked the sophistication to express the concept of an epenthetic ultrashort vowel, and thus he described it as bi-ʾiskān ‘without a vowel’. However, the oral tradition apparently places an epenthetic vowel here. See also the discussion in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 1020–21) where al-Dānī seems to explicitly prefer the taʿddū reading calling it ʾāṯar ‘better supported by sources’.

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads sa-yuʾtīhim with yāʾ and the rest with nūn (sa-nuʾtīhim(ū)).

statements.heading: F.4. Sūrat al-Nisāʾ
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads zubūran here, in Subḥān[44] (Q17:55) and in al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ fì z-zubūri (Q21:105), in these three places with ḍammah on the zāy. The rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., zabūran, az-zabūri). In this sūrah, there are no yāʾs that are disagreed upon at all.

footnotes.text: Again, Pretzl has ୚ඤن for Subḥān (al-Dānī 2008a, 267). Subḥān is an alternative name for Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ (Kandil 1992, 50).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read šanʾānu qawmin in two places (here and in Q5:8) with no vowel on the nūn, and the rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., šanaʾānu). Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read ʾin ṣaddūkum(ū) with kasrah on the hamzah and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., ʾan).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ read wa-ʾarǧulakum with naṣb of the lām and the rest with ǧarr (i.e., ʾarǧulikum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: al-muḥṣanāt[45] and ʾaw lamastum[46] (Q5:6) have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read qulūbahum qasiyyatan with gemination of the yāʾ and without ʾalif. The rest read it without gemination and with ʾalif (i.e., qāsiyatan).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: rus(u)lunā has already been mentioned.[47]

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read li-s-suḥuti in three places (here, Q5:62 and Q6:63) with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and the rest read it without a vowel (li-s-suḥti).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads wa-l-ʿaynu bi-l-ʿayni and what comes after it (i.e., wa-l-ʾanfu bi-l-ʾanfi wa-l-ʾuḏunu bi-l-ʾuḏuni wa-s-sinnu bi-sinni, wa-l-ǧurūḥu) with rafʿ. Ibn Kaṯīr, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū ʿAmr only have the rafʿ for al-ǧurūḥu. The rest read all of these with naṣb (i.e., wa-l-ʿayna bi-l-ʿayni, etc.). Nāfiʿ reads al-(ʾ)uḏna bi-l-(ʾ)uḏni and fī ʾuḏnayhi (Q31:7) with no vowel on the ḏāl whenever it occurs, and the rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., al-ʾuḏuni, etc.).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads wa-li-yaḥkuma ʾahlu with kasrah on the lām and naṣb on the mīm. The rest read it with no vowel on the lām and ǧazm on the mīm (i.e., wa-l-yaḥkum). Warš applies the vowel of the hamzah of ʾahlu to it (the mīm) in accordance with his general principle (i.e., wa-l-yaḥkum‿ahlu).[48]

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads tabġūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yabġūna).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: The two of the holy cities and Ibn ʿĀmir read yaqūlu llāḏīna without wāw before the yāʾ. The rest read it with wāw. ʾAbū ʿAmr applied the naṣb to the lām (i.e., wa-yaqūla) but the rest read it with rafʿ (i.e., wa-yaqūlu).[49]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 140).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read man yartadid with two dāls where the second one carries no vowel. The rest read it with one geminate (dāl) that carries a fatḥah (man yartadda).[50]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 140).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read al-kuffē/āri ʾawliyāʾa with ḫafḍ of the rāʾ, and the rest with naṣb (al-kuffāra).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads ʿabuda with ḍammah on the bāʾ and aṭ-ṭāġūti with ḫafḍ of the tāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the bāʾ and naṣb of the tāʾ (i.e., ʿabada ṭ-ṭāġūta).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū Bakr read fa-mā balaġat risālātihī in the plural with kasrah on the tāʾ, and the rest read it in the singular with naṣb of the tāʾ (i.e., risālatahū).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾal-lā takūnu with rafʿ of the nūn and the rest with naṣb (i.e., takūna).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: Ibn Ḏakwān reads bimā ʿāqattum with ʾalif without gemination, but ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read it without gemination and without ʾalif (i.e., ʿaqattum). The rest read it with gemination and without ʾalif (i.e., ʿaqqattum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: The Kufans said fa-ǧazāʾun with nunation and miṯlu mā with rafʿ of the lām. The rest read it without nunation and with ḫafḍ of the lām (i.e., fa-ǧazāʾu miṯli mā). Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read ʾaw kaffāratu ṭaʿāmi as a construct and the rest read it with tanwīn and rafʿ of the mīm (i.e., ʾaw kaffāratun ṭaʿāmu). They did not disagree on the pluralisation of masākīna here.[51]

footnotes.text: Unlike F.2:184. and F.34:15., where the miskīn/masākīn is disagreed upon.

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads qiyaman li-n-nāsi without ʾalif and the rest with ʾalif (i.e., qiyāman).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads min allaḏīna staḥaqqa with fatḥah on the tāʾ and ḥāʾ and, when starting (on this word), kasrah on the ʾalif (i.e., #ʾistaḥaqqa). The rest read it with ḍammah on the tāʾ and kasrah on the ḥāʾ (i.e., stuḥiqqa) and, when they start (on this word), with ḍammah on the ʾalif (i.e., #ʾustuḥiqqa). ʾAbū Bakr and Ḥamzah read ʿalayhi/umu l-ʾawwalīna in the plural and the rest read al-ʾawlayāni in the dual.

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr and Ḥamzah read al-ġiyūb with kasrah on the ʿayn whenever it occurs (here and Q5:116; Q9:78; Q34:48), and the rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., al-ġuyūb).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: ṭayran/tāʾiran[52] and qud(u)s[53] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾillā sāḥirun here, in Hūd (Q11:7) and in al-Ṣaff (Q61:6), with an ʾalif in all three cases. The rest read it without ʾalif (i.e., siḥrun).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads hat⸗tastaṭīʿu rabbaka with tāʾ, assimilation of the lām and naṣb of the bāʾ. The rest read it with yāʾ and rafʿ of the bāʾ (hal yastaṭīʿu rabbuka).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read ʾinnī munazziluhā with gemination and the rest without gemination (i.e., munziluhā).

statements.heading: F.5. Sūrat al-Māʾidah
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads hāḏā yawma with the naṣb of the mīm and the rest with the rafʿ (i.e., yawmu).

statements.heading: F.5.1. [Yāʾs of Q5]
statements.text: There are six yāʾs: 1. yadiya ʾilayka (Q5:28) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ. 2. ʾinniya ʾaḫāfu (Q5:28) and 3. liya ʾan ʾaqūla (Q5:116) both with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 4. ʾinniya ʾurīdu (Q55:29) and 5. fa-ʾinniya ʾuʿaḏḏibuhū both with fatḥah for Nāfiʿ. 6. wa-ʾummiya ʾilāhayni (Q5:116) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ.

statements.heading: F.5.2. [Removed yāʾs of Q5]
statements.text: There is a removed one: wa-ḫšawnī wa-lā (Q5:44) maintains (its yāʾ) in connected speech by ʾAbū ʿAmr.

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read man yaṣrif with fatḥah on the yāʾ and kasrah on the rāʾ. The rest read it with ḍammah of the yāʾ and fatḥah of the rāʾ (i.e., yuṣraf).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ṯumma lam yakun with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., takun). Ibn Kaṯīr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read fitnatuhum(ū) with rafʿ and the rest with naṣb (i.e., fitnatahum). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-ḷḷāhi rabbanā with naṣb of the bāʾ and the rest with ḫafḍ (i.e., rabbinā).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ḥamzah and Ḥafṣ read wa-lā nukaḏḏiba and wa-nakūna with naṣb, both the bāʾ and the nūn. Ibn ʿĀmir only reads nakūna with naṣb. The rest read both with rafʿ (i.e., wa-lā nukaḏḏibu, wa-nakūnu).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads wa-la-dāru l-ʾāḫirati with a single lām and ḫafḍ of the tāʾ.[54] The rest read it with two lāms and rafʿ of the tāʾ (i.e., wa-la-d-dāru l-(ʾ)āḫiratu).[55] Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read ʾa-fa-lā taʿqilūna here and in al-ʾAʿrāf (Q7:169) with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaʿqilūna).

footnotes.text: The Pretzl edition renders it incorrectly with two lāms. It should read وუჸار اগᔃজൡൿة. Corrected by al-Ḍāmin (al-Dānī 2008a, 274).
This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 140).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read lā yukḏibūnaka without gemination, and the rest with gemination (i.e., lā yukaḏḏibūnaka).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads ʾa-ra.aytum, ʾa-ra.ayta, ʾa-fa-ra.ayta and what is like it[56] with a softening of the hamzah which comes after the rāʾ whenever there is hamzah before the rāʾ. Al-Kisāʾī drops (the hamzah) regularly (i.e., ʾa-raytum, ʾa-rayta, ʾa-fa-rayta). The rest pronounce the hamzah (i.e., ʾa-raʾaytum(ū), etc.), but Ḥamzah in pause follows Nāfiʿ.[57]

footnotes.text: This is different from the modern practice of Warš in the path of al-ʾAzraq, which allows this option, but seems to prefer replacing the hamzah with ā, thus creating overlong vowels like ʾa-râytum because the ā stands before a two-consonant cluster (Ibn al-Ǧazarī 2018, §1501–2).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads fattaḥnā ʿalayhim here, in al-ʾAʿrāf (Q7:96) and al-Qamar (Q54:11) and he reads futtiḥat in al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ (Q21:96), with gemination of the tāʾ in all four. The rest read it without gemination (i.e., fataḥnā, futiḥat).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ibn ̣ʿĀmir reads bi-l-ġudwati here and in al-Kahf (Q18:28) with wāw and ḍammah on the ġayn. The rest read it with ʾalif and fatḥah on the ġayn (i.e., bi-l-ġadāti).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read ʾannahū man ʿamila and fa-ʾannahū ġafūrun raḥīmun with fatḥah on both hamzahs. Nāfiʿ only placed fatḥah on the first (i.e., ʾannahū man ʿamila but fa-ʾinnahū ġafūrun raḥīmun). The rest read it with kasrah on both (i.e., ʾinnahū man ʿamila, fa-ʾinnahū ġafūrun raḥīmun).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-li-yastabīna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., wa-li-tastabīna). Nāfiʿ reads sabīla l-muǧrimīna with naṣb of the lām and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., sabīlu).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: The two of the holy cities and ʿĀṣim read yaquṣṣu with ṣād that carries a ḍammah. The rest read it with ḍād that carries a kasrah (i.e., yaqḍi), and when they pause on it, they view it as having no yāʾ following the written text (i.e., yaqḍ#, not yaqḍī#).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads tawaffēhu rusulunā and istahwēhu (Q6:71) with ʾalif with ʾimālah, and the rest read both with tāʾ (i.e., tawaffathū̆ and istahwathū̆).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads wa-ḫifyah here and in al-ʾAʿrāf (Q7:55) with kasrah on the ḫāʾ. The rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., wa-ḫufyah). The Kufans read la-ʾin ʾanǧā/ēnā with ʾalif without yāʾ and the rest with yāʾ and tāʾ (i.e., ʾanǧaytanā).[58]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 140).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: The Kufans and Hišām read qul illāhu yunaǧǧīkum with gemination and the rest read it without gemination (i.e., yunǧīkum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads ʾimmā yunassiyannaka with gemination and the rest without gemination (i.e., yunsiyannaka).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, ʾAbū Bakr and Ibn ʿĀmir read reʾē kawkaban, reʾē ʾaydiyahum, reʾēhu and what is like it for its pronunciation, whenever there is no unvowelled letter after the yāʾ (i.e., ʾalif maqṣūrah not followed by ʾalif al-waṣl), with ʾimālah of the fatḥah of both the rāʾ and hamzah. Al-Naqqāš, transmitting from al-ʾAḫfaš (← Ibn Ḏakwān), makes an exception from that which is followed by a pronominal suffix, for example, raʾāka, raʾāhā, raʾāhu, fa-raʾāhu with fatḥah on both the rāʾ and the hamzah. I recited it in that way to al-Fārisī, transmitting from him, and ʾAbū al-Fatḥ also taught me to recite like this, transmitting from his recitation to ʿAbd al-Bāqī from his companions from al-ʾAḫfaš.[59] Warš pronounces (the vowels) of rāʾ and hamzah in between the two sounds for all of it (i.e., räʾǟ, räʾǟhu, etc.). ʾAbū ʿAmr only applies ʾimālah to the hamzah (i.e., raʾē), and it was transmitted from ʾAbū Šuʿayb [al-Sūsī] in the same way as Ḥamzah (i.e., reʾē). The rest read both with fatḥah (i.e., raʾā).

footnotes.text: This transmission path is not present in U.4.4.1. but it is mentioned in al-Dānī’s Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 334).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ḥamzah and ʾAbū Bakr read reʾà l-qamara, reʾà š-šamsa and what is like it, whenever the yāʾ (i.e., ʾalif with ʾimālah) encounters a vowelless letter in the next word, with ʾimālah only on the rāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., raʾà l-qamara, raʾà š-šamsa). This is in the case in connected speech, but if you divide it from the quiescent letter (that follows) in pause, there is disagreement in accordance with what has preceded in (the discussion on) raʾā/reʾē/räʾǟ kawkaban (see F.6:76. above). Ḫalaf has transmitted from Yaḥyā [b. ʾĀdam] from ʾAbū Bakr [Šuʿbah],[60] and more than one from ʾAbū Šuʿayb [al-Sūsī] that there is ʾimālah of the fatḥah of the rāʾ and the hamzah in all of this, like the first (i.e., Q6:76) too (i.e., ʾAbū Bakr reads reʾē kawkaban/reʾè l-qamara; al-Sūsī reads reʾē kawkaban/reʾè l-qamara). ʾAbū ʿAmr (al-Dānī) said: I have recited it in both ways. ʾAbū Ḥamdūn and ʾAbū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [Ibn al-Yazīdī] transmitted it from al-Yazīdī with ʾimālah of the fatḥah of the hamzah (i.e., raʾè l-qamara), just like in the first case (i.e., raʾē kawkaban). All of this is sound and practiced.

footnotes.text: This ʾisnād for Šuʿbah is not present in U.4.5.1., but it is mentioned in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 345). This same transmission is also reported by Ibn Muǧāhid, where the ʾisnād is likewise not present in the ʾisnād section (Ibn Muǧāhid 1972, 261).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir, with disagreement in transmission from Hišām, read ʾa-tuḥāǧǧūnī without gemination on the nūn and the rest read it with gemination (i.e., ʾa-tuḥāǧǧūnnī).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: The Kufans read narfaʿu daraǧātin here and in Yūsuf (Q12:76) with tanwīn, and the rest without tanwīn (i.e., daraǧāti).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-l-laysaʿa here and in Ṣād (Q38:48) with a geminate lām and no vowel on the yāʾ. The rest read it with a single lām without vowel and with fatḥah on the yāʾ (wa-l-yasaʿa).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ibn Ḏakwān reads fa-bi-hadāhumu qtadihī with kasrah on the hāʾ and ṣilah (i.e., a yāʾ after the kasrah). Hišām reads it with kasrah without ṣilah (i.e., iqtadihi). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī remove the hāʾ in connected speech only (i.e., iqtadi but iqtadih#). The rest maintains the hāʾ with no vowel in connected speech and pause (i.e., iqtadih(#)).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read yaǧʿalūnahū qarāṭīsa yabdūnahā wa-yaḫfūna with yāʾ in all three cases and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taǧʿalūnahū qarāṭīsa tabdūnahā wa-taḫfūna).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads wa-li-yunḏira ʾumma with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., wa-litunḏira).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ḥafṣ and al-Kisāʾī read la-qad taqaṭṭaʿa baynakum with naṣb of the nūn and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., baynukum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: al-ḥayya min al-may(yi)ti and may(yi)ti min al-ḥayyi has already been mentioned.[61]

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: The Kufans read wa-ǧaʿala in the pattern faʿala and al-layla sakanan with naṣb of the lām. The rest read wa-ǧāʿilu in the pattern fāʿil with ǧarr of the lām of al-layli.

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read fa-mustaqirrun with kasrah on the qāf, and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., fa-mustaqarrun).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾilā ṯumurihī in two places here (Q6:99 and Q6:141) and in Yā-Sīn (Q36:35) with two ḍammahs and the rest with two fatḥahs (i.e., ṯamarihī).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads ḫarraqū with gemination of the rāʾ and the rest without gemination (i.e., ḫaraqū).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read dārasta with ʾalif and fatḥah on the tāʾ. Ibn ʿĀmir reads it without ʾalif, with fatḥah on the sīn and no vowel on the tāʾ (i.e., darasat). The rest read it without ʾalif, with no vowel on the sīn and fatḥah on the tāʾ (i.e., darasta).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and ʾAbū Bakr—with disagreement in transmission from the last of the three—read ʾinnahā ʾiḏā ǧāʾat with kasrah on the hamzah. The rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., ʾannahā). Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamzah read lā tuʾminūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yuʾ/ūminūna).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read kulla šayʾin qibalan with kasrah on the qāf and fatḥah on the bāʾ. The rest read it with ḍammah on both (i.e., qubulan).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read ʾannahū munazzalun with gemination and the rest without gemination (i.e., munzalun).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: The Kufans read kalimatu rabbika in the singular and the rest in the plural (i.e., kalimātu).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: The Kufans read la-yuḍillūna and in Yūnus (Q10:88) li-yuḍillū with ḍammah on the yāʾ of both. The rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., la-yaḍillūna, li-yaḍillū). The Kufans and Nāfiʿ read wa-qad faṣṣala with fatḥah on the fāʾ and ṣād. The rest read it with ḍammah on the fāʾ and kasrah on the ṣād (i.e., fuṣṣila). Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ read mā ḥarrama with fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and rāʾ. The rest read it with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and kasrah on the rāʾ (i.e., ḥurrima).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads ʾa-wa-man kāna mayyitan, in Yā-Sīn al-(ʾ)arḍu l-mayyitatu (Q36:33) and in al-Ḥuǧurāt laḥma ʾaḫīhi mayyitan (Q49:12), with gemination of the yāʾ in all three. The rest reads it with no vowel (i.e., maytan, maytatu, maytan).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and Ḥafṣ read yaǧʿalu risālatahū in the singular with naṣb of the tāʾ. The rest read it in the plural with kasrah on the tāʾ (i.e., risālātihī).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads ḍayqan here and in al-Furqān (Q25:13) with no vowel on the yāʾ and the rest with gemination (of the yāʾ) (i.e., ḍayyiqan). Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū Bakr read ḥariǧan with kasrah on the rāʾ and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., ḥaraǧan). Ibn Kaṯīr reads kaʾannamā yaṣʿadu with no vowel on ungeminated ṣād and without ʾalif. ʾAbū Bakr reads yaṣṣāʿadu with gemination of the ṣād and an ʾalif after that. The rest read it with gemination of both the ṣād and the ʿayn without ʾalif (i.e., yaṣṣaʿʿadu).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads yawma yaḥšuruhum, that is, the second attestation in this sūrah, the second in Yūnus (Q10:45) and in Sabaʾ (Q34:40) yawma yaḥšuruhum … ṯumma yaqūlu with yāʾ in all of these (cases of yawma yaḥšuruhum) and ṯumma yaqūlu. The rest read them with nūn (i.e., yawma naḥšuruhum(ū) and ṯumma naqūlu).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads ʿammā taʿmalūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaʿmalūna).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads ʿalā makānātikum and makānātihim whenever it occurs in the plural and the rest in the singular (i.e., makānatikum(ū), makānatihim(ū)). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read man yakūnu lahū here and in al-Qaṣaṣ (Q28:37) with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., takūnu).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads bi-zuʿmihim in two cases (here and in Q6:138) with ḍammah of the zāy and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., bi-zaʿmihim(ū)).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads ka-ḏālika zuyyina with ḍammah on the zāy and kasrah on the yāʾ, qatlu with rafʿ of the lām, ʾawlādahum with naṣb of the dāl and šurakāʾihim with ḫafḍ of the hamzah. The rest read them with fatḥah on the zāy and yāʾ,[62] naṣb of the lām, ḫafḍ of the dāl and rafʿ of the hamzah (i.e., wa-ka-ḏālika zayyana … qatlu ʾawlādihum šurakāʾuhum(ū)).[63]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 140).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr and Ibn ʿĀmir read wa-ʾin takun with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yakun). Ibn Kaṯīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read maytatun with rafʿ and the rest with naṣb (i.e., maytatan).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: allaḏīna qat(t)alū has already been mentioned.[64]

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim and ʾAbū ʿAmr read yawma ḥaṣādihī with fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and the rest with kasrah (i.e., ḥiṣādihī).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: The Kufans and Nāfiʿ read wa-min al-maʿzi with no vowel on the ʿayn and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., al-maʿazi).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamzah read ʾillā ʾan takūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yakūna). Ibn ʿĀmir reads maytatun with rafʿ and the rest with naṣb (i.e., maytatan).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read taḏakkarūna with tāʾ and without gemination on the ḏāl whenever it occurs. The rest read it with gemination (i.e., taḏḏakkarūna).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-ʾinna hāḏā with kasrah on the hamzah and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., wa-ʾanna hāḏā). Ibn ʿĀmir pronounces it without gemination of the nūn (i.e., wa-ʾan hāḏā) and the rest read it with gemination.

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾillā ʾan yaʾtiyahum with yāʾ here and in al-Naḥl (Q16:33), and the rest read it with tāʾ (i.e., taʾ/ātiyahum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read fāraqū here and in al-Rūm (Q30:32) with ʾalif and without gemination. The rest read it without ʾalif and with gemination (i.e., farraqū).

statements.heading: F.6. Sūrat al-ʾAnʿām
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read dīnan qiyaman with kasrah on the qāf and fatḥah on the yāʾ without gemination. The rest read it with fatḥah on the qāf and kasrah on a geminated yāʾ (i.e., qayyiman).

statements.heading: F.6.1. [Yāʾs of Q6]
statements.text: There are eight yāʾs: 1. ʾinniya ʾaḫāfu (Q6:15) and 2. ʾinniya ʾarā/ǟ/ēka (Q6:74) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 3. ʾinniya ʾumirtu (Q6:14) and 4. mamātiya li-llāhi (Q6:162) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ. 5. waǧhiya li-llaḏī (Q6:79) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ. 6. ṣirāṭiya mustaqīman (Q6:153) with fatḥah by Ibn ʿĀmir. 7. rabbiya ʾilā ṣirāṭin (Q6:161) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 8. maḥyāy (Q6:162) with no vowel by Nāfiʿ with disagreement in transmission from Warš. What I recited to [Ḫalaf b. ʾIbrāhīm] Ibn Ḫāqān, transmitting from his teachers from him [Warš], is without a vowel. I adopt it because ʾAḥmad b. ʿUmar b. Muḥammad related to us, saying: ʾAḥmad b. ʾIbrāhīm related to us, saying: Bakr b. Sahl reported to us, saying: ʾAbū al-ʾAzhar [ʿAbd al-Ṣamad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān] reported to us from Warš from Nāfiʿ: wa-maḥyāy without a vowel on the yāʾ (wāqifatu l-yāʾ).[65] ʾAbū al-ʾAzhar [ʿAbd al-Ṣamad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān] said: ʿUṯmān b. Saʿīd [Warš] commanded me, “Place a fatḥah on it,” like miṯwāya. He claimed that it was more regular in terms of grammar. Ḫalaf b. ʾIbrāhīm [Ibn Ḫāqān] the teacher related to me, saying: ʾAḥmad b. ʾUsāmah related to me from his father from Yūnus from Warš from Nāfiʿ that it is wa-maḥyāy without a vowel on the yāʾ (mawqūfatu l-yāʾ), and mamātiya with naṣb of the yāʾ.[66] Yūnus said: ʿUṯmān [Warš] said to me: I prefer to apply naṣb to maḥyāya and apply no vowel to mamātī. ʾAbū ʿAmr [al-Dānī] said: So, this indicates, on the basis of the words of Warš, that he transmitted from Nāfiʿ with no vowel but that he himself preferred to pronounce it with fatḥah.

footnotes.text: The unusual use of the term wāqifah for no vowel, where al-Dānī usually uses the term ʾiskān, suggests that he is citing an older source with different vocabulary here. Indeed, ʾAbū al-ʾAzhar ʿAbd al-Ṣamad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān wrote a book dedicated to the reading of Nāfiʿ as contrasted with that of Ḥamzah; these quotes probably come from this book (Hamdan 2018, 48, fn. 5). The riwāyah transmission of Warš in the Taysīr in fact comes through this cited ʾisnād, and probably took the form of the transmission of this book. See U.4.1.2. and the discussion in Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 1072).
This ʾisnād is not in the Taysīr but it is mentioned in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 299).

statements.heading: F.6.2. [Removed yāʾ of Q6]
statements.text: There is a removed one: wa-qad hadānī (Q6:80) is maintained in connected speech by ʾAbū ʿAmr.

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads qalīlan mā yataḏakkarūna with the addition of yāʾ and the rest read it without yāʾ (i.e., taḏ(ḏ)akkarūna).[67]

footnotes.text: See F.6:152. This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 140).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Ibn Ḏakwān read wa-minhā taḫruǧūna, and in al-Zuḫruf wa-ka-ḏālika taḫruǧūna (Q43:11) with fatḥah on the tāʾ and ḍammah on the rāʾ for both. The rest read it with ḍammah on the tāʾ and fatḥah on the rāʾ (i.e., tuḫraǧūna).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read wa-libāsa t-taqwā/ǟ/ē with naṣb and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., wa-libāsu).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads ḫāliṣatun with rafʿ and the rest with naṣb (i.e., ḫāliṣatan).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads wa-lākin lā yaʿlamūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taʿlamūna).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads lā tuftaḥu with tāʾ and without gemination. Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read it with yāʾ and without gemination (i.e., lā yuftaḥu). The rest read it with tāʾ and gemination (i.e., lā tufattaḥu).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads mā kunnā li-nahtadiya without wāw and the rest read wa-mā with wāw.[68]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 140).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads qālū naʿim whenever it occurs with kasrah on the ʿayn and the rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., naʿam). Al-Bazzī, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾanna laʿnata ḷḷāhi with gemination of the nūn and naṣb of the tāʾ. The rest read it without gemination and rafʿ of the tāʾ (i.e., ʾan laʿnatu ḷḷāhi).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read yuġaššì l-layla with gemination, and likewise in al-Raʿd (Q13:3). The rest read it without gemination (i.e., yuġšī). Ibn ʿĀmir reads aš-šamsu wa-l-qamaru wa-n-nuǧūmu musaḫḫarātun with rafʿ of all four. The rest applies the naṣb to them, except to the tāʾ. That one carries kasrah in musaḫḫarātin (i.e., aš-šamsa, wa-l-qamara wa-n-nuǧūma musaḫḫarātin).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: wa-ḫi/ufyah has already been mentioned.[69]

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: ar-rīḥ/ar-riyāḥ has already been mentioned.[70] ʿĀṣim reads bušran with a bāʾ that carries a ḍammah and with no vowel on the šīn whenever it occurs. Ibn ʿĀmir reads it with a nūn that carries a ḍammah and with no vowel on the šīn (i.e., nušran). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read it with a nūn that carries a fatḥah and with no vowel on the šīn (i.e., našran). The rest read it with a nūn that carries a ḍammah and with ḍammah on the šīn (i.e., nušuran).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads min ʾilāhin ġayrihī with ḫafḍ of the rāʾ whenever min occurs before ʾilāhin which triggers the ḫafḍ (Q6:65, 73, 85; Q11:50, etc.). The rest read it with rafʿ (i.e., ġayruhū).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads ʾubliġukum in two places in this sūrah (here and Q7:68) and in al-ʾAḥqāf (Q46:23) without gemination. The rest read it with gemination (i.e., ʾuballiġukum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: bas/ṣṭah has already been mentioned.[71]

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads wa-qāla l-malaʾu llaḏīna stakbarū in the story of Ṣāliḥ[72] with the addition of the wāw. The rest read it without the wāw (i.e., qāla).[73]

footnotes.text: As opposed to the same phrase in Q7:88 in the story of Šuʿayb.
This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 140).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ read ʾinnakum la-taʾ/ātūna with a hamzah that carries a kasrah as a declarative sentence and the rest read it as an interrogative sentence (i.e., ʾaʾinnakum, ʾa.innakumū, ʾā.innakum). Their manner (of treating two hamzahs in a row) has already preceded in the chapter on two hamzahs.[74]

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: la-fat(t)aḥnā ʿalayhi/um has already been mentioned.[75]

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: The two of the holy cities and Ibn ʿĀmir read ʾaw ʾamina with no vowel on the wāw. Warš, in accordance with his general principle, places the vowel of the hamzah on the wāw (i.e., ʾaw‿amina).[76] The rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., ʾa-wa-ʾamina). Nāfiʿ reads ʿalayya ʾan lā with fatḥah on a geminate yāʾ. The rest read it with no vowel on the yāʾ and turn it into ʾalif in the pronunciation (i.e., ʿalā).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and Hišām read ʾarǧiʾhū here and in al-Šuʿarāʾ (Q26:36) with hamzah and ḍammah on the hāʾ, with ṣilah of wāw. ʾAbū ʿAmr reads it with hamzah and ḍammah, but without the ṣilah (of wāw) (ʾarǧiʾhu). Ibn Ḏakwān reads it with hamzah and kasrah of the hāʾ, without the ṣilah of yāʾ (i.e., ʾarǧiʾhi). Qālūn reads it without hamzah and with shortened pronunciation of the kasrah (i.e., ʾarǧihi). Warš and al-Kisāʾī read (it) without hamzah and with the ṣilah of yāʾ to the hāʾ (i.e., ʾarǧihī). ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read (it) without hamzah and with no vowel on the hāʾ (i.e., ʾarǧih). In pause, it carries no vowel without any disagreement, except in the manner of those who apply the ḍammah regardless of whether there is a ṣilah of wāw or not; in those cases rawm (i.e., ʾarǧiʾhᵘ#) or ʾišmām (i.e., ʾarǧiʾhʷ#) are allowed.

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read bi-kulli saḥḥārin here and in Yūnus (Q10:79) with an ʾalif after the ḥāʾ. The rest read it with ʾalif after the sīn (i.e., sāḥirin).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: The two of the holy cities and Ḥafṣ read ʾinna lanā la-ʾaǧran with a hamzah carrying kasrah as a declarative sentence. The rest read it as an interrogative sentence (i.e., ʾaʾinna, ʾa.inna, ʾā.inna), and they do so according to the manners that have been mentioned in the chapter of two hamzahs within a word.[77]

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads talqafu mā here, in Ṭāhā (Q20:69) and al-Šuʿarāʾ (Q26:45) without a vowel on the lām and without gemination. The rest read it with fatḥah on the lām and gemination (i.e., talaqqafu).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Qunbul reads qāla firʿawnu wa-.āmantumū bihī,[78] replacing in connected speech the hamzah of the interrogative with a wāw that carries a fatḥah and length after it as the equivalent of two ʾalifs (i.e., |ʾaAaAmantumuw|). In Ṭāhā (20:71) he reads it as a declarative sentence with hamzah and ʾalif (i.e., ʾāmantumū). In al-Šuʿarāʾ (Q26:49) he reads it as an interrogative sentence with hamzah and with stretched length with the equivalent of two ʾalifs (i.e., ʾa-.āmantumū). Ḥafṣ reads these three with hamzah and ʾalif as a declarative sentence (i.e., ʾāmantum). ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read them as interrogatives with two hamzahs pronounced fully[79] and an ʾalif behind them (i.e., ʾa-ʾāmantum). The rest read it as an interrogative, with a hamzah and length stretched as the equivalent of two ʾalifs (i.e., ʾa-.āmantum |ʾaAaAmantum|). There is not a single one of them who inserts an ʾalif between the fully pronounced hamzah and the softly pronounced hamzah in these places like they introduce it in ʾā-.anḏartahum (i.e., no one reads **ʾā.āmantum) and its class[80] due to the dislike of the meeting of three ʾalifs after the hamzah (the underlying form would be |ʾaAAaAmantum|).

footnotes.text: This is according to the general principle of Ibn Kaṯīr that ʾa-ʾā is pronounced with the softening of the second hamzah (see section U.11.1.).
The Pretzl edition has ‘ ੀඟففتഽنtwo softened hamzahs’, but this is certainly a mistake. It should read ੀචققتഽن instead, correct in the al-Ḍāmin edition (al-Dānī 2008a, 292).
The class being words with two hamzahs in a row; see section U.11.1.

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: The two of the holy cities read sa-naqtulu with fatḥah on the nūn and ḍammah on an ungeminated tāʾ. The rest read it with ḍammah on the nūn and kasrah on the geminate tāʾ (i.e., sa-nuqattilu).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr and Ibn ʿĀmir read yaʿrušūna here and in al-Naḥl (Q16:68) with ḍammah on the rāʾ and the rest read it with kasrah (i.e., yaʿrišūna).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read yaʿkifūna with kasrah on the kāf, and the rest with ḍammah (i.e., yaʿkufūna).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads wa-ʾiḏ ʾanǧākum with ʾalif after the ǧīm and without yāʾ and nūn. The rest read it with yāʾ and nūn and an ʾalif after it (i.e., ʾanǧaynākum(ū)).[81] Nāfiʿ reads yaqtulūna ʾabnāʾakum with fatḥah on the yāʾ and ḍammah on an ungeminated tāʾ. The rest read it with ḍammah on the yāʾ, fatḥah on the qāf and kasrah on a geminate tāʾ (i.e., yuqattilūna).

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 140).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ǧaʿalahū dakkâʾa here with length and a hamzah without tanwīn. The rest read it with tanwīn and without hamzah (i.e., dakkan).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: The two of the holy cities read bi-risālatī in the singular and the rest in the plural (i.e., bi-risālātī).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read sabīla r-rašadi with two fatḥahs and the rest with ḍammah on the rāʾ and no vowel on the šīn (i.e., ar-rušdi).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read min ḥiliyyihim with kasrah on the ḥāʾ and the rest with ḍammah (i.e., ḥuliyyihim(ū)).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read tarḥamnā rabbanā wa-taġfir lanā with tāʾ on both and naṣb of the bāʾ of rabbanā. The rest read it with yāʾ and rafʿ of the bāʾ (i.e., yarḥamnā rabbunā wa-yaġfir lanā).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read qāla bna ʾummi here and in Ṭāhā (Q20:94) with kasrah on the mīm and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., ibna ʾumma).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads ʿanhum ʾāṣārahum[82] with fatḥah on the hamzah with ʾalif as a plural, and the rest read it with kasrah on the hamzah without ʾalif as a singular (i.e., ʾisrahum(ū)).

footnotes.text: Pretzl renders this word as   ا༠ศٰهمwhich is wrong. It should be ءا༠ٰศهم.

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read tuġfar lakum with tāʾ that carries a ḍammah and with fatḥah on the fāʾ. The rest read it with nūn that carries a fatḥah and with kasrah on the fāʾ (i.e., naġfir). ʾAbū ʿAmr reads ḫaṭāyākum like the word qaḍāyākum without hamzah. Ibn ʿĀmir reads ḫaṭīʾatukum with hamzah and rafʿ of the tāʾ without ʾalif as a singular. Nāfiʿ reads it like that except he reads it as a plural (i.e., ḫaṭīʾātukum), and the rest like that except they place kasrah on the tāʾ (i.e., ḫaṭīʾātikum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads qālū maʿḏiratan with naṣb and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., maʿḏiratun).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads bi-ʿaḏābin bīsin with kasrah on the bāʾ and without hamzah just like ʿīsin.[83] Ibn ʿĀmir reads it with kasrah on the bāʾ and with hamzah without vowel after it (i.e., biʾsin). ʾAbū Bakr reads, with disagreement in transmission from him, bayʾasin with fatḥah on the bāʾ and with hamzah that carries a fatḥah after the yāʾ, like qayqab. The rest read baʾīsin with fatḥah on the bāʾ and with hamzah that carries a kasrah and after it a yāʾ, like raʾīs. This option has (also) been transmitted from ʾAbū Bakr.

footnotes.text: Pretzl renders this word า༓ ,໣يwhich is certainly a mistake. It should read ໣يس ‘camels of good stock’, which is found in the manuscript that I have consulted and the al-Ḍāmin edition (al-Dānī 2008a, 295).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: ʾa-fa-lā y/taʿqilūna has already been mentioned.[84]

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads wa-llaḏīna yumsikūna without gemination and the rest with gemination (i.e., yumassikūna).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read ḏuriyyātihim in the plural with kasrah on the tāʾ. The rest read it in the singular with naṣb of the tāʾ (i.e., ḏuriyyatahum(ū)). ʾAbū ʿAmr reads ʾan yaqūlū with yāʾ on both (here and in Q7:173) and the rest read it with tāʾ (i.e., taqūlū).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads yalḥadūna here and in Fuṣṣilat (Q41:40) with fatḥah on the yāʾ and ḥāʾ. The rest read it with ḍammah on the yāʾ and kasrah on the ḥāʾ (i.e., yulḥidūna).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: ʿĀṣim and ʾAbū ʿAmr read wa-yaḏaruhum with yāʾ and rafʿ of the rāʾ. Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read it with yāʾ and with ǧazm of the rāʾ (i.e., wa-yaḏarhum). The rest read it with nūn and rafʿ of the rāʾ (i.e., wa-naḏaruhum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū Bakr read lahū širkan with kasrah on the šīn and no vowel on the rāʾ with tanwīn. The rest read it with ḍammah on the šīn, with fatḥah on the rāʾ, length and hamzah without tanwīn (i.e., šurakâʾa).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads lā yatbaʿūkum here and in al-Šuʿarāʾ yatbaʿuhumu l-ġāwūna (Q26:224) with fatḥah on an ungeminated tāʾ.[85] The rest read it with fatḥah on a geminated tāʾ (i.e., lā yattabiʿūkum(ū), yattabiʿuhum(ū)).

footnotes.text: Pretzl has bāʾ here. This is a mistake.

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read ṭayfun without hamzah or ʾalif. The rest read it with ʾalif and hamzah (i.e., ṭāʾifun).

statements.heading: F.7. Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads yumiddūnahum with ḍammah on the yāʾ and kasrah on the mīm. The rest read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ and ḍammah on the mīm (i.e., yamuddūnahum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.7.1. [Yāʾs of Q7]
statements.text: There are seven yāʾs: 1. rabbì l-fawāḥiša (Q7:33) without vowel by Ḥamzah. 2. ʾinniya ʾaḫāfu (Q7:59) and 3. min baʿdiya ʾa-ʿaǧiltum(ū) (Q7:150) with fatḥah on both by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 4. maʿiya banī ʾisrāʾīl (Q7:105) with fatḥah by Ḥafṣ. 5. ʾinniya ṣṭafaytuka (Q7:144) with fatḥah by Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 6. ʿan ʾāyāti llaḏīna (Q7:146) without vowel by Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamzah. 7. ʿaḏābiya ʾuṣību (Q7:156) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ.

statements.heading: F.7.2. [Removed yāʾ of Q7]
statements.text: There is a removed one: ṯumma kaydūnī falā (Q7:195) with retention in connected speech and pause by Hišām, with disagreement in transmission from him. It is read with retention in connected speech only by ʾAbū ʿAmr. Success comes from God.

statements.heading: F.8. Sūrat al-ʾAnfāl
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads murdafīna with fatḥah on the dāl. Likewise, I was told by Muḥammad b. ʾAḥmad, transmitting from Ibn Muǧāhid, that he recited it so to Qunbul and he said that it is wrong.[86] The rest read it with kasrah (i.e., murdifīna).

footnotes.text: This has not come down in the recension of Ibn Muǧāhid’s work available to us. He does mention this variant transmitted from Ibn Kaṯīr, but not through Qunbul, but rather through al-Ḥulwānī, and he does not say that it is mistaken (Ibn Muǧāhid 1972, 304).

statements.heading: F.8. Sūrat al-ʾAnfāl
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read ʾiḏ yaġšākum(ū) with fatḥah on the yāʾ and šīn, with ʾalif after it, and an-nuʿāsu with [rafʿ of the sīn. Nāfiʿ reads yuġšīkum with ḍammah on the yāʾ and kasrah on an ungeminated šīn and al-nuʿāsa][87] with naṣb. The rest read it like that, except that they apply fatḥah to ġayn and geminate the šīn (i.e., yuġaššīkum).

footnotes.text: Due to eye-skip, Pretzl missed this section of the text. It is fixed based on the al-Ḍāmin edition (al-Dānī 2008a, 42).

statements.heading: F.8. Sūrat al-ʾAnfāl
statements.text: ar-ruʿ(u)b[88] and wa-lākin illāhu (Q8:17)[89] in both cases (in that verse) have been mentioned already.

statements.heading: F.8. Sūrat al-ʾAnfāl
statements.text: The two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr read muwahhinun kayda with fatḥah on the wāw and with a geminate hāʾ. The rest read it without a vowel on the wāw and without gemination[90] of the hāʾ (i.e., mūhinun). Ḥafṣ removes the tanwīn and applies ḫafḍ[91] to the dāl of kaydi as a construct phrase (i.e., muwahhinu kaydi). The rest applies tanwīn and naṣb to the dāl (i.e., muwahhinun/mūhinun kayda).

footnotes.text: In the Pretzl edition this reads ,๰ඟفضclearly mixed up with the next variant discussed. It should read ๽ඟفيف (al-Dānī 2008a, 299).
In the Pretzl edition this reads ,๽ඟفيفclearly mixed up with the previous variant discussed. It should read ๰ඟفض (al-Dānī 2008a, 299).

statements.heading: F.8. Sūrat al-ʾAnfāl
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read wa-ʾanna ḷḷāha maʿa with fatḥah on the hamzah and the rest with kasrah (i.e., ʾinna).

statements.heading: F.8. Sūrat al-ʾAnfāl
statements.text: li-yamīza/yumayyiza ḷḷāhu has already been mentioned.[92]

statements.heading: F.8. Sūrat al-ʾAnfāl
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read bi-l-ʿidwati in both cases (in this verse) with kasrah on the ʿayn. The rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., bi-l-ʿudwati). Nāfiʿ, al-Bazzī and ʾAbū Bakr read man ḥayiya ʿan with two yāʾs, with the first carrying a kasrah. The rest read it with one geminate (yāʾ) carrying a fatḥah (i.e., ḥayya).

statements.heading: F.8. Sūrat al-ʾAnfāl
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads ʾiḏ tatawaffà llaḏīna with two tāʾs and the rest read it with yāʾ and tāʾ (i.e., yatawaffà llaḏīna).

statements.heading: F.8. Sūrat al-ʾAnfāl
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamzah read wa-lā yaḥsabanna llaḏīna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taḥsa/ibanna). Ibn ʿĀmir reads ʾannahum lā yuʿǧizūna with fatḥah on the hamzah and the rest read it with kasrah (i.e., ʾinnahum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.8. Sūrat al-ʾAnfāl
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads li-s-silmi with kasrah on the sīn and the rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., li-s-salmi).

statements.heading: F.8. Sūrat al-ʾAnfāl
statements.text: The Kufans read ʾin yakun minkum miʾatun yaġlibū and fa-ʾin yakun minkum miʾatun ṣābiratun (Q8:66) with yāʾ on both. ʾAbū ʿAmr reads it with yāʾ on the first only (i.e., ʾin yakun minkum miʾatun yaġlibū, ʾin takun minkum miʾatun ṣābiratun). The rest read it with tāʾ on both (i.e., ʾin takun minkum miʾatun yaġlibū, ʾin takun minkum miʾatun ṣābiratun).

statements.heading: F.8. Sūrat al-ʾAnfāl
statements.text: Ḥamzah and ʿĀṣim read fīkum ḍaʿfan with fatḥah on the ḍād, and the rest with ḍammah (i.e., ḍuʿfan).

statements.heading: F.8. Sūrat al-ʾAnfāl
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads ʾan takūna lahū with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yakūna). ʾAbū ʿAmr reads min al-ʾusārē in the pattern fuʿalā and the rest in the pattern faʿlā (i.e., al-(ʾ)asrā/ǟ/ē).

statements.heading: F.8. Sūrat al-ʾAnfāl
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads min wilāyatihim with kasrah on the wāw and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., walāyatihim(ū)).

statements.heading: F.8.1. [Yāʾs of Q8]
statements.text: There are two yāʾs: 1. ʾinniya ʾarā/ē (Q8:48) and 2. ʾinniya ʾaḫāfu (Q8:48) with fatḥah on both by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū Amr.

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read ʾaʾimmah with two hamzahs whenever it occurs. Hišām, according to my recitation to ʾAbū al-Fatḥ, inserts an ʾalif (i.e., ʾāʾimmah). The rest read with hamzah and yāʾ as an ultrashort kasrah, without length (i.e., ʾa.immah).[93] Ibn ʿĀmir reads lā ʾīmāna lahū with kasrah on the hamzah and the rest on the fatḥah (i.e., ʾaymāna).

footnotes.text: The literal reading of this description points to ʾayĭmmah. In modern recitation this is understood to be ʾa.immah, and described as such by Ibn al-Ǧazarī (2018, §1430–31). But Ibn al-Ǧazarī also mentions the option with yāʾ, so it may be possible that ʾayĭmmah is in fact the intended reading here.

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read the first ʾan yaʿmurū masǧida ḷḷāhi in the singular, the rest in the plural (i.e., masāǧida). There is no disagreement on the second (always in the plural).

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: yabšuruhum/yubašširuhum(ū) has already been mentioned.[94]

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads wa-ʿašīrātukum in the plural, and the rest in the singular (i.e., wa-ʿašīratukum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read ʿuzayrun ibnu ḷḷāhi with tanwīn and kasrah. It is not allowed to apply the ḍammah in the manner of al-Kisāʾī[95] because the ḍammah of the nūn is functioning as a case vowel and it is not part of the word formation (which would make it possible) to transfer it (i.e., not ʿazīzun ubnu because the u of ibnu is not part of the stem, but ʾiʿrāb). The rest read without tanwīn (i.e., ʿuzayru bnu ḷḷāhi). ʿĀṣim reads yuḍāhiʾūna with hamzah and kasrah on the hāʾ. The rest read it with ḍammah on the hāʾ without hamzah (yuḍāhūna).

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: Warš reads ʾinnamà n-nasiyyu with gemination of the yāʾ without hamzah. The rest read it with hamzah and length and no vowel on the yāʾ (i.e., an-nasîʾu). When Ḥamzah or Hišām pause, they follow Warš (i.e., an-nasiyy#). Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read yuḍallu bihī with ḍammah on the yāʾ and fatḥah on the ḍād. The rest read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ and kasrah on the ḍād (i.e., yaḍillu).

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: ʾaw ka/urhan has already been mentioned.[96]

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: ʾuḏ(u)nun qul ʾuḏ(u)nu ḫayrin lakum has already been mentioned.[97]

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: ʿĀṣim reads ʾin naʿfu ʿan ṭāʾifatin with a nūn that carries a fatḥah and with rafʿ of the fāʾ, nuʿaḏḏib with nūn and kasrah on the ḏāl, and ṭāʾifatan with naṣb. The rest read it with a yāʾ that carries a ḍammah and with fatḥah on the fāʾ on the first word, and the second one with tāʾ, fatḥah on the ḏāl and rafʿ of ṭāʾifatun (i.e., ʾin yuʿfa ʿan ṭāʾifatin, tuʿaḏḏab ṭāʾifatun).

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read dāʾiratu s-sūʾi here and in al-Fatḥ (Q48:6) with ḍammah on the sīn and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., as-sawʾi).

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: Warš reads qurubatun lahum with ḍammah of the rāʾ and the rest without a vowel (i.e., qurbatun lahum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads min taḥtihā after the (verse) 100,[98] with the addition of min and ḫafḍ of the tāʾ. The rest read it without min and with fatḥah on the tāʾ (i.e., taḥtahā).[99]

footnotes.text: In the Kufan verse count of the ubiquitous Ḥafṣ reading, this word occurs not after 100, but in verse 100. In the Medinan verse count that was native to al-Dānī as well as the Meccan verse count, however, this is verse 101 (Spitaler 1935, 38).
This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 141).

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾinna ṣalātaka and in Hūd ʾa-ṣalātuka taʾmuruka (Q11:89) in the singular and naṣb of the tāʾ here. The rest read both in the plural with kasrah on the tāʾ here and no disagreement on the rafʿ of the tāʾ in Hūd (i.e., ʾinna ṣalawātika, ʾa-ṣalawātuka taʾ/āmuruka).

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū Bakr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read murǧaʾūna here and in al-ʾAḥzāb turǧiʾu (Q33:51) with hamzah for both. The rest read it without hamzah (i.e., murǧawna, turǧī).

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read allaḏīna ttaḫaḏū without wāw before the allaḏīna. The rest read with wāw (i.e., wa-llaḏīna ttaḫaḏū).[100]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 141).

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read ʾa-fa-man ʾussisa bunyānuhū and ḫayrun ʾam man ʾussisa banyānuhū with ḍammah on the hamzah, kasrah on the sīn and rafʿ of the nūn in both. The rest read it with fatḥah on the hamzah and sīn, and naṣb of the nūn of bunyānahū (i.e., ʾassasa bunyānahū). Ibn ʿĀmir, ʾAbū Bakr and Ḥamzah read ǧurfin without a vowel on the rāʾ. The rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., ǧurufin). Ibn Kaṯīr, Ḥamzah, Ḥafṣ, Hišām and al-Naqqāš, transmitting from al-ʾAḫfaš [from Ibn Ḏakwān],[101] read hārin with fatḥah and Warš reads it in between the two sounds (i.e., hǟrin). The rest read it with ʾimālah (i.e., hērin). The rāʾ is the third root letter of the stem, so it has been made into the second root letter by metathesis (hērin is analysed as |haAriy-n|, which is considered a metathesis of hāʾirun |haAyiru-n|).[102]

footnotes.text: This is the only tilāwah ʾisnād for Ibn Ḏakwān in the Taysīr. Other transmissions from Ibn Ḏakwān are mentioned in Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 1160) and they do not all transmit this reading for him.

The reason why this form is analysed as such, and not as |hawirin~haArin|—which would be eligible for ʾimālah because of ār + ǧarr—is a bit convoluted. But lexicographical works point out that even in the nominative the phrase is ǧur(u)fun hārin, thus the adjective must be analysed as |haAriyun| (Lane 1863, 2968a; Ibn Manẓūr n.d., 4719c). This analysis is irrelevant for the use in the Qurʾān, however.

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ and Ḥamzah read ʾillā ʾan taqaṭṭaʿa with fatḥah on the tāʾ and the rest with ḍammah (i.e., tuqaṭṭaʿa).

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: fa-yaqtulūna wa-yuqtalūna has already been mentioned.[103]

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: Ḥafṣ and Ḥamzah read yazīġu qulūbu with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tazīġu qulūbu).

statements.heading: F.9. Sūrat al-Tawbah
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads ʾa-wa-lā tarawna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yarawna).

statements.heading: F.9.1. [Yāʾs of Q9]
statements.text: There are two yāʾs: 1. maʿī ʾabadan (Q9:83) with no vowel by ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī. 2. maʿiya ʿaduwwan (Q9:84) with fatḥah by Ḥafṣ.

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Qālūn and Ḥafṣ read ʾalif-lām-rā (in the beginning of Q10, Q11, Q12, Q14, Q15) and ʾalif-lām-mīm-rā (in the beginning of Q13) with fatḥah and Warš in between the two sounds (i.e., ʾalif-lām-rǟ, ʾalif-lām-mīm-rǟ). The rest read it with ʾimālah (ʾalif-lām-rē, ʾaliflām-mīm-rē).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn Kaṯīr read la-sāḥirun mubīnun with ʾalif and the rest read la-siḥrun without ʾalif.

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Qunbul reads ḍiʾāʾan and bi-ḍiʾāʾin here, in al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ (Q21:48) and al-Qaṣaṣ (Q28:71) with hamzah after the ḍād. The rest read it with a yāʾ that carries a fatḥah after (the ḍād) (i.e., ḍiyāʾan, bi-ḍiyāʾin). Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ read yufaṣṣilu l-ʾāyāti with yāʾ and the rest with nūn (i.e., nufaṣṣilu).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads la-qaḍā ʾilayhim with fatḥah on the qāf and ḍād, and ʾaǧalahum with naṣb of the lām. The rest read it with ḍammah on the qāf, kasrah on the ḍād, fatḥah on the yāʾ and rafʿ of the lām (i.e., la-quḍiya ʾilayhi/um(ū) ʾaǧaluhum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Qunbul reads wa-la-ʾadrākumū bihī without the ʾalif after the lām. Al-Naqqāš transmitted it like that from ʾAbū Rabīʿah from al-Bazzī, and ʾAbū al-Qāsim [ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Fārisī] taught me to recite it like that, transmitting from him (al-Naqqāš ← ʾAbū Rabīʿah ← al-Bazzī). The rest read it with ʾalif (i.e., wa-lā ʾadrākum).[104] Ibn Kaṯīr, Qālūn, Ḥafṣ, Hišām and al-Naqqāš from al-ʾAḫfaš (from Ibn Ḏakwān)[105] read ʾadrāka and ʾadrākum(ū) whenever it occurs with fatḥah, Warš in between the two sounds (i.e., ʾadrǟka, ʾadrǟkum) and the rest with ʾimālah (i.e., ʾadrēka, ʾadrēkum).

footnotes.text: The wording here suggests that this reading for al-Bazzī has reached al-Dānī through two modes of transmission (riwāyah and tilāwah). The ʾisnād al-Naqqāš ← ʾAbū Rabīʿah ← al-Bazzī is only reported as a tilāwah ʾisnād, however. This is the tilāwah ʾisnād in the Taysīr, and it is also reported as a tilāwah ʾisnād in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 306).
