This is the path from Ibn Ḏakwān present in the Taysīr, but the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān reports that ʿAbū al-Fatḥ Fāris b. ʾAḥmad ← ʿAbd al-Bāqī ← his teachers ← al-ʾAḫfaš ← Ibn Ḏakwān transmit this with ʾimālah (al-Dānī 2007, 1172).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʿammā tušrikūna here, in two places in al-Naḥl (Q16:1, 3) and in al-Rūm (Q30:33) with tāʾ in all four places. The rest read it with yāʾ (i.e., yušrikūna).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads yanšurukum fì l-barri wa-l-baḥri with nūn and šīn of (the verb) al-našr and the rest with sīn and yāʾ of (the verb) al-tasyīr, i.e., yusayyirukum(ū).[106]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 141).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads matāʿa l-ḥayāti d-dunyā with naṣb and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., matāʿu).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and al-Kisāʾī read qaṭʿan min al-layli with no vowel on the ṭāʾ and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., qaṭaʿan).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read hunālika tatlū with tāʾ and the rest with bāʾ (i.e., tablū).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read kalimātu rabbika here, at the end of the sūrah (Q10:96), and in al-Ġāfir (Q40:6), in these three places, in the plural and the rest in the singular (i.e., kalimatu).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Warš and Ibn ʿĀmir read ʾamman lā yahaddī with fatḥah on the yāʾ and hāʾ, and gemination of the dāl. Qālūn and ʾAbū ʿAmr read it like that, except that they apply ʾiḫfāʾ[107] to the vowel of the hāʾ (i.e., lā yahăddī), and the texts from Qālūn say it is without vowel (i.e., lā yahddī). Al-Yazīdī, transmitting from ʾAbū ʿAmr, said that he used to give the hāʾ a little bit of ʾišmām of the fatḥah (i.e., lā yahăddī). ʾAbū Bakr reads it with kasrah of the yāʾ and hāʾ (i.e., yihiddī), and Ḥafṣ with fatḥah on the yāʾ and kasrah on the hāʾ (i.e., yahiddī). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ, no vowel on the hāʾ and no gemination on the dāl (i.e., yahdī).

footnotes.text: This is an imprecise term for what is properly called iḫtilās. Such a use is not uncommon in al-Dānī’s wording.

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-lākin in-nāsu with kasrah on an ungeminated nūn and rafʿ of the sīn. The rest read it with fatḥah on the geminated nūn and naṣb of the sīn (i.e., wa-lākinna n-nāsa).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: yawma y/taḥšuruhum kaʾan lam has already been mentioned.[108]

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads bihī ʾā-lāna and ʾā-lāna wa qad ʿaṣayta (Q10:91) with fatḥah on the lām without hamzah. The rest read it with no vowel on the lām and hamzah after it. Everyone softens the hamzat al-waṣl that comes after the hamzah of interrogation in this and what is like it, such as His speech ʾāḏ-ḏakarayni (Q6:143, 144), qul ʾāḷḷāhu ʾaḏina lakum(ū) (Q10:59) and ʾāḷḷāhu ḫayrun (Q27:59), and none of them pronounces it fully (so never ʾa-ʾaḷḷāhu, etc.), nor does anyone place anything (i.e., an ʾalif) between it and the word that comes after the ʾalif because of its weakness (so never ʾā-.aḷḷāhu, etc.). Because the replacement (of the bayna bayn realisation of hamzah with an ʾalif, so that you get ʾāḷḷāhu etc.) is the opinion of most of the reciters and grammarians, (badal) is required for these (cases).[109]

footnotes.text: While al-Dānī’s prescription suggests ʾāḷḷāhu, etc. is preferred, the wording clearly indicates that some also read ʾa-.aḷḷāhu, etc., pronounced bayna bayn. This is spelled out more explicitly in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 524).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads ḫayrun mimmā taǧmaʿūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaǧmaʿūna).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads wa-mā yaʿzibu ʿan rabbika here and in Sabaʾ (Q34:3) with kasrah on the zāy. The rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., yaʿzubu). Ḥamzah reads wa-lā ʾaṣġaru min ḏālika wa-lā ʾakbaru with rafʿ of both and the rest with fatḥah.

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: bi-kulli sāḥirin/saḥḥārin has already been mentioned.[110]

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads bihī ʾâ-s-siḥru with length as an interrogative and the rest read it without length as a declarative (i.e., bihi s-siḥru).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: ʿUbayd Aḷḷāh b. ʾAbī Muslim transmitted from his father [ʾAbū Muslim ʿAbd al-Raḥmān] and Hubayrah, [both] from Ḥafṣ, that he paused on His words ʾan tatabawwaʾā as tabawwayā# with yāʾ replacing the hamzah.[111] Ibn Ḫuwāstī [al-Fārisī] told us, transmitting from ʾAbū Ṭāhir from al-ʾUšnānī [from ʿUbayd from Ḥafṣ], that he paused with a hamzah (i.e., tatabawwaʾā#) and that is what I recited and adopted.

footnotes.text: This is an ʾisnād not included in the Taysīr, while the variant tatabawwaʾā# does follow the ʾisnād presented in the Taysīr. The transmission via ʿUbayd Aḷḷāh b. ʾAbī Muslim is quoted from Ibn Muǧāhid’s Kitāb al-sabʿ, and al-Dānī says that the transmission of Hubayrah is taken from a book on ʿĀṣim’s reading authored by Ibn Muǧāhid (al-Dānī 2007, 1187; Ibn Muǧāhid 1972, 329).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: li-yaḍillū/li-yuḍillū has already been mentioned.[112]

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Ibn Ḏakwān reads wa-lā tattabbiʿāni without gemination of the nūn and the rest with gemination (i.e., tattabiʿānni). There is no disagreement on the gemination of the tāʾ.

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾāmantu ʾinnahū with kasrah on the hamzah and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., ʾannahū).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads naǧʿalu r-riǧsa[113] with nūn and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaǧʿalu).

footnotes.text: Pretzl has a typographical error ศ༓ اආ඗جfor اආ඗جس (al-Dānī 2008a, 312).

statements.heading: F.10. Sūrat Yūnus (s)
statements.text: Ḥafṣ and al-Kisāʾī read nunǧi l-muʾminūna without gemination and the rest read with gemination (i.e., nunaǧǧi). All of them pause on this and what is like it (i.e., final weak verbs with ǧazm) from what is written in the muṣḥaf without yāʾ (i.e., nun(aǧ)ǧ#, etc.) in accordance with its writing (ننج), except that which is transmitted (otherwise) from them, so one falls back on it (if nothing exceptional is mentioned).

statements.heading: F.10.1. [Yāʾs of Q10]
statements.text: There are five yāʾs: 1. liya ʾan ʾubaddilahū (Q10:10) and 2. ʾinniya ʾaḫāfu (Q10:10) with fatḥah on both by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 3. nafsiya ʾin ʾattabiʿu (Q10:15) and 4. rabbiya ʾinnahū la-ḥaqqun (Q10:35) with fatḥah on both by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 5. ʾin ʾaǧriya ʾillā ʿalà ḷḷāhi (Q10:72) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ, and it is like that whenever it occurs.

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: ʾalif-lām-rā/ǟ/ē[114] and ʾillā siḥrun/sāḥirun (Q11:7)[115] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read ʾannī lakum(ū) naḏīrun with fatḥah on the hamzah and the rest with kasrah (i.e., ʾinnī).

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads bādiʾa r-raʾ/āyi with a hamzah that carries a fatḥah after the dāl. The rest read it with a yāʾ that carries the fatḥah (i.e., bādiya r-raʾyi).

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read fa-ʿummiyat ʿalaykum with ḍammah on the ʿayn and gemination of the mīm. The rest read it with fatḥah on the ʿayn and without gemination on the mīm (i.e., ʿamiyat).

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads min kullin zawǧayni ṯnayni here and in al-Muʾminūn (Q23:27) with tanwīn on the lām. The rest read it without tanwīn (i.e., min kulli zawǧayni ṯnayni).

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read maǧrēhā with fatḥah on the mīm and the rest with ḍammah (i.e., muǧrā/ǟhā). We have already mentioned the disagreement about (the ʾimālah) of the rāʾ in the chapter on ʾimālah.[116]

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: ʿĀṣim reads yā bunayya rkab here with fatḥah on the yāʾ. The rest read it with kasrah (i.e., yā bunayyi). ʾarkam⸗maʿanā,[117] wa-qǖla, wa-ġǖḍa (Q11:44),[118] min (ʾ)ilāhin ġayru/ihū/ī (Q11:50)[119] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads ʾinnahū ʿamila with kasrah on the mīm and fatḥah on the lām and ġayra ṣāliḥin with naṣb of the rāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the mīm and rafʿ of the lām with tanwīn and rafʿ of the rāʾ (i.e., ʾinnahū ʿamalun ġayru ṣāliḥin). Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read fa-lā tasʾalanni with fatḥah on the lām and kasrah on the geminated nūn. Ibn Kaṯīr also reads it like that except that he placed fatḥah on the nūn (i.e., tasʾalanna). The rest read it with no vowel on the lām and kasrah on the nūn without gemination (i.e., tasʾalni).

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read wa-man ḫizyi yawmaʾiḏin with fatḥah on the mīm and the rest with kasrah (i.e., wa-min ḫizyi yawmaʾiḏin).

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: Ḥafṣ and Ḥamzah read ʾa-lā ʾinna ṯamūda here and in al-Furqān (Q25:38) and al-ʿAnkabūt (Q29:38) with fatḥah on the dāl without tanwīn and pause on it without ʾalif (i.e., ṯamūd#). The rest read it with tanwīn (i.e., ṯamūdan) and pause on it with ʾalif (i.e., ṯamūdā#) instead. Al-Kisāʾī reads ʾa-lā buʿdan li-ṯamūdin with the ḫafḍ of the dāl with tanwīn and the rest read it with fatḥah on the dāl without tanwīn (i.e., li-ṯamūda).

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read qāla silmun here and in al-Ḏāriyāt (Q51:25) with kasrah on the sīn and no vowel on the lām. The rest read it with fatḥah on the sīn and lām and with an ʾalif after it (i.e., salāmun).

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah and Ḥafṣ read yaʿqūba // qālat with naṣb and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., yaʿqūbu).

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read sǖʾa bihim, sǖʾat and what is like it with ʾišmām of the ḍammah on the sīn, here and in al-ʿAnkabūt (Q29:33) and al-Mulk (Q67:27). The rest read it with pure pronunciation of the kasrah on the sīn (i.e., sīʾa, sīʾat).

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: The two of the holy cities read fa-sri and ʾan isri with ʾalif al-waṣl whenever it occurs, and the rest read it with ʾalif al-qaṭʿ (i.e., fa-ʾasri, ʿan ʾasri). Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read ʾillà mraʾatuka with rafʿ and the rest with naṣb (i.e., imraʾataka).

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: ʾa-ṣalawātuka[120] and ʿalā makānātikum (Q11:92)[121] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read allaḏīna suʿidū with ḍammah on the sīn and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., saʿidū).

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: The two of the holy cities and ʾAbū Bakr read wa-ʾin kullan with no vowel on the nūn and the rest with gemination (i.e., wa-ʾinna). ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamzah read lammā li-yuwaffiyannahum here,[122] in Yā-Sīn lammā ǧamīʿun (Q36:32) and in al-Ṭāriq lammā ʿalayhā (Q86:4) with gemination on the mīm, in these three places. The rest read it without gemination (i.e., lamā).

footnotes.text: Pretzl does not have hunā here (al-Dānī 2008a, 45).

statements.heading: F.11. Sūrat Hūd (s)
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ read ʾilayhi yurǧaʿu with ḍammah on the yāʾ and fatḥah of the ǧīm. The rest read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ and kasrah on the ǧīm (i.e yarǧiʿu). Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read ʿammā taʿmalūna here and at the end of al-Naml (Q27:93) with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaʿmalūna).

statements.heading: F.11.1. [Yāʾs of Q11]
statements.text: There are 18 yāʾs: 1. fa-ʾinniya ʾaḫāfu (Q11:3), 2. fa-ʾinniya ʾaḫāfu (Q11:82), 3. ʾinniya ʾaʿiḏ̣uka (Q11:46), 4. ʾinniya ʾaʿūḏu bika (Q11:47), 5. ʾinniya ʾaḫāfu (Q11:26) and 6. šiqāqiya ʾan (Q11:89) with fatḥah on all six by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 7. ʿanniya ʾinniya (Q11:10), 8. nuṣḥiya ʾin (ʾ)arattu (Q11:34), 9. ʾinniya ʾiḏān lamina (Q11:31) and 10. fī ḍayfiya ʾa-laysa (Q11:78) with fatḥah on all four by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 11. wa-lākinniya ʾarā/ǟ/ēkum(ū) (Q11:29) and 12. wa-ʾinniya ʾarā/ǟ/ēkum(ū) (Q11:84) with fatḥah for both by Nāfiʿ, al-Bazzī and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 13. ʾin (ʾ)aǧriya ʾillā (Q11:29) and 14. ʾin (ʾ)aǧriya ʾillā (Q11:51) with fatḥah for both by Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ. 15. faṭaraniya ʾa-fa-lā (Q11:51) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ and al-Bazzī. 16. ʾinniya ʾušhidu ḷḷāha (Q11:54) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ. 17. wa-mā tawfīqiya ʾillā bi-llāhi (Q11:88) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 18. ʾa-raḥṭiya ʾaʿazzu (Q11:92) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ibn Ḏakwān.

statements.heading: F.11.2. [Removed yāʾs of Q11]
statements.text: There are three removed ones: 1. fa-lā tasʾalannī/tasʾalnī (Q11:46) with the retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Warš and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 2. wa-lā tuḫzūnī (Q11:78) with the retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by ʾAbū ʿAmr. 3. yawma yaʾ/ātī (Q11:105) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr, and retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Nāfiʿ, ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī.

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads yā ʾabata with fatḥah on the tāʾ whenever it occurs (Q12:100; Q19:42, 43, 44, 45; Q28:26; Q37:102) and the rest with kasrah (i.e., yā ʾabati). Ibn Kaṯīr and Ibn ʿĀmir pause on it as yā ʾabah# with hāʾ and it has already been mentioned in the chapter on pause.[123]

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads yā bunayya here and in al-Ṣāffāt (Q37:102) with fatḥah on the yāʾ. The rest read it with kasrah (i.e., yā bunayyi).

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads ʾāyatun li-s-sāʾilīna in the singular, and the rest in the plural (i.e., ʾāyātun).

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads ġayābāti l-ǧubbi in two places (here and in Q12:15) in the plural and the rest in the singular (i.e., ġayābati l-ǧubbi).

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: All of them read mā laka taʾ/āmanʷnā with assimilation of the first nūn to the second one with ʾišmām of the ḍammah. The function of the ʾišmām in that word is to indicate the vowel on the nūn which receives no articulation (i.e., taʾmanʷnā/tāmanʷnā). It may (also) be read with ʾiḫfāʾ, without true assimilation because the vowel is not made (fully) silent immediately, rather it is weakened in its sound, so that in this way there is a separation between what is assimilated and what it is assimilated to (i.e., taʾmanŭnā/ tāmanŭnā). This is the opinion of most of my teachers, and it is correct for the specification of its indication and its soundness in terms of analogy.

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: The Kufans and Nāfiʿ read yartaʿ(i) wa-yalʿab with yāʾ on both, and the rest with nūn (i.e., nartaʿ(i) wa-nalʿab). The two of the holy cities apply kasrah to the ʿayn of yartaʿi/nartaʿi and the rest makes it ǧazm (i.e., yartaʿ/nartaʿ).

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: Warš, al-Kisāʾī and ʾAbū ʿAmr—when he weakens his hamzah—read aḏ-ḏību without hamzah. The rest read it with hamzah in connected speech and pause. Ḥamzah reads it according to his principle in pause (i.e., aḏ-ḏiʾbu in connected speech, aḏ-ḏīb# in pause).[124]

footnotes.text: See U.11.6.1. for Ḥamzah’s pausal rules.

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: The Kufans read yā bušrā/ē in the pattern fuʿlā/ē. Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī apply ʾimālah to the fatḥah (i.e., yā bušrē). The rest read it with ʾalif after the rāʾ and fatḥah on the yāʾ (i.e., yā bušrā/ǟ-ya). Warš reads the rāʾ in between the two sounds (i.e., yā bušrǟ-ya), and the rest read it with pure fatḥah (i.e., yā bušrā-ya). The majority of the people of the oral tradition in the manner of ʾAbū ʿAmr read it like that (i.e., ya-bušrā-ya, not ya-bušrē-ya). This is what Ibn Muǧāhid says,[125] and I recited it like that, and texts from him via al-Sūsī from al-Yazīdī and others also convey it.[126]

footnotes.text: Al-Dānī cites Ibn Muǧāhid’s book Kitāb qirāʾat ʾAbī ʿAmr in his Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān for this opinion (al-Dānī 2007, 1226).

The discussion here clearly implies that some people stipulated that this word is to be read as yā bušrē-ya (or yā bušrǟ-ya) in the reading of ʾAbū ʿAmr, which is the expected reflex of a fuʿlā noun whose last root letter is rāʾ (see U.13.). See the discussion in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān and the Našr (Ibn al-Ǧazarī 2018, §1987; al-Dānī 2007, 1125–26).

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn Ḏakwān read hīta laka with kasrah on the hāʾ without hamzah and fatḥah on the tāʾ. Hišām reads it like that, except that he did apply the hamzah (i.e., hiʾta laka), and it has been transmitted from him with ḍammah on the tāʾ (i.e., hiʾtu laka). Ibn Kaṯīr reads it with fatḥah on the hāʾ and ḍammah on the tāʾ (i.e., haytu laka). The rest read it with fatḥah on both (i.e., hayta laka).

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: The Kufans and Nāfiʿ read al-muḫlaṣīna when before it there is a definite article whenever it occurs with fatḥah on the lām. The rest read it with kasrah (i.e., al-muḫliṣīna).

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads ḥāšā li-llāhi in two cases (here and in Q12:51) with ʾalif in connected speech, and when he pauses, he removes it, following what is written (i.e., حش ḥāš#). This is transmitted from al-Yazīdī in written form by his son ʾAbū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [Ibn al-Yazīdī], ʾAbū Ḥamdūn, ʾAḥmad b. Wāṣil and ʾAbū Šuʿayb [al-Sūsī] in the transmission of ʾAbū al-ʿAbbās the belletrist from him (al-Sūsī).[127] The rest read it without ʾalif in connected speech and pause (i.e., ḥāša, ḥāš#).

footnotes.text: None of the people mentioned here are referred to in U.4.3., but they are present in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān, except for the transmission path of ʾAbū al-ʿAbbās from al-Sūsī (al-Dānī 2007, 327–29).

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads daʾaban with a vowel on the hamzah and the rest without a vowel (i.e., daʾ/āban)

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-fīhi taʿṣirūna with tāʾ, the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaʿṣirūna).

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: Qālūn and al-Bazzī read bi-s-suwwi ʾillā with a geminate wāw replacing the hamzah in connected speech, and full pronunciation of the hamzah of ʾillā. Warš and Qunbul treat the two hamzahs carrying kasrahs according to their principles (i.e., bi-s-sūʾīllā)[128] and so does ʾAbū ʿAmr also according to his principle (i.e., bi-s-sū ʾillā). The rest treat them according to their principles (i.e., bi-s-sūʾi ʾillā).

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads ḥayṯu našāʾu with nūn and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., ḥayṯu yašāʾu).

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-qāla li-fityānihī with ʾalif and nūn, and the rest read it with tāʾ without the ʾalif (i.e., li-fityatihī).

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾaḫānā yaktal with yāʾ and the rest with nūn (i.e., naktal).

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ḫayrun ḥāfiḏ̣an with fatḥah on the ḥāʾ, ʾalif after it and kasrah on the fāʾ. The rest read it with a kasrah on the ḥāʾ, no vowel on the fāʾ and without an ʾalif (i.e., ḥifḏ̣an).

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: narfaʿu daraǧāti(n) has already been mentioned.[129]

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: Al-Bazzī, in my recitation to [ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz b. Ǧaʿfar] Ibn Ḫuwāstī al-Fārisī, transmitting from al-Naqqāš from ʾAbū Rabīʿah from him (al-Bazzī),[130] reads fa-lammà stāyasū minhū, wa-lā tāyasū min rawḥi llāhi ʾinnahū lā yāyasu (Q12:87), ḥattā ʾiḏà stāyasa r-rusulu (Q12:110) and in al-Raʿd ʾa-fa-lam yāyas illāḏīna ʾāmanū (Q13:31) with ʾalif and fatḥah on the yāʾ without hamzah in all five cases. The rest read it with hamzah and no vowel on the yāʾ without ʾalif in the word (i.e., istayʾasū, tayʾasū, yayʾasu, istayʾasa, yayʾas). When Ḥamzah pauses, he transfers the vowel of the hamzah onto the yāʾ in accordance with his principle (i.e., istayasū#, tayasū#, yayas#, istayas#, yayas#).

footnotes.text: This is the tilāwah ʾisnād of the Taysīr, but the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān mentions that most paths from al-Bazzī transmit with hamzah (al-Dānī 2007, 1234).

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads ʾinnaka la-ʾanta with a hamzah carrying a kasrah as a declarative sentence. The rest read it as an interrogative and follow their principles for that (i.e., ʾa-ʿinnaka, ʾā.innaka, ʾa.innaka, etc.).[131]

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads nūḥī ʾilayhim here and in al-Naḥl (Q16:43) and the first attestation in al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ (Q21:7) with nūn and kasrah on the ḥāʾ. The rest read it with yāʾ and fatḥah on the yāʾ (i.e., yūḥā/ǟ). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī applied ʾimālah according to their principle (i.e., yūḥē). Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read ʾa-fa-lā taʿqilūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaʿqilūna).

statements.heading: F.12. Sūrat Yūsuf (s)
statements.text: The Kufans read qad kuḏibū without gemination on the ḏāl and the rest with gemination (i.e., kuḏḏibū). Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read fa-nuǧǧiya man našāʾu with a single nūn, gemination of the ǧīm and fatḥah on the yāʾ. The rest read it with two nūns, with the second one carrying no vowel, no gemination of the ǧīm and no vowel on the yāʾ (i.e., nunǧī).

statements.heading: F.12.1. [Yāʾs of Q12]
statements.text: There are 22 yāʾs: 1. li-yaḥzununiya ʾan (Q12:13) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities. 2. rabbiya ʾaḥsana (Q12:23), 3. ʾarā/ē/ǟniya ʾaʿṣiru (Q12:36), 4. ʾarā/ē/ǟniya ʾaḥmalu (Q12:36), 5. ʾinniya ʾarā sabʿa (Q12:36), 6. ʾinniya ʾana/ā ʾaḫūka (Q12:69), 7. ʾabiya ʾaw yaḥkuma ḷḷāhu (Q12:80), 8. and ʾinniya ʾaʿlamu (Q12:96) with fatḥah on all seven by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 9. ʾinniya ʾarā/ē/ǟniya (Q12:36), 10. ʾinniya ʾarā/ē/ǟniya (Q12:36)—I mean the yāʾ of ʾinnī, 11. rabbiya ʾinnī taraktu (Q12:37), 12. nafsiya ʾinna (Q12:53), 13. rabbiya ʾinna (Q12:53), 14. yaʾ/āḏana liya ʾabiya (Q12:80)—I mean the yāʾ of liya, 15. rabbiya ʾinnahū huwa (Q12:98) 16. and biya ʾiḏ ʾaḫraǧanī (Q12:100) with fatḥah of all eight by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 17. ʾābāʾī ʾibrāhīm (Q12:38) 18. and laʿallī ʾarǧiʿu (Q12:46) both without a vowel by the Kufans. 19. ʾinniya ʾūfì l-kayla (Q12:59) 20. and sabīliya ʾadʿū (Q12:108) both with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ. 21. wa-ḥuzniya ʾilā (Q12:86) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 22. bayna ʾiḫwatiya ʾinna (Q12:100) with fatḥah by Warš.

statements.heading: F.12.2. [Removed yāʾs of Q12]
statements.text: There are two removed ones: 1. ḥattā tuʾtūnī mawṯiqan (Q12:66) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr. With the retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by ʾAbū ʿAmr (i.e., tuʾ/ūtūnī, tuʾ/ūtūn#). 2. ʾinnahū man yattaqī (Q12:90) with retention of the (yāʾ) in connected speech and pause by Qunbul, and removal by the rest in connected speech and pause (i.e., yattaqqi, yattaq#). ʾAbū Rabīʿah and Ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ transmitted from Qunbul[132] nartaʿī(#) (Q12:12) with retention of the yāʾ after the ʿayn in connected speech and pause, but transmitters other than those two report from (Qunbul) removal in connected speech and pause (i.e., nartaʿi, nartaʿ#). The rest removed it on both (i.e., y/nartaʿi, y/nartaʿ#).

footnotes.text: Neither of these transmission paths appear in the Taysīr, but they are present in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 305–6).

statements.heading: F.13. Sūrat al-Raʿd
statements.text: I have already mentioned yuġšì/yuġaššì l-layla.[133]

statements.heading: F.13. Sūrat al-Raʿd
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ read zarʿun wa-naḫīlun ṣinwānun ġayru with rafʿ of all four words. The rest read it with ḫafḍ (i.e., zarʿin wa-naḫīlin ṣinwānin ġayri). ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read yusqā bi-māʾin with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tusqā/ē/ǟ). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-yufaḍḍilu baʿḍahā with yāʾ and the rest with nūn (i.e., wa-nufaḍḍilu).

statements.heading: F.13. Sūrat al-Raʿd
statements.text: They disagreed on the two interrogatives when they meet, for example, in the words of the Almighty (ʾa-)ʾiḏā kunnā turāban (ʾa-)ʾinnā la-fī ḫalqin ǧadīdin, (ʾa)-ʾiḏā ḍalalnā fì l-ʾarḍi (ʾa)-ʾinnā la-fī ḫalqin ǧadīdin (Q32:10) and what is like it. These are altogether 11 places (Q13:5; Q17:49, 98; Q23:82; Q27:67; Q29:28–29; Q32:10; Q37:16, 53; Q56:47; Q79:10– 11). So Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī used to make the first of the two an interrogative and the second declarative (ʾā̆-ʾ/.iḏā kunnā turāban ʾinnā la-fī ḫalqin ǧadīdin). Nāfiʿ makes the interrogative with hamzah and yāʾ (i.e., bayna bayn) after it (i.e., ʾa-.iḏā kunnā turāban ʾinnā la-fī ḫalqin ǧadīdin).[134] Qālūn introduces an ʾalif between them (i.e., ʾā-.iḏā). Al-Kisāʾī places two hamzahs (i.e., ʾa-ʾiḏā). Nāfiʿ deviated from this principle in al-Naml (Q27:67) and al-ʿAnkabūt (Q29:28–29), so he makes the first of them the declarative and the second the interrogative (i.e., ʾiḏā kunnā turāban wa-ʾabāʾunā ʾā̆-.innā la-muḫraǧūna; ʾinnakum la-taʾ/ātūna l-faḥišata mā sabaqakum bihā min (ʾ)aḥadin min al-ʿālimīna // ʾā̆-.innakum la-taʾ/ātūna). Al-Kisāʾī also deviates from this principle, but only in al-ʿAnkabūt. He places the interrogative on both (i.e., ʾa-ʾinnakum la-taʾtūna l-faḥišatamā sabaqakum bihā min ʾaḥadin min al-ʿālimīna // ʾa-ʾinnakum la-taʾtūna). He also adds a nūn to the declarative in al-Naml, so he reads (ʾa-ʾiḏā kunnā turāban wa-ʾābāʾunā) ʾinnanā la-muḫraǧūna with two nūns. Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read both of the two (potential) interrogatives with hamzah and yāʾ in the whole Qurʾān (i.e., ʾa-.iḏā kunnā turāban ʾa-.innā la-fī ḫalqin ǧadīdin, etc.). Ibn Kaṯīr did not make the vowel long after the hamzah but ʾAbū ʿAmr did (i.e., ʾâ-.iḏā … ʾâ-.innā). Ibn Kaṯīr deviates from his principle in one place, namely, in al-ʿAnkabūt (Q29:28–29), so he makes the first of the two a declarative (i.e., ʾinnakumū la-taʾtūna l-faḥišata mā sabaqakumū bihā min ʾaḥadin min al-ʿālimīna // ʾa-.innakumū la-taʾtūna). ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read all of the two (potential) interrogatives with two hamzahs whenever they occur (i.e., ʾa-ʾiḏā kunnā turāban ʾa-ʾinnā la-fī ḫalqin ǧadīdin, etc.). Ḥafṣ deviates from his principle in the first occurrence of al-ʿAnkabūt only: he makes it a declarative with a single hamzah that carries the kasrah (i.e., ʾinnakum la-taʾtūna l-faḥišata mā sabaqakum bihā min ʾaḥadin min al-ʿālimīna // ʾa-ʾinnakum la-taʾtūna). Ibn ʿĀmir reads it, making the first of the two (potential) interrogatives a declarative with a single hamzah that carries a kasrah and the second as an interrogative with two hamzahs (i.e., ʾiḏā kunnā turāban ʾā̆-ʾinnā la-fī ḫalqin ǧadīdin, etc.). Hišām introduces between the two hamzahs an ʾalif (i.e., ʾā-ʾinnā), and Ibn Ḏakwān does not do so whenever it occurs (i.e., ʾa-ʾinnā). He (Ibn ʿĀmir) deviates from his principle in three places: in al-Naml (Q27:67), al-Wāqiʿah (Q56:47) and al-Nāziʿāt (79:10–11). In al-Naml and al-Nāziʿāt he reads it with the first one made an interrogative and the second a declarative, and he adds a nūn to the declarative of al-Naml just like al-Kisāʾī (i.e., ʾā̆-ʾiḏā kunnā turāban wa-ʾābāʾunā ʾinnanā; ʾā̆-ʾinnā la-mazdūdūna fì l-ḥāfirati // ʾiḏā kunnā ʿiḏ̣āman naḫiratan).[135] He reads it in al-Wāqiʿah making both of them interrogatives with two hamzahs. Hišām according to his principle introduces an ʾalif between the two hamzahs (i.e., ʾā̆-ʾiḏā mutnā wa-kunnā turāban wa-ʿiḏ̣āman ʾā̆-ʾinnā).

footnotes.text: This is a somewhat imprecise description: it is rather a hamzah pronounced bayna bayn, see the discussion in U.11.1.
This reading is the result of a different parsing of the undotted rasm   اﯩﯩﺎas  اﻧﻧﺎrather than اﯾﻧﺎ.

statements.heading: F.13. Sūrat al-Raʿd
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads hādin, wālin, wāqin and mā ʿinda ḷḷāhi bāqin with tanwīn in connected speech, but when he pauses on it, he pauses on all four words with yāʾ whenever it occurs and nothing else (i.e., hādī#, wālī#, wāqī#, bāqī#). The rest pronounce it in connected speech with tanwīn but pause without the yāʾ (i.e., hād#, wāl#, wāq#, bāq#).

statements.heading: F.13. Sūrat al-Raʿd
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾam hal yastawī with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tastawī).

statements.heading: F.13. Sūrat al-Raʿd
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-mimmā yūqīdūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tūqidūna).

statements.heading: F.13. Sūrat al-Raʿd
statements.text: Al-Bazzī reads ʾa-fa-lam yāyasu with fatḥah on the yāʾ without hamzah, as was al-ready mentioned.[136]

statements.heading: F.13. Sūrat al-Raʿd
statements.text: The Kufans read wa-ṣuddū ʿan is-sabīli and in Ġāfir (Q40:37) wa-ṣudda ʿan is-sabīli with ḍammah on the ṣād of both, and the rest read it with fatḥah on both (i.e., ṣaddū, ṣadda).

statements.heading: F.13. Sūrat al-Raʿd
statements.text: ʾuk(u)luhā was already mentioned.[137]

statements.heading: F.13. Sūrat al-Raʿd
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʿĀṣim and ʾAbū ʿAmr read wa-yuṯbitu wa-ʿindahum(ū) without gemination and the rest read it with gemination (wa-yuṯabbitu).

statements.heading: F.13. Sūrat al-Raʿd
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read wa-sa-yaʿlamu l-kuffāru in the plural and the rest in the singular (i.e., al-kāfiru).

statements.heading: F.13.1. [Removed yāʾ of Q13]
statements.text: There is a removed yāʾ: al-kabīru l-mutaʿālī (Q13:9) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr. The rest remove it in connected speech and pause (i.e., al-mutaʿāli, al-mutaʿāl#).

statements.heading: F.14. Sūrat ʾIbrāhīm (s)
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read al-ḥamīdi // llāhu with rafʿ of the hāʾ and the rest with ǧarr when starting on this verse and in connected speech (fī al-ḥālayn) (i.e., (#)aḷḷāhi).

statements.heading: F.14. Sūrat ʾIbrāhīm (s)
statements.text: rus(u)luhum (Q14:12),[138] sub(u)lanā (Q14:18)[139] and ar-rīḥ/ar-riyāḥ[140] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.14. Sūrat ʾIbrāhīm (s)
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ḫāliqu s-samāwati wa-l-ʾarḍi, and in al-Nūr ḫāliqu kulli dābbatin (Q24:45) with ʾalif, rafʿ of the qāf in the pattern fāʿil and ḫafḍ of what comes after that. The rest read ḫalaqa in the pattern faʿala with naṣb of what comes after it except that the tāʾ of as-samāwāti receives kasrah because it is the tāʾ of the feminine plural (i.e., ḫalaqa s-samawāti wa-l-(ʾ)arḍa).

statements.heading: F.14. Sūrat ʾIbrāhīm (s)
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads bi-muṣriḫiyyi ʾinnī with kasrah on the yāʾ. This is a dialectal usage al-Farrāʾ[141] and Quṭrub[142] talked about, and ʾAbū ʿAmr condoned it.[143] The rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., bi-muṣriḫiyya).

footnotes.text: Al-Farrāʾ attributes it not to Ḥamzah but Ḥamzah’s teacher al-ʾAʿmaš and Yaḥyā b. Waṯṯāb, who was in turn al-ʾAʿmaš’s teacher. He explicitly calls this form erroneous (wahm) (al-Farrāʾ 1983, II:75).
Quṭrub attributes it to al-ʾAʿmaš (and also to Ḥamzah in Quṭrub 2021, 774). He calls it “ugly and detestable” (radīʾun marġūbun ʿanh) (Quṭrub 2021, 413; see also 774).
Presumably the reader ʾAbū ʿAmr who was also an authority as a grammarian and could be expected to have an opinion on such matters. But possibly it is a third-person reference to al-Dānī himself.

statements.heading: F.14. Sūrat ʾIbrāhīm (s)
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read li-yaḍillū here and li-yaḍilla (Q22:9) in al-Ḥaǧǧ, Luqmān (Q31:6) and al-Zumar (Q39:8) with fatḥah on the yāʾ of all four and the rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., li-yuḍillū, li-yuḍilla).

statements.heading: F.14. Sūrat ʾIbrāhīm (s)
statements.text: lā bayʿa/un fīhi wa-lā ḫalāla/un has already been mentioned.[144]

statements.heading: F.14. Sūrat ʾIbrāhīm (s)
statements.text: Hišām, in my recitation to ʾAbū al-Fatḥ, reads ʾafʾīdatan min an-nāsi with yāʾ after the hamzah, and like that it specified in writing by al-Ḥulwānī from him,[145] the rest read it without yāʾ (i.e., ʾafʾidatan).

footnotes.text: Al-Ḥulwānī had a book dedicated to the transmission of Hišām (see Hamdan 2018, 62), which al-Dānī is referencing here.

statements.heading: F.14. Sūrat ʾIbrāhīm (s)
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads la-tazūlu minhu with fatḥah on the first lām and rafʿ on the second. The rest read it with kasrah on the first and naṣb of the second (i.e., li-tazūla).

statements.heading: F.14.1. [Yāʾs of Q14]
statements.text: There are three yāʾs: 1. wa-mā kāna liya (Q14:22) with fatḥah by Ḥafṣ. 2. qul li-ʿibādì llaḏīna (Q14:31) with no vowel by Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī. 3. ʾinniya ʾaskantu (Q14:37) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr.

statements.heading: F.14.2. [Removed yāʾs of Q14]
statements.text: There are three removed ones: 1. wa-ḫāfa waʿīdī (Q14:14) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Warš. 2. bi-mā ʾašraktumūnī (Q14:22) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by ʾAbū ʿAmr. 3. wa-taqabbal duʿāʾī (Q14:40) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr, and with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Warš, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥamzah.

statements.heading: F.15. Sūrat al-Ḥiǧr
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim read rubamā without gemination of the bāʾ and the rest read it with gemination (i.e., rubbamā).

statements.heading: F.15. Sūrat al-Ḥiǧr
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read mā nunazzilu with two nūns, the first carrying a ḍammah and the second a fatḥah, and with kasrah on the zāy, and al-malāʾikata with naṣb. ʾAbū Bakr reads it with tāʾ carrying a ḍammah, fatḥah on the nūn and zāy, and al-malāʾikatu with rafʿ (i.e., tunazzalu l-malāʾikatu). The rest read it like that, except that they apply the fatḥah to the tāʾ (i.e., tanazzalu l-malāʾikatu).

statements.heading: F.15. Sūrat al-Ḥiǧr
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads ʾinnamā sukirat without gemination of the kāf, and the rest with gemination (i.e., sukkirat).

statements.heading: F.15. Sūrat al-Ḥiǧr
statements.text: ar-rīḥa/riyāḥa laqāqiḥa,[146] ǧuz(u)ʾun (Q15:44),[147] al-muḫli/aṣīna (Q15:40)[148] and fa-ʾasri/fa-sri (Q15:65)[149] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.15. Sūrat al-Ḥiǧr
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, ʾAbū ʿAmr, Ḥafṣ and Hišām read wa-ʿuyūn and al-ʿuyūn with ḍammah on the ʿayn whenever it occurs. The rest read it with kasrah (i.e., wa-ʿiyūn, al-ʿiyūn).

statements.heading: F.15. Sūrat al-Ḥiǧr
statements.text: ʾinnā nabšuruka/nubašširuka has already been mentioned.[150]

statements.heading: F.15. Sūrat al-Ḥiǧr
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read wa-man yaqniṭu, in al-Rūm yaqniṭūna (Q30:36) and in al-Zumar (Q39:53) lā taqniṭū with kasrah on the nūn in all three and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., yaqnaṭu, yaqnaṭūna, taqnaṭū).

statements.heading: F.15. Sūrat al-Ḥiǧr
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾinnā la-munǧūhum without gemination and the rest with gemination (i.e., la-munaǧǧūhum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.15. Sūrat al-Ḥiǧr
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads qadarnā ʾinnahā here and in al-Naml (Q27:57) without gemination of the dāl. The rest read it with gemination (i.e., qaddarnā).

statements.heading: F.15.1. [Yāʾs of Q15]
statements.text: There are four yāʾs: 1. ʿibādiya (2.) ʾanniya ʾana (Q15:49) and 2. ʾinniya ʾana n-naḏīru (Q15:89) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 3. banātiya ʾin kuntum (Q15:71) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ.

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: I have already mentioned ʿammā y/tušrikūna in these two places.[151]

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads nunbitu lakum with nūn and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yunbitu).

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads wa-š-šamsu wa-l-qamaru wa-n-nuǧūmu musaḫḫarātun with rafʿ of all four. Ḥafṣ reads rafʿ of an-nuǧūmu and musaḫḫarātun only (i.e., wa-š-šamsa wa-l-qamara wa-n-nuǧūmu musaḫḫarātun). The rest read with naṣb and with the tāʾ of musaḫḫarātin carrying a kasrah (i.e., wa-š-šamsa wa-l-qamara wa-n-nuǧūma musaḫḫarātin).

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: ʿĀṣim reads wa-llaḏīna yadʿūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tadʿūna).

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: Al-Bazzī, with disagreement in transmission from him, reads ʾayna šurakāya llaḏīna without hamzah. The rest read it with hamzah (i.e., šurakāʾiya). Nāfiʿ reads tušāqqūni fīhim with kasrah on the nūn and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., tušāqqūna).

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads allaḏīna yatawaffēhum in two places (here and in Q16:32) with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tatawaffā/ē/ǟhum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: ʾillā ʾan y/taʾ/ātīhi/umu l-malāʾikatu has already been mentioned.[152]

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: The Kufans read lā yahdī man with fatḥah on the yāʾ and kasrah on the dāl. The rest read it with ḍammah on the yāʾ and fatḥah on the dāl (i.e., yuhdā/ǟ).

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read fa-yakūna here and in Yā-Sīn (Q36:82) with naṣb. The rest read it with rafʿ (i.e., fa-yakūnu).

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: nūḥī/ē/ǟ/ā ʾilayhi/um(ū) has already been mentioned.[153]

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾa-wa-lam taraw ʾilā mā with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaraw). ʾAbū ʿAmr reads tatafayyaʾu ḏ̣ilāluhū with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yatafayyaʾu).

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads mufriṭūna with kasrah on the rāʾ and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., mufraṭūna).

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū Bakr read nasqīkum here and in al-Muʾminūn (Q23:21) with fatḥah on the nūn and the rest with ḍammah (i.e., nusqīkum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: yaʿri/ušūna has already been mentioned.[154]

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr read taǧḥadūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaǧḥadūna).

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: min buṭūni ʾu/immi/ahātikum(ū) has already been mentioned.[155]

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamzah read ʾa-lam taraw ʾilà ṭ-ṭayri with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaraw).

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read yawma ḏ̣aʿnikum with no vowel on the ʿayn and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., ḏ̣aʿanikum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʿĀṣim read wa-li-naǧziyanna llaḏīna with nūn. Al-Naqqāš said, transmitting from al-ʾAḫfaš from Ibn Ḏakwān, that he reads it like that. In my opinion, however, this is a mistake, because al-ʾAḫfaš, transmitting from him, mentioned in his book that it is with yāʾ, and the rest read it with yāʾ (i.e., wa-li-yaǧziyanna llaḏīna).[156]

footnotes.text: Al-ʾAḫfaš had two books dedicated to the transmission of Ibn Ḏakwān, Kitāb al-ḫāṣṣ and Kitāb al-ʿāmm which sometimes differ in the details. As these works are not extant, it is difficult to decide which of the two he might be referring to (Hamdan 2018, 75–76).

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: al-qud(u)s has been mentioned.[157]

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read yalḥadūna here with fatḥah on the yāʾ and ḥāʾ. The rest read it with ḍammah on the yāʾ and kasrah on the ḥāʾ (i.e., yulḥidūna).

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads min baʿdi mā fatanū with fatḥah on the fāʾ and tāʾ; the rest read it with ḍammah on the fāʾ and kasrah on the tāʾ (i.e., futinū).

statements.heading: F.16. Sūrat al-Naḥl
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads fī ḍīqin here and in an-Naml (Q27:70) with kasrah on the ḍād. The rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., ḍayqin). There are no yāʾs in it at all.

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads ʾa-lā yattaḫiḏū with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tattaḫiḏū).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamzah read li-yasūʾa wuǧūhakum with yāʾ and naṣb of the hamzah in the singular. Al-Kisāʾī reads it with nūn and naṣb of the hamzah in the plural (i.e., li-nasūʾa). The rest read it with yāʾ and a hamzah that carries a ḍammah in between two wāws in the plural (i.e., li-yasūʾū).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: yabšuru/yubašširu l-muʾminīna has already been mentioned.[158]

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads yulaqqāhu with gemination and a yāʾ that carries a ḍammah. The rest read it without gemination and with a yāʾ that carries a fatḥah (i.e., yalqā/ǟ/ēhū̆).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾimmā yabluġānni with kasrah on the nūn and with an ʾalif before it. The rest read it with fatḥah (on the nūn) without ʾalif and there is no disagreement on the gemination of the nūn (i.e., yabluġanna). Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ read ʾuffin here, in al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ (Q21:67) and in al-ʾAḥqāf (Q46:17) with tanwīn and with kasrah on the fāʾ. Ibn Kaṯīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with fatḥah without tanwīn (i.e., ʾuffa). The rest read it with kasrah without tanwīn (i.e., ʾuffi).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads kāna ḫiṭâʾan with kasrah on the ḫāʾ and fatḥah on the ṭāʾ with length. Ibn Ḏakwān reads it with fatḥah on the ḫāʾ and ṭāʾ without length (i.e., ḫaṭaʾan). The rest read it with kasrah on the ḫāʾ without a vowel on the ṭāʾ (i.e., ḫiṭʾan).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read fa-lā tusrif. The rest read it with yāʾ (i.e., yusrif).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read bi-l-qisṭāsi here and in al-Šuʿarāʾ (Q26:182) with kasrah on the qāf. The rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., bi-l-qusṭāsi).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read kāna sayyiʾuhū with ḍammah on the hamzah and hāʾ as masculine (noun). The rest read it with fatḥah on both with tanwīn, as feminine (noun) (i.e., sayyiʾatan).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read li-yaḏkurū here and in al-Furqān (Q25:50) with no vowel on the ḏāl and with ḍammah on an ungeminated kāf. The rest read it with fatḥah on both and with gemination on both (i.e., li-yaḏḏakkarū).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and Ḥafṣ read kamā yaqūlūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taqūlūna).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʿammā taqūlūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaqūlūna).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: The two of the holy cities, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū Bakr read yusabbiḥu lahū with a yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tusabbiḥu).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: The two interrogatives in two places[159] and wa-za/ubūran (Q17:55)[160] have al-ready been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads wa-raǧilika with kasrah on the ǧīm; the rest read it without vowel (i.e., wa-raǧlika).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read ʾan naḫsifa, ʾaw nursila, ʾan nuʿīdakum(ū), fa-nursila and fa-nuġriqakum(ū) with nūn on all five. The rest read it with yāʾ (i.e., yaḫsifa, yursila, yuʿīdakum, fa-yursila, fa-yuġriqakum).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾaʿmē in both occurrences (in this verse) with ʾimālah. ʾAbū ʿAmr applies ʾimālah to the first one only (i.e., ʾaʿmē … ʾaʿmā). Warš reads them in between (the two sounds) in accordance with his general principle (i.e., ʾaʿmǟ … ʾaʿmǟ). The rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., ʾaʿmā … ʾaʿmā).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ḫilāfaka ʾillā with kasrah on the ḫāʾ and fatḥah on the lām with ʾalif after it. The rest read it with fatḥah on the ḫāʾ and with no vowel on the lām (i.e., ḫalfaka).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: Ibn Ḏakwān reads wa-nāʾa bi-ǧānibihī here and in Fuṣṣilat (Q41:51), putting the hamzah after the ʾalif. The rest places the hamzah before the ʾalif (i.e., naʾā). Al-Kisāʾī and Ḫalaf apply ʾimālah to the fatḥah of the nūn and the hamzah in both sūrahs (i.e., neʾē), but Ḫallād applies ʾimālah only to the hamzah (i.e., naʾē). It has been transmitted from ʾAbū Šuʿayb [al-Sūsī] like that as well (i.e., naʾē).[161] ʾAbū Bakr applies ʾimālah to the fatḥah of the hamzah here and pronounces it with a pure vowel there (i.e., Q17:83 naʾē, but Q41:51 naʾā). The rest read both with fatḥah (i.e., naʾā). Warš reads it in accordance with his principle of stem-final yāʾ (i.e., naʾǟ).

footnotes.text: The passive formulation should probably be understood as implying that it has also been reported differently, indeed naʾā is also attributed to al-Sūsī (al-Dānī 2007, 1292).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: The Kufans read ḥattā tafǧura with fatḥah on the tāʾ and ḍammah on the ǧīm without gemination. The rest read it with ḍammah on the tāʾ and kasrah on the ǧīm with gemination (i.e., tufaǧǧira). There is no disagreement on the second occurrence (Q17:91, all read fa-tufaǧǧira).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read kisafan with fatḥah on the sīn and the rest without vowel (i.e., kisfan).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read qāla subḥāna rabbī with ʾalif and the rest read qul without ʾalif.

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads la-qad ʿalimtu with ḍammah on the tāʾ and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., ʿalimta).

statements.heading: F.17. Sūrat al-ʾIsrāʾ
statements.text: The pausing on ʾayyan mā is mentioned in its chapter.[162]

statements.heading: F.17.1. [Yāʾ of Q17]
statements.text: There is one yāʾ: it is raḥmati rabbiya ʾiḏān (Q17:100) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr.

statements.heading: F.17.2. [Removed yāʾs of Q17]
statements.text: There are two removed ones: 1. la-ʾin (ʾ)aḫḫartanī ʾilā (Q17:62) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr, and retention in connected speech by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 2. fa-h(u)wa l-muhtadī (Q17:97) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr.

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads ʿiwaǧā, placing a slight silence after the ʾalif, without drawing breath (qaṭʿ) and without tanwīn, and then he says qayyiman. It is also like that where he used to introduce a silence while intending connected speech on the ʾalif in Yā-Sīn Q36:52) in the speech of the Almighty min marqadinā and then he says hāḏā. Likewise, he introduces silence on the nūn in al-Qiyāmah (Q75:27) in His speech man and then he says rāqin. He likewise introduces silence on the lām in al-Mutaffifīn (Q83:14) in His speech bal and then he says rāna. The rest pronounces these in connected speech without silence and they apply assimilation to the nūn and lām to the rāʾ (i.e., ʿiwaǧan, min marqadinā hāḏā, mar⸗rāqin, bar⸗rā/ēna).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads min ladʷnihī with no vowel on the dāl, with a little bit of ʾišmām of the ḍammah, and with kasrah on the nūn and hāʾ with application of ṣilah of yāʾ to the hāʾ. The rest read it with ḍammah on the dāl, without a vowel on the nūn and with ḍammah on the hāʾ (i.e., ladunhu). Ibn Kaṯīr reads it with ṣilah of the wāw according to his principle (i.e., ladunhū). yabšuru/yubašširu l-muʾminīna has already been mentioned.[163]

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read marfiqan with fatḥah on the mīm and kasrah on the fāʾ. The rest read it with kasrah on the mīm and fatḥah on the fāʾ (i.e., mirfaqan).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir tazwarru ʿan kahfihim with no vowel on the zāy and gemination of the rāʾ. The Kufans read it with fatḥah on the zāy without gemination and with an ʾalif after it (i.e., tazāwaru). The rest read it with gemination of the zāy and the retention of the ʾalif (tazzāwaru).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: The two of the holy cities read la-mulliʾta with gemination of the lām and the rest read it without gemination (i.e., la-muliʾ/īta). ruʿ(u)ban has already been mentioned.[164]

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr, ʾAbū Bakr and Ḥamzah read bi-warqikum with no vowel on the rāʾ. The rest read it with kasrah (i.e., bi-wariqikum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads wa-lā tušrik with tāʾ and ǧazm of the kāf. The rest read it with yāʾ and rafʿ of the kāf (i.e., yušriku).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: bi-l-ġadāti/bi-l-ġudwati has already been mentioned.[165]

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ṯalāṯa miʾati sinīna without tanwīn and the rest with tanwīn (i.e., ṯalāṯa miʾatin sinīna).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: ʿĀṣim reads wa-kāna lahū ṯamarun and wa-ʾuḥīṭu bi-ṯamarihī (Q18:42) with fatḥah on both the ṯāʾ and the mīm. ʾAbū ʿAmr reads it with ḍammah on the ṯāʾ and without a vowel on the mīm (i.e., ṯumrun, ṯumrihī). The rest read it with ḍammah on both (i.e., ṯumurun, ṯumurihī).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: The two of the holy cities and Ibn ʿĀmir read ḫayran minhumā with mīm as dual and the rest without the mīm as singular (i.e., minhā).[166]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 141).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads lākinnā huwa ḷḷāhu with retention of the ʾalif in connected speech and the rest remove it (i.e., lākinna). Everyone retains it in pause (i.e., lākinnā#).[167]

footnotes.text: The rasm of this word is  ل೺ടا and is understood to be a contraction of lākin ʾana.

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-lam yakun lahū with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., takun).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read hunālika l-wilāyatu with kasrah on the wāw and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., al-walāyatu). ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read li-llāhi l-ḥaqqu with rafʿ and the rest with the ǧarr (i.e., al-ḥaqqi). ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read wa-ḫayrun ʿuqban with no vowel on the qāf and the rest with ḍammah (i.e., ʿuquban).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: taḏrūhu r-riyāḥu/r-rīḥu has already been mentioned.[168]

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: The Kufans and Nāfiʿ read yawma nusayyiru with nūn, kasrah on the yāʾ and naṣb of al-ǧibāla. The rest read it with tāʾ and fatḥah on the yāʾ and with rafʿ of al-ǧibālu (i.e., tusayyaru l-ǧibālu).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads yawma naqūlu with nūn and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaqūlu).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: The Kufans read qubulan with two ḍammahs and the rest read it with kasrah on the qāf and fatḥah on the bāʾ (i.e., qibalan).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads li-mahlakihim and in al-Naml mahlaka ʾahlihī (Q27:49) with fatḥah on the mīm and lām. Ḥafṣ reads it with fatḥah on the mīm and kasrah on the lām (i.e., li-mahlikihim and mahlika ʾahlihī). The rest read it with ḍammah on the mīm and fatḥah on the lām (i.e., li-muhlakihim(ū) and muhlaka ʾahlihī).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads wa-mā ʾansānīhu ʾillā and in al-Fatḥ ʿalayhu ḷḷāha (Q48:10) with ḍammah on the hāʾ of both in connected speech. The rest read them with kasrah (i.e., ʾansānīhī̆ and ʿalayhi llāha).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads mimmā ʿullimta rašadan with fatḥah on the rāʾ and sīn. The rest read it with ḍammah on the rāʾ and with no vowel on the šīn (i.e., rušdan).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read fa-lā tasʾalannī with fatḥah on the lām with gemination of the nūn. The rest read it with no vowel on the lām and no gemination on the nūn (i.e., tasʾalnī).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read li-yaġraqa with a yāʾ that carries a fatḥah and with fatḥah on the rāʾ, and ʾahluhā with rafʿ of the lām. The rest read it with a tāʾ that carries a ḍammah, with kasrah on the rāʾ and naṣb of the lām (li-tuġriqa ʾahlahā).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read nafsan zakiyyatan with gemination of the yāʾ without ʾalif. The rest read it with ʾalif and without gemination of the yāʾ (i.e., zākiyatan). Nāfiʿ, ʾAbū Bakr and Ibn Ḏakwān read nukuran in two places, here (Q18:74 and 87) and in al-Ṭalāq (Q65:8), with ḍammah on the kāf. The rest read it without a vowel (i.e., nukran).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads min ladunī with ḍammah on the dāl and with no gemination of the nūn. ʾAbū Bakr reads it with no vowel of the dāl, with ʾišmām of the ḍammah and with no gemination of the nūn (i.e., ladʷnī). The rest read it with ḍammah on the dāl and gemination of the nūn (i.e., ladunnī).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read wa-la-taḫiḏta/taḫitta ʿalayhī̆ with no gemination of the tāʾ and kasrah on the ḫāʾ. The rest read it with gemination of the tāʾ and fatḥah on the ḫāʾ (i.e., la-ttaḫaḏta/la-ttaḫatta).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr read ʾan yubaddilahumā (here), in al-Taḥrīm ʾan yubaddilahū (Q66:5) and in Nūn wa-l-Qalam[169] ʾan yubaddilanā (Q68:32), in all three places, with gemination. The rest read it without gemination (i.e., yubdilahumā, yubdilahū, yubdilanā). Ibn ʿĀmir reads ruḥuman with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and the rest read it without vowel (i.e., ruḥman).

footnotes.text: Nūn wa-l-Qalam is an alternative name for al-Qalam (Kandil 1992, 52).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read fa-ʾatbaʿa (Q17:85), ṯumma ʾatbaʿa (Q17:89) and ṯumma ʾatbaʿa (Q17:92), in all three places, with ʾalif al-qaṭʿ and ungeminated tāʾ. The rest read it with ʾalif al-waṣl with geminate tāʾ (i.e., ittabaʿa).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read fī ʿaynin ḥāmiyatin with ʾalif without hamzah and the rest read it without the ʾalif and with hamzah (i.e., ḥamiʾatin).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read fa-lahū ǧazāʾan il-ḥusnā/ē with tanwīn and naṣb. The rest read it with rafʿ and without tanwīn (i.e., ǧazāʾu l-ḥusnā/ǟ).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ read bayna s-saddayni with fatḥah on the sīn and the rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., as-suddayni). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read yufqihūna with ḍammah on the yāʾ and kasrah on the qāf. The rest read it with fatḥah on both (i.e., yafqahūna).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: ʿĀṣim reads ʾinna yaʾǧūǧa wa-maʾǧūǧa here and in al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ (Q21:96) with hamzah on both. The rest read it without hamzah (i.e., yāǧūǧa wa-māǧūǧa). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read laka ḫarāǧan here and in al-Muʾminūn (Q23:72) with ʾalif and the rest read it without ʾalif (i.e., ḫarǧan). Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū Bakr read wa-baynahum suddan with ḍammah on the sīn and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., saddan).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr mā makkananī with two ungeminated nūns, the first of which carries a fatḥah and the second a kasrah. The rest read it with one geminated nūn that carries a kasrah (i.e., makannī).[170]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 146).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads radman // iʾtūnī, with kasrah on the tanwīn and a hamzah without vowel with the meaning of maǧīʾ ‘to come’ (as opposed to ʾātūnī, which has the meaning ʾiʿṭāʾ ‘to give’). When he starts, he places kasrah on the hamzat al-waṣl, replacing the hamzah with no vowel after it with yāʾ (i.e., #ʾītūnī). The rest read it with hamzat al-qaṭʿ and length after it when starting on it and in connected speech (fī al-ḥālayn) (i.e., ʾātūnī). Warš, in accordance with his general principle, transfers the vowel of the hamzah onto the tanwīn before it (i.e., radman‿ātūnī).[171]

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read bayna ṣ-ṣudufayni with two ḍammahs, and ʾAbū Bakr with ḍammah on the ṣād and no vowel on the dāl (i.e., aṣ-ṣudfayni) and the rest read it with two fatḥahs (i.e., aṣ-ṣadafayni). Ḥamzah and ʾAbū Bakr, with disagreement in transmission from the latter, read qāla ʾtūnī with a vowelless hamzah after the lām with the meaning of maǧīʾ ‘to come’ (as opposed to ʾātūnī, which has the meaning ʾiʿṭāʾ ‘to give’). When they start, it is with kasrah for the hamzat al-waṣl and with replacement of the vowelless hamzah with yāʾ (i.e., #ʾītūnī). The rest read it with full pronunciation of the hamzah and length after it when starting on it and in connected speech (fī al-ḥālayn) (i.e., ʾātūnī).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads fa-mà sṭṭāʿū with gemination of the ṭāʾ and the rest without gemination (i.e., isṭāʿū).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: The Kufans read ǧaʿalahū dakkâʾa with length and hamzah and without tanwīn. The rest read it with tanwīn and without hamzah (i.e., dakkan).

statements.heading: F.18. Sūrat al-Kahf
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read qablu ʾan yanfada with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tanfada).

statements.heading: F.18.1. [Yāʾs of Q18]
statements.text: There are nine yāʾs: 1. rabbiya ʾaʿlamu (Q18:22), 2. bi-rabbiya ʾaḥadan (Q18:38), 3. rabbiya ʾan yuʾ/ūtiyani (Q18:40) and 4. bi-rabbiya ʾaḥadan (Q18:42) with fatḥah on all four by the two of the holy cities, and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 5. maʿiya ṣabran in three places (Q18:67, 6. 72, 7. 75) with fatḥah by Ḥafṣ. 8. sa-taǧiduniya ʾin šāʾa ḷḷāhu (Q18:69) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ. 9. min dūniya ʾawliyāʾa (Q18:102) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr.

statements.heading: F.18.2. [Removed yāʾs of Q18]
statements.text: There are seven removed ones: 1. al-muhtadī (Q18:17) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 2. ʾan yahdiyanī (Q18:24), 3. ʾan yuʾ/ūtiyanī (Q18:40) and 4. ʿalā ʾan tuʿallimanī (Q18:66) with retention (of the yāʾ) in both connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr, and retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 5. ʾin taranī ʾana ʾaqalla (Q18:39) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr and retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Qālūn and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 6. mā kunnā nabġī (Q18:64) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr, and retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Nāfiʿ, ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī. 7. fa-lā tasʾalanni (18:70) with removal in connected speech and pause by Ibn Ḏakwān, with disagreement transmitted from al-ʾAḫfaš from him (Ibn Ḏakwān). The rest retain (the yāʾ) in connected speech and pause, and that is how it is written in the rasm.

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr and al-Kisāʾī read ʾimālah on the hāʾ and yāʾ of kāf-hē-yē-ʿayn-ṣād. I recited it like that, in the transmission of ʾAbū Šuʿayb [as-Sūsī], to [ʾAbū al-Fatḥ] Fāris b. ʾAḥmad according to his (as-Sūsī’s) recitation. Ibn Kaṯīr and Ḥafṣ read it with fatḥah on both (i.e., kāf-hā-yā-ʿayn-ṣād). Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamzah read it with fatḥah on the hāʾ and ʾimālah of the yāʾ (i.e., kāf-hā-yē-ʿayn-ṣād). ʾAbū ʿAmr reads with ʾimālah of the hāʾ and a fatḥah on the yāʾ (i.e., kāf-hē-yā-ʿayn-ṣād). Nāfiʿ reads the hāʾ and yāʾ in between (ʾimālah and fatḥah) (i.e., kāf-hǟ-yǟ-ʿayn-ṣād).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: The two of the holy cities and ʿĀṣim did not assimilate the dāl of the (disconnected) letters to the ḏāl (of ḏikru in the next verse) (i.e., kāf-hā/ē-yā/ē-ʿayn-ṣād // ḏikru). The rest assimilated it (i.e., kāf-hā/ē-yā/ē-ʿayn-ṣāḏ⸗ḏikru).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr and Ibn ʿĀmir read zakariyyāʾa // ʾid nādā and yā zakariyyāʾu ʾinnā (Q19:7) and what is like it with full retention of both hamzahs. This has already been mentioned.[172]

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read yariṯnī wa-yariṯ with ǧazm of the ṯāʾ of both. The rest read both with rafʿ (i.e., yariṯunī wa-yariṯu).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: ʾinnā nabšuruka/nubašširuka and li-tabšuru/li-tubašširu bihī (Q19:97) have already been mentioned.[173]

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ read all cases of ʿitiyyan, ṣiliyyan and ǧiṯiyyan that occur in this sūrah (Q19:8, 68, 69, 70, 72) with kasrah on the first root letter. Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī also read bikiyyan (Q19:58) with kasrah on the bāʾ. The rest read the first root letter of (all of) that with ḍammah (i.e., ʿutiyyan, ṣuliyyan, ǧuṯiyyan, bukiyyan).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ḫalaqnāka with nūn and ʾalif, and the rest with a tāʾ that carries a ḍammah without ʾalif (i.e., ḫalaqtuka).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: Warš and ʾAbū ʿAmr read li-yahaba with yāʾ and it was transmitted like that by al-Ḥulwānī from Qālūn.[174] The rest read it with hamzah (i.e., li-ʾahaba).

footnotes.text: This ʾisnād is not present in the Taysīr, but it is present in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 287–89).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: Ḥafṣ and Ḥamzah read wa-kuntu nasyan with fatḥah on the nūn and the rest with kasrah (i.e., nisyan).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʾAbū ʿAmr and ʾAbū Bakr read man taḥtahā with fatḥah on the mīm and the rest with kasrah (i.e., min taḥtihā).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads tusāqiṭ ʿalayki with ḍammah on the tāʾ and kasrah on the qāf without gemination of the sīn. Ḥamzah reads both (consonants) with fatḥah without gemination (i.e., tasāqaṭ). The rest read both (consonants) with fatḥah and gemination (i.e., tassāqaṭ).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read qawla l-ḥaqqi with naṣb of the lām and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., qawlu l-ḥaqqi).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read wa-ʾinna ḷḷāha with kasrah on the hamzah and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., wa-ʾanna).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: kun fa-yakūna/u[175] and yā ʾabah/t#[176] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: The Kufans read muḫlaṣan with fatḥah on the lām and the rest with kasrah (i.e., muḫliṣan).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: yadḫulūna/yudḫalūna l-ǧannata has already been mentioned.[177]

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: Ibn Ḏakwān reads ʾiḏā mā muttu with a single hamzah that carries a kasrah as a declarative. Al-Naqqāš, transmitting from al-ʾAḫfaš from him (Ibn Ḏakwān), said that it was with two hamzahs (i.e., ʾaʾiḏā).[178] The rest read it as an interrogative and they follow in what has preceded in their respective manners (i.e., ʾaʾiḏā, ʾā.iḏā etc.).[179]

footnotes.text: This is the tilāwah ʾisnād for Ibn Ḏakwān. Other transmissions (but not the riwāyah ʾisnād in the Taysīr) report the form that al-Dānī mentions first, as can be seen in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 1344).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read ʾa-wa-lā yaḏkuru with no vowel on the ḏāl and with ḍammah on an ungeminated kāf. The rest read both with fatḥah and gemination (i.e., yaḏḏakkaru).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads ṯumma nunǧì llaḏīna without gemination and the rest read it with gemination (i.e., nunaǧǧī).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads ḫayrun muqāman with ḍammah on the mīm and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., maqāman).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: Qālūn and Ibn Ḏakwān read ʿaṯāṯan wa-riyyan with gemination of the yāʾ without hamzah, and the rest read it with hamzah (i.e., wa-riʾyan). Ḥamzah pauses in the manner mentioned in his respective section (i.e., riyyā#).[180]

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read mālan wa-wuldan, ar-raḥmānu wuldan (Q19:88), li-rraḥmāni wuldan (Q19:91), ʾan yattaḫiḏa wuldan (Q19:92) and in al-Zuḫruf li-r-raḥmāni wuldun (Q43:81) with ḍammah on the wāw and no vowel on the lām in all five cases. The rest read it with fatḥahs on both of these five (i.e., waladan, waladun).

statements.heading: F.19. Sūrat Maryam (s)
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read yakādu s-samāwātu here and in al-Šūrā (Q42:5) with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., takādu). The two of the holy cities, Ḥafṣ and al-Kisāʾī read yatafaṭṭarna here with tāʾ and with fatḥah on the geminated ṭāʾ. The rest read it with nūn and with kasrah on an ungeminated ṭāʾ (i.e., yanfaṭirna).

statements.heading: F.19.1. [Yāʾs of Q19]
statements.text: There are six yāʾs: 1. min warāʾiya wa-kānat (Q19:5) with fatḥah by Ibn Kaṯīr. 2. iǧʿal liya ʾāyatan (Q19:10) and 3. laka rabbiya ʾinnahū (Q19:47) with fatḥah of both by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 4. ʾinniya ʾaʿūḏu (Q19:18) and 5. ʾinniya ʾaḫāfu (Q19:45) with fatḥah of both by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 6. ʾātānì l-kitāba (Q19:30) with no vowel by Ḥamzah.

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read with ʾimālah of the fatḥah on the ṭāʾ and hāʾ (of ṭā-hā) (i.e., ṭē-hē). Warš and ʾAbū ʿAmr only read with ʾimālah of the hāʾ (i.e., ṭā-hē). The rest read both with fatḥah (i.e., ṭā-hā).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads li-ʾahlihu mkuṯū here and in al-Qaṣaṣ (Q28:29) with ḍammah on the hāʾ in connected speech. The rest read it with kasrah (i.e., li-ʾahlihi mkuṯū).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read ʾanniya ʾana rabbuka with fatḥah on the hamzah and the rest with kasrah (i.e., ʾinnī/ʾinniya ʾana rabbuka). The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read ṭuwan here and in al-Nāziʿāt (Q79:16) with tanwīn and placing a kasrah on there (i.e., on the n of the tanwīn) due to the (meeting of) two letters that do not carry a vowel (i.e., ṭuwan iḏhab). The rest read it without tanwīn (i.e., ṭuwā, ṭuwǟ).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads wa-ʾannā with gemination of the nūn and iḫtarnāka with nūn and ʾalif. The rest read it without gemination of the nūn and with a tāʾ that carries a ḍammah without ʾalif (i.e., wa-ʾana ḫtartuka).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads ʾaḫī // ʾašdud with ʾalif al-qaṭʿ and fatḥah when starting on it and in connected speech (fī al-ḥālayn), and wa-ʾušrikhu (Q20:32) with ḍammah on the hamzah. The rest read it with ʾalif al-waṣl of the first and when starting on it with ḍammah, and with fatḥah on the hamzah in the second case (i.e., ʾaḫì šdud, #ʾušdud; wa-ʾašrikhū̆).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: The Kufans read mahdan here and in al-Zuḫruf (Q43:10) with fatḥah on the mīm and no vowel on the hāʾ. The rest read it with kasrah on the mīm, fatḥah on the hāʾ and with ʾalif after it (i.e., mihādan). They did not disagree on what occurs in al-Nabaʾ (Q78:6) (i.e., all read mihādan).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamzah read makānan suwan with ḍammah on the sīn. The rest read it with kasrah (i.e., siwan). ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī pause on su/iwē# and in al-Qiyāmah on ʾan yutraka sudē# (Q75:36) with ʾimālah. Warš and ʾAbū ʿAmr (pause on it) according to their principle in between (the two sounds) (i.e., siwǟ#, sudǟ#). The rest read it with fatḥah in accordance with their principles (i.e., su/iwā#, sudā#).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read fa-yusḥitakum with ḍammah on the yāʾ and kasrah on the ḥāʾ and the rest read it with fatḥah on both (i.e., fa-yasḥatakum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and Ḥafṣ read qālū ʾin with no vowel on the nūn and the rest with gemination (i.e., ʾinna). ʾAbū ʿAmr reads hāḏayni with yāʾ[181] and the rest with ʾalif (i.e., hāḏān(n)i). Ibn Kaṯīr reads it with gemination of the nūn (i.e., hāḏānni), while the rest read it without gemination (i.e., hāḏāni).

footnotes.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr disagrees with the rasm هذن here.

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads fa-ǧmaʿū with ʾalif al-waṣl and fatḥah on the mīm. The rest read it with ʾalif al-qaṭʿ and kasrah on the mīm (i.e., fa-ʾaǧmiʿū).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Ibn Ḏakwān reads tuḫayyalu ʾilayhi with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yuḫayyalu).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Ibn Ḏakwān reads talaqqafu mā with rafʿ of the fāʾ and the rest with ǧazm (i.e., talaqqaf). The manner of al-Bazzī with the gemination of tāʾ (i.e., mâ ttalaqqaf) in al-Baqarah,[182] and the manner of Ḥafṣ with the lack of vowel on the lām and the lack of gemination of the qāf (has also preceded) (i.e., talqaf).[183] Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read kaydu siḥrin with kasrah on the sīn and no vowel on the ḥāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the sīn and with ʾalif after it, and with kasrah on the ḥāʾ (i.e., sāḥirin).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Qunbul and Ḥafṣ read ʾāmantum(ū) lahū as an indicative and the rest as an interrogative (i.e., ʾa-ʾāmantum, ʾa-.āmantum(ū), etc.) and it has already preceded.[184]

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Qālūn, with some disagreement, reads wa-man yaʾtihi muʾminan with shortened realisation of the kasrah on the hāʾ in connected speech. ʾAbū Šuʿayb [al-Sūsī] reads it with no vowel (i.e., yātih) and the rest with full pronunciation (i.e., yaʾ/ātihī).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads lā taḫaf darakan with ǧazm of the fāʾ and the rest apply rafʿ to it with an ʾalif before it (i.e., lā taḫāfu darakan).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read qad ʾanǧaytukum min ʿaduwwikum wa-wāʿattukum, mā razaqtukum (Q20:81) with a tāʾ that carries a ḍammah on all three words. The rest read it with a nūn that carries a fatḥah and with ʾalif after it (i.e., ʾanǧaynākum(ū), wa-wāʿadnākum(ū), mā razaqnākum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads fa-yaḥulla ʿalaykum with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and wa-man yaḥlul with ḍammah on the first lām. The rest read them with kasrah on the ḥāʾ and lām (i.e., yaḥilla, yaḥlil). There is no disagreement regarding the kasrah on the ḥāʾ of His speech ʾan yaḥilla ʿalaykum (Q81:86); it is the third word (of this type that occurs).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and ʿĀsim read bi-malkinā with fatḥah on the mīm. Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read it with ḍammah (i.e., bi-mulkinā). The rest read it with kasrah (i.e., bi-milkinā). The two of the holy cities, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read ḥummilnā with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and kasrah on the geminated mīm. The rest read it with fatḥah on both and without gemination (i.e., ḥamalnā).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: ya-bna-ʾumma/i has already been mentioned.[185]

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read bi-mā lam tabṣurū with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yabṣurū).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read lan yuḫlifahū with kasrah on the lām and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., yuḫlafahū).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads yawma nanfuḫu with a nūn that carries a fatḥah and with ḍammah on the fāʾ. The rest read it with a yāʾ that carries a ḍammah and with fatḥah on the fāʾ (i.e., yunfaḫu).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads fa-lā yaḫaf ḏ̣ulman with ǧazm of the fāʾ. The rest read it with rafʿ and with an ʾalif before it (i.e., yaḫāfu).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū Bakr read wa-ʾinnaka lā with kasrah on the hamzah and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., wa-ʾannaka).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr and al-Kisāʾī read la-ʿallaka turḍā/ē with ḍammah on the tāʾ and the rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., tarḍā/ǟ/ē).

statements.heading: F.20. Sūrat Ṭā-Hā
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ read ʾa-wa-lam taʾ/ātihim with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaʾtihim(ū)). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī apply ʾimālah to the ends of the verses of this sūrah, from His speech li-tašqē (Q20:2) up to the end wa-man ihtadē (Q20:135). ʾAbū ʿAmr applies ʾimālah to all of that only for those that have rāʾ, such as aṯ-ṯarē (Q20:6), man iftarē (Q20:61), lā taʿrē (Q20:118) and what is like it. Whatever remains, he pronounces in between (the two sounds) (e.g., taḍḥǟ, Q20:119). Warš pronounces all of these in between (i.e., aṯ-ṯarǟ, man iftarǟ, taḍḥǟ, etc.). The rest pronounces them with a pure fatḥah sound for all (i.e., aṯ-ṯarā, man iftarā, taḍḥā, etc.). That is what we have explained in the chapter on ʾimālah.[186]

statements.heading: F.20.1. [Yāʾs of Q20]
statements.text: Its yāʾs are 13: 1. ʾinniya ʾānastu (Q20:10), 2. ʾi/anniya ʾana rabbuka (Q20:12) and 3. ʾinnaniya ʾana ḷḷāhu (Q20:14) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 4. laʿallī ʾātā/ēkum (Q20:10) with no vowel by the Kufans. 5. la-ḏikriya // ʾinna (Q20:14–15), 6. wa-yassir liya ʾamrī (Q20:26), 7. wa-ʿalā ʿayniya // ʾiḏ (Q20:39–40) and 8. wa-lā bi-raʾ/āsiya ʾinnī (Q20:94) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 9. wa-liya fīhā (Q20:18) with fatḥah by Warš and Ḥafṣ. 10. ʾaḫiya // šdud (Q20:30–31) with fatḥah by Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 11. li-nafsì // ḏhab (Q20:41–42) and 12. fī ḏikrì // ḏhabā (Q20:42–43) with no vowel by the Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir. They drop the (yāʾ) from the word here due to the meeting of two unvowelled letters (analysed as |ḏikriy ḏhab|). 13. lima ḥašartaniya ʾaʿmā/ǟ (Q20:125) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities.

statements.heading: F.20.2. [Removed yāʾ of Q20]
statements.text: There is a removed one: ʾallā tattabiʿanī ʾa-fa-ʿaṣayta (Q20:93)[187] with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech and pause, with no vowel by Ibn Kaṯīr. Likewise, with retention (of the yāʾ) and no vowel, but only in connected speech by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr.

footnotes.text: Pretzl edition has اগজ تتبعوᆇي افعصيت. This is incorrect and was corrected by al-Ḍāmin (al-Dānī 2008a, 52).

statements.heading: F.21. Sūrat al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read qāla rabbī yaʿlamu with ʾalif and the rest without ʾalif (i.e., qul).

statements.heading: F.21. Sūrat al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ
statements.text: nūḥī/yūḥā/ǟ/ē ʾilayhu/im(ū) has already been mentioned.[188]

statements.heading: F.21. Sūrat al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read the second case of nūḥī ʾilayhi with nūn and with kasrah on the ḥāʾ. The rest read it with yāʾ and fatḥah on the ḥāʾ (i.e., yūḥā/ǟ).

statements.heading: F.21. Sūrat al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads ʾa-lam tara llaḏīna kafarū without wāw after the hamzah and the rest with wāw (i.e., ʾa-wa-lam).[189]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 146).

statements.heading: F.21. Sūrat al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads wa-lā tusmiʿu with a tāʾ that carries a ḍammah and with kasrah on the mīm, and aṣ-ṣumma with naṣb. The rest read it with a yāʾ that carries a fatḥah and with fatḥah on the mīm, and aṣ-ṣummu with rafʿ (i.e., wa-lā tasmaʿu ṣ-ṣummu).

statements.heading: F.21. Sūrat al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads miṯqālu ḥabbatin here and in Luqmān (Q31:16) with rafʿ of the lām. The rest read them with naṣb (i.e., miṯqāla).

statements.heading: F.21. Sūrat al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ
statements.text: wa-ḍiy/ʾāʾan has already been mentioned.[190]

statements.heading: F.21. Sūrat al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads ǧiḏāḏan with kasrah on the ǧīm and the rest with ḍammah (i.e., ǧuḏāḏan).

statements.heading: F.21. Sūrat al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ
statements.text: ʾuffu/i/a(n) lakum(ū)[191] and ʾā̆ʾ/.immah (Q67:77)[192] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.21. Sūrat al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read li-tuḥṣinakum with tāʾ and ʾAbū Bakr with nūn (i.e., li-nuḥṣinakum). The rest read it with yāʾ (i.e., li-yuḥṣinakum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.21. Sūrat al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū Bakr read nuǧǧì l-muʾminīna with a single nūn and gemination. The rest read it with two nūns without gemination (i.e., nunǧī).

statements.heading: F.21. Sūrat al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-ḥirmun with kasrah on the ḥāʾ and no vowel on the rāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on both (consonants) and with ʾalif after the rāʾ (i.e., ḥarāmun).

statements.heading: F.21. Sūrat al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ
statements.text: ʾiḏā fut(t)iḥat[193] and yaʾ/āǧūǧu wa-maʾ/āǧūǧu[194] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.21. Sūrat al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read li-l-kutubi in the plural and the rest read it in the singular (i.e., li-l-kitābi).

statements.heading: F.21. Sūrat al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ
statements.text: fì z-za/ubūri has already been mentioned.[195]

statements.heading: F.21. Sūrat al-ʾAnbiʾāʾ
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads qāla rabbì ḥkum with ʾalif and the rest without ʾalif (i.e., qul).

statements.heading: F.21.1. [Yāʾs of Q21]
statements.text: There are four yāʾs: 1. man maʿiya (Q21:24) with fatḥah by Ḥafṣ. 2. ʾinniya ʾilāhin (Q21:29) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 3. massanì ḍ-ḍurru (Q21:83) and 4. ʿibādì ṣ-ṣāliḥūna (Q21:105) with no vowel by ḥamzah.

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
