statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read sakrē wa-mā hum bi-sakrē without ʾalif, for both words, in the pattern faʿlā and the rest read it with ʾalif in the pattern fuʿālā (i.e., sukārā/ǟ/ē).

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: li-yaḍilla/li-yuḍilla has already been mentioned.[196]

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: Warš, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read ṯumma li-yaqṭaʿ with kasrah on the lām. Warš, Qunbul, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read ṯumma li-yaqḍū (Q22:29) with kasrah on the lām. Ibn Ḏakwān reads wa-li-yūfū (Q22:29) and wa-li-yaṭṭawwafū (Q22:29) with kasrah on the lām of both. The rest read it with no vowel on the lām of all four (i.e., ṯumma l-yaqṭaʿ, ṯumma lyaqḍū, wa-l-yūfū/wa-l-yuwaffū, wa-l-yaṭṭawwafū).

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: hāḏān(n)i has already been mentioned.[197]

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim read luʾluʾan here and in Fāṭir (Q35:33) with naṣb. The rest read it with ḫafḍ (i.e., luʾluʾin). ʾAbū Bakr and ʾAbū ʿAmr—when the latter softens the hamzah—remove the first hamzah of lūluʾun, al-lūluʾu and lūluʾan/in in the whole Qurʾān. When Ḥamzah pauses, he softens both hamzahs in accordance with his principle (i.e., lūlū#, al-lūlū#). Hišām softens the second (hamzah) of these that are not naṣb (in pause), also in accordance with his principle (i.e., luʾlū# but luʾluʾā#). The rest fully pronounced both (i.e., luʾluʾ#, etc.).

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads li-n-nāsi sawāʾan with naṣb and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., sawāʾun).

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads wa-l-yuwaffū with fatḥah on the wāw and gemination of the fāʾ. The rest read it with no vowel on the wāw and no gemination (i.e., wa-l(i)-yūfū).

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads fa-taḫaṭṭafuhū with fatḥah on the ḫāʾ and gemination of the ṭāʾ. The rest read it with no vowel on the ḫāʾ and without gemination of the ṭāʾ (i.e., fa-taḫṭafuhū).

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read mansikan in two places (here and Q22:67) with kasrah on the sīn. The rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., mansakan).

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read ʾinna ḷḷāha yadfaʿu with fatḥah on the yāʾ and fāʾ, and with no vowel on the dāl and without ʾalif. The rest read it with ḍammah on the yāʾ, fatḥah on the dāl, with an ʾalif after it and with kasrah on the fāʾ (i.e., yudāfiʿu).

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and ʾAbū ʿAmr read ʾuḏina llaḏīna with ḍammah on the hamzah and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., ʾaḏina). Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read yuqātalūna with fatḥah on the tāʾ and the rest with kasrah (i.e., yuqātilūna).

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: wa-lawlā dafʿu/diʿāfu ḷḷāhi has already been mentioned.[198] The two of the holy cities read la-hudimat ṣawāmiʿu with no gemination on the dāl and the rest read it with gemination (i.e., la-huddimat). The tāʾ was assimilated to the ṣād here by Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ibn Ḏakwān (i.e., la-huddimaṣ⸗ṣawāmiʿu).

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads ʾahlaktuhā with a tāʾ that carries a ḍammah and the rest read it with a nūn that carries a fatḥah with ʾalif after it (i.e., ʾahlaknāhā).

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read mimmā yaʿuddūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taʿuddūna).

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read muʿaǧǧizīna here and in two places in Sabaʾ (Q34:5, 38) with gemination of the ǧīm without ʾalif. The rest read it with ʾalif without gemination of the ǧīm (i.e., muʿāǧizīna).

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: ṯumma qut(t)ilū[199] and mu/adḫalan (Q22:59)[200] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: The two of the holy cities, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū Bakr read wa-ʾinna mā tadʿūna here and in Luqmān (Q31:30) with tāʾ. The rest read it with yāʾ (i.e., yadʿūna).

statements.heading: F.22. Sūrat al-Ḥaǧǧ
statements.text: mansa/ikan has already been mentioned.[201]

statements.heading: F.22.1. [Yāʾ of Q22]
statements.text: There is one yāʾ: baytiya li-ṭ-ṭāʾifīna (Q22:26) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ, Ḥafṣ and Hišām.

statements.heading: F.22.2. [Removed yāʾs of Q22]
statements.text: There are two removed ones: 1. al-bādī wa-man (Q22:25) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr and retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Warš and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 2. kāna nakīrī (Q22:44) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech whenever it occurs (Q34:45; Q35:26; Q67:18) by Warš.

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads li-ʾamānatihimū here and in al-Maʿāriǧ (Q70:32) without ʾalif as a singular, and the rest read it with ʾalif in the plural (i.e., li-ʾamānātihim).

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr and Ibn ʿĀmir read ʿaḏ̣man fa-kasawnà l-ʿaḏ̣ma with fatḥah on the ʿayn and with no vowel on the ḏ̣āʾ of both words. The rest read it with kasrah on the ʿayn, and fatḥah on the ḏ̣āʾ and with ʾalif after it (i.e., ʿiḏ̣āman, al-ʿiḏ̣āma).

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read saynāʾa with fatḥah on the sīn and the rest with kasrah (i.e., sīnāʾa). Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read tunbitu bi-d-duhn with ḍammah on the tāʾ and kasrah on the bāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the tāʾ and ḍammah on the bāʾ (i.e., tanbutu).

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: na/usqīkum(ū),[202] min ʾilāhin ġayrihī/ġayruhū (Q23:23, 32)[203] and min kulli(n) zawǧayni (Q23:27)[204] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads manzilan with fatḥah on the mīm and kasrah on the zāy. The rest read it with ḍammah on the mīm and fatḥah on the zāy (i.e., munzalan).

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: hayhāt/h# hayhāt/h# has already been mentioned.[205]

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read tatran with tanwīn and when they pause with ʾalif replacing it (i.e., tatrā#). The rest read it without tanwīn and treat the rāʾ according to their principles (that is, whether they apply ʾimālah or not)[206] (i.e., tatrā/ē/ǟ).

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: ʾilā ra/ubwati has already been mentioned.[207]

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: The Kufans read wa-ʾinna hāḏihī with kasrah on the hamzah and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., wa-ʾanna). Ibn ʿĀmir reads it without gemination of the nūn (i.e., wa-ʾan) and the rest with gemination (i.e., wa-ʾinna/ʾanna).

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads tuhǧirūna with ḍammah on the tāʾ and kasrah on the ǧīm. The rest read it with fatḥah on the tāʾ and ḍammah on the ǧīm (i.e.tahǧurūna).

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: ʾam tasʾaluhum(ū) ḫar(ā)ǧan has already been mentioned.[208] Ibn ʿĀmir reads fa-ḫarǧu rabbika with no vowel on the rāʾ and without ʾalif. The rest read it with fatḥah and ʾalif (i.e., fa-ḫarāǧu).

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads sa-yaqūlūna ḷḷāhu in the two latter phrases with ʾalif (al-waṣl) and rafʿ of the hāʾ. The rest read it without ʾalif (al-waṣl), with kasrah on the lām and with ǧarr of the hāʾ (i.e., sa-yaqūlūna li-llāhi) and there is no disagreement on the first phrase (Q23:85, all read it as sa-yaqūlūna li-llāhi).[209]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 141).

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ read ʿālimi l-ġaybi with ḫafḍ of the mīm and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., ʿālimu l-ġaybi).

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read šaqāwatunā with ʾalif along with fatḥah on the šīn and qāf. The rest read it with kasrah on the šīn with no vowel on the qāf without ʾalif (i.e., šiqwatunā).

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read suḫriyyan here and in Ṣād (Q38:63) with ḍammah on the sīn. The rest read it with kasrah (i.e., siḫriyyan), and there is no disagreement in al-Zuḫruf (Q43:32, all read it as suḫriyyan).

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾinnahum hum with kasrah on the hamzah and the rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., ʾannahum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read qul kam labiṯtumū/labittum without ʾalif, and Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read qul ʾin labittum (Q23:114) without ʾalif. The rest read both with ʾalif (i.e., qāla).[210]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 147).

statements.heading: F.23. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read lā tarǧiʿūna with fatḥah on the tāʾ and kasrah on the ǧīm. The rest read it with ḍammah on the tāʾ and fatḥah on the ǧīm (i.e., turǧaʿūna).

statements.heading: F.23.1. [Yāʾ of Q23]
statements.text: There is one yāʾ: laʿallī ʾaʿmalu (Q23:100) with no vowel by the Kufans.

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read wa-farraḍnāhā with gemination of the rāʾ and the rest read it without gemination (i.e., wa-faraḍnāhā).

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads bihimā raʾafatun here with vocalisation of the hamzah and the rest read it without a vowel. There is no disagreement on the one that occurs in al-Ḥadīd (Q57:27, read by all as raʾ/āfatan).

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: al-muḥṣa/ināt has already been mentioned.[211]

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾarbaʿu šahādātin with rafʿ of the ʿayn at the first attestation, and the rest with naṣb (i.e., ʾarbaʿa šahādātin). There is no disagreement on the second attestation (Q24:8, all read ʾarbaʿa šahādātin).

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads wa-l-ḫāmisata ʾanna ġaḍaba ḷḷāhi with naṣb of the tāʾ and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., wa-l-ḫāmisatu). There is no disagreement on the first occurrence (Q24:7, all read wa-lḫāmisatu). Nāfiʿ reads ʾan laʿnatu ḷḷāhi (Q24:7) and ʾan ġaḍiba ḷḷāhu without gemination of the nūn of both, with rafʿ of the tāʾ, with kasrah on the ḍād of ġaḍiba and rafʿ of the hāʾ of the name of God Almighty. The rest read it with gemination of the nūn, naṣb of the tāʾ, fatḥah on the ḍād and ǧarr of the hāʾ (i.e., ʾanna laʿnata ḷḷāhi, ʾanna ġaḍaba ḷḷāhi).

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: ḫuṭ(u)wāt has already been mentioned.[212]

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read yawma yašhadu with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tašhadu).

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Hišām read ʿalā ǧuyūbihinna with ḍammah on the ǧīm and the rest with kasrah (i.e., ǧiyūbihinna). ʾAbū Bakr and Ibn ʿĀmir read ġayra ʾulì l-ʾirbati with naṣb of the rāʾ and the rest with ǧarr (i.e., ġayri). Ibn ʿĀmir reads ʾayyuhu l-muʾminūna, in al-Zuḫruf yā ʾayyuhu s-sāḥiru (Q43:49) and in al-Raḥmān ʾayyuhu ṯ-ṯaqalāni (Q55:31) with ḍammah on the hāʾ in connected speech for all three. The rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., ʾayyuha, yā ʾayyuha). ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī paused on these as ʾayyuhā# with ʾalif.[213] The rest paused on it without ʾalif (i.e., ʾayyuh#).

footnotes.text: This is in conflict with the rasm ايه.

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾāyātin mubayyinātin in two places, here and in al-Ṭalāq (Q65:11), with kasrah on the yāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., mubayyanātin).

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read dirrīʾun with kasrah on the dāl and length and hamzah. ʾAbū Bakr and Ḥamzah read it with ḍammah and hamzah (i.e., durrīʾun). When he pauses, Ḥamzah softens the hamzah in accordance with his principle (i.e., durriyy#).[214] The rest read it with ḍammah on the dāl and gemination of the yāʾ without hamzah (i.e., durriyyun). Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read tawaqqada with a tāʾ that carries a fatḥah, with fatḥah on the wāw and the dāl, and with geminated qāf. ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read it with a tāʾ that carries a ḍammah, no vowel on the wāw and ḍammah on the dāl without gemination (i.e., tūqadu). The rest read it like that too but with yāʾ (i.e., yūqadu).

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū Bakr read yusabbaḥu lahū with fatḥah on the bāʾ. The rest read it with kasrah (i.e., yusabbiḥu).

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: Al-Bazzī reads saḥābu without tanwīn and the rest with tanwīn (i.e., saḥābun). Ibn Kaṯīr reads ḏ̣ulumātin with ḫafḍ and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., ḏ̣ulumātun).

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: ḫāliqu/a kulli dābbatin has already been mentioned.[215]

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḫallād, with some disagreement, read wa-yattaqih with no vowel on the hāʾ. Qālūn reads it with shortened kasrah (i.e., wa-yattaqihi). The rest read it with ṣilah, i.e., wa-yattaqihī. Ḥafṣ reads wa-yattaqhi with no vowel on the qāf and with a shortened kasrah on the hāʾ. The rest read it with kasrah on the hāʾ. In pause, all agree on no vowel of the hāʾ (i.e., wa-yattaq(i)h#).

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads kamà stuḫlifa with ḍammah on the tāʾ and kasrah on the lām. When starting (on this word), he reads it with ḍammah on the ʾalif (i.e., #ʾustuḫlifa). The rest read it with two fatḥahs (i.e., kamà staḫlafa) and, when starting (on this word), with kasrah on the ʾalif (i.e., #ʾistaḫlafa). Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū Bakr read wa-li-yubdilannahum(ū) and the rest with gemination (i.e., wa-li-yubaddilannahum).

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamzah read lā yaḥsabanna llaḏīna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taḥsa/ibanna).

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ṯalāṯa ʿawrātin[216] with naṣb and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., ṯalāṯu).

footnotes.text: Pretzl has  ৫৹ّٰت here. This is a mistake (al-Dānī 2008a, 55).

statements.heading: F.24. Sūrat al-Nūr
statements.text: ʾaw bi/uyūtu[217] ʾi/umma/ihātikum(ū)[218] has already been mentioned. There are no yāʾs at all.

statements.heading: F.25. Sūrat al-Furqān
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read naʾkulu minhā with nūn and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaʾ/ākulu).

statements.heading: F.25. Sūrat al-Furqān
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū Bakr read wa-yaǧʿalu with rafʿ of the lām and the rest read it with ǧazm (i.e., wa-yaǧʿal).

statements.heading: F.25. Sūrat al-Furqān
statements.text: ḍiʾ/yāʾa has already been mentioned.[219]

statements.heading: F.25. Sūrat al-Furqān
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and Ḥafṣ read wa-yawma yaḥšuruhum(ū) with yāʾ and the rest with nūn (i.e., naḥšuruhum). Ibn ʿĀmir reads fa-naqūlu ʾā̆ʾ/.antum with nūn and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., fa-yaqūlu).

statements.heading: F.25. Sūrat al-Furqān
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads fa-mā tastaṭīʿūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yastaṭīʿūna).

statements.heading: F.25. Sūrat al-Furqān
statements.text: The Kufans and ʾAbū ʿAmr read wa-yawma tašaqqaqu here and in Qāf (Q50:44) without gemination of the šīn. The rest read it with gemination (i.e., taššaqqaqu). Ibn Kaṯīr reads nunzilu with two nūns, the second without vowel, without gemination of the zāy and with rafʿ of the lām, and al-malāʾikata with naṣb. The rest read it with one nūn, gemination of the zāy and fatḥah on the lām, and with rafʿ of al-malāʾikatu (i.e., nuzzila lmalāʾikatu).[220]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 147).

statements.heading: F.25. Sūrat al-Furqān
statements.text: ṯamūda(n)[221] and ar-rīḥ/ar-riyāḥ (Q25:48),[222] nuš(u)ran/bušran (Q25:48),[223] li-yaḏḏakkarū/li-yaḏkuru (Q25:50)[224] have already been mentioned before.

statements.heading: F.25. Sūrat al-Furqān
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read limā yaʾmurunā with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taʾ/āmurunā).

statements.heading: F.25. Sūrat al-Furqān
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read fīhā suruǧan with two ḍammahs. The rest read it with kasrah on the sīn, fatḥah on the rāʾ and an ʾalif after it (i.e., sirāǧan).

statements.heading: F.25. Sūrat al-Furqān
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads ʾan yaḏkura with no vowel on the dāl and ḍammah on the ungeminated kāf. The rest read it with both fatḥah and gemination (i.e., yaḏḏakkara).

statements.heading: F.25. Sūrat al-Furqān
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read wa-lam yuqtirū with ḍammah on the yāʾ and kasrah on the tāʾ. Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū ʿAmr read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ and kasrah on the tāʾ (i.e., yaqtirū). The rest read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ and ḍammah on the tāʾ (i.e., yaqturū).

statements.heading: F.25. Sūrat al-Furqān
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū Bakr read yuḍāʿafu/yuḍaʿʿafu and wa-yaḫludu with rafʿ of the fāʾ and the dāl. The rest read them with ǧazm of both (i.e., yuḍāʿaf/yuḍaʿʿaf and wa-yaḫlud). Ibn Kaṯīr and Ibn ʿĀmir, in accordance with their general principle, removed the ʾalif and applied gemination to the ʿayn (i.e., yuḍaʿʿaf(u)). Ibn Kaṯīr and Ḥafṣ read fīhī muhānan with addition of the yāʾ to the hāʾ (for Ḥafṣ) only here (and Ibn Kaṯīr always does so). The rest read it with a shortened kasrah (i.e., fīhi).

statements.heading: F.25. Sūrat al-Furqān
statements.text: The two of the holy cities, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read wa-ḏuriyyātinā in the plural and the rest read it without ʾalif, in the singular (i.e., wa-ḏuriyyatinā).

statements.heading: F.25. Sūrat al-Furqān
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-yalqūna fīhā with fatḥah on the yāʾ and no vowel on an ungeminated lām. The rest read it with ḍammah on the yāʾ and fatḥah on a geminated lām (i.e., yulaqqūna).

statements.heading: F.25.1. [Yāʾs of Q25]
statements.text: There are two yāʾs: 1. yā laytaniya ttaḫattu (Q25:27) with fatḥah by ʾAbū ʿAmr. 2. ʾinna qawmiya ttaḫaḏū (Q25:30) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ, ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Bazzī.

statements.heading: F.26. Sūrat al-Šuʿarāʾ
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ṭē-sīn-mīm here and at the beginning of al-Qaṣaṣ (Q28), and ṭē-sīn at the beginning of al-Naml (Q27) with ʾimālah of the fatḥah of the ṭāʾ. The rest read them with pure pronunciation of the fatḥah (i.e., ṭā-sīn(-mīm)). Ḥamzah does not assimilate the nūn of the letter sīn to the mīm here and in al-Qaṣaṣ (i.e., ṭē-sīn-mim); the rest assimilate it (i.e., ṭē/ā-sīm⸗mīm).

statements.heading: F.26. Sūrat al-Šuʿarāʾ
statements.text: ʾarǧi(ʾ)h(i/u),[225] qāla naʿa/im (Q26:42),[226] talqaf/talaqqaf (Q26:45),[227] ʾā/amantum(ū) (Q26:49),[228] ʾan (ʾa)sri (Q26:52)[229] and wa-ʿu/iyūn (Q26:57)[230] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.26. Sūrat al-Šuʿarāʾ
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn Ḏakwān read ḥāḏirūna with ʾalif and the rest without ʾalif (i.e., ḥaḏirūna).

statements.heading: F.26. Sūrat al-Šuʿarāʾ
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads fa-lammā tarēʾà l-ǧamʿāni with ʾimālah of the fatḥah of the rāʾ in connected speech. When he pauses, the hamzah follows it (the rāʾ in terms of ʾimālah), so ʾimālah is applied to it and it is turned into a (hamzah) bayna bayn in accordance with his principle. So, it comes in between two ʾalifs that have undergone ʾimālah, the first being because of the ʾimālah of the fatḥah of the rāʾ and the second because of the ʾimālah of the fatḥah of the hamzah (i.e., tarē.ē#). This is what oral transmission determines, but this is in fact in accordance with his general principles.[231] The rest read it with pure pronunciation of the fatḥah on the rāʾ in connected speech (i.e., tarāʾà l-ǧamʿāni). Al-Kisāʾī pauses with ʾimālah on the fatḥah on the hamzah (i.e., tarāʾē#), so he applies ʾimālah to the ʾalif after it which is a replacement of the yāʾ because of its ʾimālah. Warš makes it in between (the two sounds) according to his general principle of the stem-final yāʾs (i.e., tarāʾǟ#). The rest pause on the fatḥah (i.e., tarāʾā#).

statements.heading: F.26. Sūrat al-Šuʿarāʾ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read ʾillā ḫalqa l-ʾawwalīna with fatḥah on the ḫāʾ and no vowel on the lām. The rest read both (letters) with ḍammah (i.e., ḫuluqa).

statements.heading: F.26. Sūrat al-Šuʿarāʾ
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read fārihīna with ʾalif and the rest without ʾalif (i.e., farihīna).

statements.heading: F.26. Sūrat al-Šuʿarāʾ
statements.text: The two of the holy cities and Ibn ʿĀmir read ʾaṣḥābu laykata here and in Ṣād (Q38:13) with a lām that carries a fatḥah, no hamzah after it, no ʾalif (al-waṣl) before it and fatḥah on the tāʾ. The rest read it with ʾalif (al-waṣl), lām with hamzah and ḫafḍ of the tāʾ (i.e., ʾaṣḥābu l-(ʾ)aykati). The one that occurs in al-Ḥiǧr (Q15:78) and in Qāf (Q50:14) are read with a unanimous interpretation (i.e., as ʾaṣḥābu l-ʾaykati),[232] with the exception that Warš transposes the vowel of the hamzah of both onto the lām in accordance with his general principle (i.e., ʾaṣḥābu l‿aykati).[233]

footnotes.text: The difference between these two pairs of verses stems from a difference in the rasm. Q26:176 and Q38:13 are spelled اඞචب ليჀ჎ whereas the ones at Q15:78 and Q50:14 are spelled اඞචب اগজيჀ჎. In the latter case, then, it is not possible to read the lām as anything other than being part of the definite article.

statements.heading: F.26. Sūrat al-Šuʿarāʾ
statements.text: bi-l-qu/isṭāsi has already been mentioned.[234]

statements.heading: F.26. Sūrat al-Šuʿarāʾ
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads kasafan here and in Sabaʾ (Q34:9) with fatḥah on the sīn and the rest without a vowel (i.e., kasfan).

statements.heading: F.26. Sūrat al-Šuʿarāʾ
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah, ʾAbū Bakr and al-Kisāʾī read nazzala bihī with gemination of the zāy and ar-rūḥa l-ʾamīna with naṣb of both (words). The rest read it without gemination of the zāy and with rafʿ (i.e., nazala bihi r-rūḥu l-(ʾ)amīnu).

statements.heading: F.26. Sūrat al-Šuʿarāʾ
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads ʾa-wa-lam takun with tāʾ and lahum ʾāyatun with rafʿ. The rest read it with yāʾ and naṣb (i.e., ʾa-wa-lam yakun lahum(ū) ʾāyatan).

statements.heading: F.26. Sūrat al-Šuʿarāʾ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read fa-tawakkal with fāʾ and the rest with wāw (i.e., wa-tawakkal).[235]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 141).

statements.heading: F.26. Sūrat al-Šuʿarāʾ
statements.text: yatbaʿuhumu/yattabiʿuhumu l-ġāwūna has already been mentioned.[236]

statements.heading: F.26.1. [Yāʾs of Q26]
statements.text: There are 13 yāʾs: 1. ʾinniya ʾaḫāfu (Q26:12), 2. ʾinniya ʾaḫāfu (Q26:135) and 3. rabbiya ʾaʿlamu (Q26:188) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 4. bi-ʿibādiya ʾinnakum (Q26:52) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ. 5. ʾinna maʿiya rabbī (Q26:62) with fatḥah by Ḥafṣ. 6. liya ʾillā rabba (Q26:77) and 7. li-ʾabiya ʾinnahū (Q26:86) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 8. wa-man maʿiya (Q26:118) with fatḥah by Warš and Ḥafṣ. 9. ʾin ʾaǧriya ʾillā in five places (Q26:109; 10. Q26:127; 11. Q26:145; 12. Q26:164; 13. Q26:180) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ.

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: The Kufans read bi-šihābin with tanwīn and the rest without tanwīn (i.e., bi-šihābi).

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads ʾaw la-yaʾtiyannanī with two nūns, the first with fatḥah and gemination. The rest read it with a single geminated nūn carrying a kasrah (i.e., la-yaʾ/ātiyannī).[237]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 147).

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: ʿĀṣim reads fa-makaṯa with fatḥah on the kāf and the rest with ḍammah (i.e., fa-makuṯa). Al-Bazzī and ʾAbū ʿAmr read min sabaʾa here and in Sabaʾ (Q34:15) with fatḥah on the hamzah of both without tanwīn. Qunbul reads it with no vowel on both as if intending it to be in pause (i.e., min sabaʾ). The rest read it with ḫafḍ of both and with tanwīn (i.e., min sabaʾin).

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads ʾa-lā yà sǧudū without gemination of the lām, he pauses on it as ʾa-lā yā# and starts on #ʾusǧudū as an imperative. It is (to be parsed as) ʾa-lā yā ʾayyuhā n-nāsu sǧudū “verily! O people, prostrate!” The rest read it with gemination of the lām because of the assimilation of the nūn (i.e., ʾallā parsed as ʾan-lā) and they pause on it as a single word (i.e., ʾallā yasǧudū#). Ḥafṣ and al-Kisāʾī read mā tuḫfūna wa-mā tuʿlinūna with tāʾ on both and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yuḫfūna, yuʿlinūna).

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: ʿĀṣim, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥamzah read fa-ʾalqih ʾilayhi/um with no vowel on the hāʾ and Qālūn with short vowel in connected speech (i.e., fa-ʾalqihi). The rest pronounce it fully (i.e., fa-ʾalqihī).

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: ʾana ʾā/ētīka bihī has already been mentioned.[238]

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: Qunbul reads ʿan saʾqayhā, in Ṣād bi-suʾūqin/bi-suʾqin (Q38:33) and in al-Fatḥ ʿalā suʾūqihī/suʾqihī (Q48:29) with hamzah, for all three places. The rest read it without hamzah (i.e., sāqayhā, sūqin, sūqihī).[239]

footnotes.text: Al-Dānī’s description is ambiguous as to whether the plural form should be read suʾq or suʾūq. Both opinions are known. Ibn al-Ǧazarī (2018, §3810) presents the first option first, but also mentions that al-Šāṭibī (who wrote the famous didactic poem based on the Taysīr) transmitted suʾūq. Indeed, on checking the Šāṭibiyyah, both options are mentioned: maʿa s-sūqi sāqayhā wa-sūqi hmizū Zakā. wa-waǧhun bi-hamzin baʿdahu l-wāwu wukkilā “With as-sūqi sāqayhā and sūqi, apply hamzah to it (when reading as) zāy (i.e., Qunbul). An option with hamzah and a wāw after it has been accepted.” (al-Šāṭibī 2010, line 938).

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read la-tubbayyitunnahū and ṯumma la-taqūlunna with tāʾ on both, ḍammah on the second tāʾ [of the first word],[240] and ḍammah on the second lām of the second word. The rest read them with nūn and with fatḥah on the tāʾ and lām (i.e., la-tubayyitannahū, ṯumma la-taqūlanna). mahlika/muhlak ʾahlihī has already been mentioned.[241]

footnotes.text: This emendation is present in one of the manuscripts of Pretzl’s edition and listed in the footnotes. The text as printed in the main text is clearly inferior.

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: The Kufans read ʾannā dammarnāhum with fatḥah on the hamzah and the rest with kasrah (i.e., ʾinnā).

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: qad(d)arnāhā has already been mentioned.[242]

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: ʿĀṣim and ʾAbū ʿAmr read ḫayrun ʾammā yušrikūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tušrikūna).

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr and Hišām read qalīlan mā yaḏḏakkarūna and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taḏ(ḏ)akkarūna).

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read bal ʾadraka with ʾalif al-qaṭʿ, with no vowel on the dāl and without ʾalif. The rest read it with ʾalif al-waṣl, gemination of the dāl and an ʾalif after it (i.e., iddāraka).

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads ʾiḏā kunnā turāban with a hamzah that carries a kasrah as a declarative. The rest read it as an interrogative (i.e., ʾaʾiḏā etc.), and they follow their methods which have already been mentioned.[243] Ibn Kaṯīr and al-Kisāʾī read ʾinnanā la-muḫraǧūna with two nūns as a declarative, and the rest read it with one (nūn) as an interrogative (i.e., ʾaʾinnā, etc.).[244] They follow their methods which have already been mentioned.[245]

footnotes.text: This reading is related to the ambiguity of the undotted rasm اٮٮاwhich can Ibn Kaṯīr and al-Kisāʾī read as انناand the rest as اينا.

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: ar-rīḥ/ar-riyāḥ,[246] nuš(u)ran/bušran[247] and fī ḍayyiqin/ḍayqin (Q27:70)[248] have al-ready been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads wa-lā yasmaʿu with a yāʾ that carries a fatḥah, with fatḥah on the mīm and with rafʿ of aṣ-ṣummu; it is like that in al-Rūm as well (Q30:25). The rest read it with a tāʾ that carries a ḍammah, with kasrah on the mīm (i.e., tusmiʿu) and aṣ-ṣumma with naṣb.

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads wa-mā ʾanta tahdī with a tāʾ that carries a fatḥah and no vowel on the hāʾ in two sūrahs, here and in al-Rūm (Q30:52), and al-ʿumya with naṣb. When he pauses, he retains the yāʾ of both (i.e., tahdī# here and in al-Rūm). The rest read it with a bāʾ that carries a kasrah, with fatḥah on the hāʾ, with an ʾalif after it and al-ʿumyi with ḫafḍ (i.e., bi-hādì l-ʿumyi). They pause on it here with a yāʾ (i.e., bi-hādī#) and in al-Rūm without yāʾ, following the muṣḥaf (i.e., bi-hād#),[249] except for al-Kisāʾī who pauses on both with a yāʾ (bi-hādī# here and in al-Rūm).

footnotes.text: The ʿUṯmānic rasm writes Q27:81 as ቙ኟدى العمىand Q30:52 as ቙ኟد العمى, which gives rise to a difference in pausal rules, following the rasm.

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: The Kufans read ʾanna n-nāsa with fatḥah on the hamzah and the rest with kasrah (i.e., ʾinna).

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: Ḥafṣ and Ḥamzah read wa-kullun ʾatawhu with shortness of the hamzah and with fatḥah on the tāʾ. The rest read it with length of the hamzah and with ḍammah on the tāʾ (i.e., ʾātūhū̆).

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Hišām read ḫabīrun bi-mā yafʿalūna and the rest read it with tāʾ (i.e., tafʿalūna).

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: The Kufans read min fazaʿin with tanwīn and the rest without tanwīn (i.e., fazaʿi). The Kufans and Nāfiʿ read yawmaʾiḏin with fatḥah on the mīm and the rest with kasrah (i.e., yawmiʾiḏīn).

statements.heading: F.27. Sūrat al-Naml
statements.text: ʿammā y/taʿmalūna has already been mentioned.[250]

statements.heading: F.27.1. [Yāʾs of Q27]
statements.text: There are five yāʾs: 1. ʾinniya ʾānastu (Q27:7) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 2. ʾawziʿniya ʾan ʾaškura (Q27:19) with fatḥah by Warš and al-Bazzī. 3. mā liya lā ʾarā/ē (Q27:20) with fatḥah by Ibn Kaṯīr, ʿĀṣim, al-Kisāʾī and Hišām. 4. ʾinniya ʾulqiya (Q27:29) and 5. li-yabluwaniya ʾā(-.a)škuru (Q27:40) with fatḥah on both by Nāfiʿ.

statements.heading: F.27.2. [Removed yāʾs of Q27]
statements.text: There are two removed ones:[251] 1. ʾattumiddūnnī bi-mālin (Q27:36): Ḥamzah reads it with a single geminated nūn and the rest with two clear nūns (ʾattumiddūnanī), with the retention of the yāʾ in connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr and Ḥamzah. Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr retain it in connected speech only. 2. fa-mā ʾātāniya ḷḷāhu (Q27:36) with retention (of the yāʾ) carrying a fatḥah in connected speech and no vowel in pause (i.e., ʾātānī#) by Qālūn, Ḥafṣ and ʾAbū ʿAmr, with some disagreement for all of them, and by that I mean in pause (i.e., some authorities stipulate ʾātān# in pause).[252] It is with fatḥah in connected speech but removal in pause by Warš (i.e., ʾātǟniya ḷḷāhu but ʾātǟn#). The rest remove the yāʾ in connected speech and pause (i.e, ʾātǟnì llāhu and ʾātǟn#). 3. Al-Kisāʾī read wādi n-namli with yāʾ in pause (i.e., wādī#) and the rest without yāʾ (wād#). This has already been mentioned previously.[253]

footnotes.text: Sic, although al-Dānī mentions three cases.
This reading is more in line with the rasm  اتان.

statements.heading: F.28. Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-yarē firʿawnu wa-hāmānu wa-ǧunūduhumā with a yāʾ that carries a fatḥah, with fatḥah on the rāʾ, with ʾimālah of that fatḥah and rafʿ of the three nouns (that follow). The rest read it with a nūn that carries a ḍammah, with kasrah of the rāʾ, fatḥah on the yāʾ and after it naṣb of the three nouns (i.e., wa-nuriya firʿawna wa-hāmāna wa-ǧunūdahumā).

statements.heading: F.28. Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʿaduwwan ḥuznan with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and no vowel on the zāy. The rest read it with fatḥah on both (i.e., ḥazanan).

statements.heading: F.28. Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū ʿAmr read ḥattā yaṣdura. The rest read it with ḍammah on the yāʾ and kasrah on the dāl (i.e., yuṣ/ẓdira).

statements.heading: F.28. Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ
statements.text: yā ʾabat/h#,[254] hātayn(n)i ʿalā ʾan (Q28:27)[255] and li-ʾahlihu/i mkuṯū[256] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.28. Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ
statements.text: ʿĀṣim reads ʾaw ǧaḏwatin with fatḥah on the ǧīm, Ḥamzah with ḍammah (i.e., ǧuḏwatin) and the rest with kasrah (i.e., ǧiḏwatin).

statements.heading: F.28. Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads min ar-rahbi with fatḥah on the rāʾ and no vowel on the hāʾ. The two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr read it with fatḥah on both (i.e., ar-rahabi). The rest read it with ḍammah on the rāʾ and no vowel on the hāʾ (i.e., ar-ruhbi). Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read fa-ḏānnika with gemination of the nūn and the rest without gemination (i.e., fa-ḏānika).

statements.heading: F.28. Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads maʿī ridan with fatḥah on the dāl without hamzah. The rest read it with no vowel on the dāl and with hamzah (i.e., ridʾan). Ḥamzah reads it in accordance with his manner in pause (i.e., ridʾan but ridā#).[257] ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read yuṣaddiqunī with rafʿ of the qāf and the rest with ǧazm (i.e., yuṣaddiqnī).

statements.heading: F.28. Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads qāla mūsā without wāw and the rest wa-qāla with wāw.[258] wa-man y/takūnu lahū has already been mentioned.[259]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 147).

statements.heading: F.28. Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾilaynā lā yarǧiʿūna with fatḥah on the yāʾ and kasrah on the ǧīm. The rest read it with ḍammah on the yāʾ and fatḥah on the ǧīm.

statements.heading: F.28. Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ
statements.text: The Kufans read qālū siḥrāni with kasrah on the sīn and no vowel on the ḥāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the sīn with an ʾalif after it and with kasrah on the ḥāʾ (i.e., sāḥirāni).

statements.heading: F.28. Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads tuǧbā/ǟ ʾilayhi with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yuǧbā/ē).

statements.heading: F.28. Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ
statements.text: fī ʾu/immihā rasūlan has already been mentioned.[260]

statements.heading: F.28. Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads ʾa-fa-lā yaʿqilūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taʿqilūna).

statements.heading: F.28. Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ
statements.text: ṯumma h(u)wa[261] and bi-ḍiy/ʾāʾin (Q28:71)[262] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.28. Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ
statements.text: (The manner of) pausing on waykaʾanna ḷḷāha and waykaʾannahū have also been mentioned in its (proper) chapter.[263] Ḥafṣ reads la-ḫasafa binā with fatḥah on the ḫāʾ and sīn. The rest read it with ḍammah on the ḫāʾ and kasrah on the sīn (i.e., la-ḫusifa).

statements.heading: F.28.1. [Yāʾs of Q28]
statements.text: There are 12 yāʾs: 1. rabbiya ʾan yahdiyanī (Q28:22), 2. ʾinniya ʾānastu (Q28:29), 3. ʾinniya ʾana ḷḷāhu (Q28:30), 4. ʾinniya ʾaḫāfu (Q28:34), 5. rabbiya ʾaʿlamu (Q28:37), 6. ʿindiya ʾa-wa-lam (Q28:78) and 7. rabbiya ʾaʿlamu (Q28:85) with fatḥah for all by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. ʾAbū Rabīʿah transmitted from Qunbul[264] and from al-Bazzī that only ʿindī was without vowel (on the yāʾ). 8. ʾinniya ʾurīdu (Q28:27) and 9. sa-taǧiduniya ʾin šāʾa ḷḷāhu (Q28:27) with fatḥah on both by Nāfiʿ. 10. laʿallī ʾātā/ēkum and 11. laʿallī ʾaṭṭaliʿu with no vowel on both by the Kufans. 12. maʿiya ridʾan with fatḥah by Ḥafṣ.

footnotes.text: For al-Bazzī this is the ʾisnād mentioned in the U.4.2., but for Qunbul it is not. This ʾisnād is mentioned in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 306).

statements.heading: F.28.2. [Removed yāʾ of Q28]
statements.text: There is a removed one: ʾan yukaḏḏibūnī qāla (Q28:34) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Warš.

statements.heading: F.29. Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾa-wa-lam taraw kayfa with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaraw).

statements.heading: F.29. Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt
statements.text: [265] Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read an-našāʾata here, in al-Naǧm (Q53:48) and al-Wāqiʿah (Q56:62) with fatḥah on the šīn and ʾalif after it. The rest read it with no vowel on the šīn and without ʾalif (i.e., an-našʾata). Ḥamzah pauses on this word in two manners. The first of these is that he transfers the vowel of the hamzah onto the šīn and then drops it by analogy (i.e., an-našah#). The second option is that he places fatḥah on the šīn and replaces the hamzah with an ʾalif following the written text (i.e., an-našāh#).[266] It has been heard similarly among the Arabs.

footnotes.text: This number is missing in the Pretzl edition.

The rasm of this word is الٮساه. This is an orthographic exception to the rule that post-consonantal hamzah is not written if one reads it as an-našʾah. Ḥamzah’s second option for the pausal reading follows the rasm in pause.

statements.heading: F.29. Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read mawaddatu with rafʿ without tanwīn and baynikum(ū) with ḫafḍ. Ḥafṣ and Ḥamzah read it with naṣb without tanwīn and baynikum with ḫafḍ (i.e., mawaddata baynikum). The rest read it with naṣb and tanwīn, and baynakum(ū) with fatḥah (i.e., mawaddatan baynakum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.29. Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt
statements.text: The two of the holy cities, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read ʾinnakum(ū) la-taʾtūna with the first hamzah carrying a kasrah as a declarative and the rest as an interrogative (i.e., ʾa-ʾinnakum, etc.). They all agreed on the interrogative of the second one (i.e., ʾa-ʾinnakum(ū) at Q29:29) and they followed their general principles for these two words as has been mentioned in Sūrat al-Raʿd.[267]

statements.heading: F.29. Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read la-nunǧiyannahū without gemination. Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾinnā munǧūka (Q29:33) without gemination. The rest read both with gemination (i.e., la-nunaǧǧiyannahū and munaǧǧūka).

statements.heading: F.29. Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt
statements.text: sī/ǖʾa bihim,[268] ʾinnā mun(a)z(z)ilūna (Q29:34)[269] and wa-ṯamūda(n) (Q29:38)[270] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.29. Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt
statements.text: ʿĀṣim and ʾAbū ʿAmr read mā yadʿūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tadʿūna).

statements.heading: F.29. Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾāyatun min rabbihī in the singular and the rest in the plural (i.e., ʾāyātun).

statements.heading: F.29. Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt
statements.text: The Kufans and Nāfiʿ read wa-yaqūlu ḏūqū with yāʾ and the rest with nūn (i.e., naqūlu).

statements.heading: F.29. Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads ʾilaynā yurǧaʿūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., turǧaʿūna).

statements.heading: F.29. Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read la-nuṯwiyannahum with a ṯāʾ that does not carry a vowel and without hamzah. The rest read it with a bāʾ that carries a fatḥah and with hamzah (i.e., la-nubawwiʾannahum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.29. Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Qālūn, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-l-yatamattaʿū with no vowel on the lām and the rest with kasrah (i.e., wa-li-yatamattaʿū).

statements.heading: F.29.1. [Yāʾs of Q29]
statements.text: There are three yāʾs: 1. ʾilā rabbiya ʾinnahū (Q29:26) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 2. yā ʿibādi llaḏīna (Q29:56) with removal (of the yāʾ) by ʾAbū ʿAmr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī in connected speech because it is a vocative. But the rule in their speech is to follow what is written when pausing, therefore retention (of the yāʾ) with no vowel as it is added in all muṣḥafs (i.e., yā ʿibādī#).[271] The rest apply the fatḥah in connected speech and retained the yāʾ with no vowel in pause (i.e., yā ʿibādiya llaḏīna, yā ʿibādī#). 3. ʾinna ʾarḍiya wāṣiʿatun (Q29:56) with fatḥah by Ibn ʿĀmir.

footnotes.text: The word is spelled  ٮعٮادى  اუჸੌںin the rasm, different from, say, Q39:10 where it is spelled ٮعٮاد اუჸੌں.

statements.heading: F.30. Sūrat al-Rūm
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read ṯumma kāna ʿāqibata llaḏīna with naṣb and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., ʿāqibatu).

statements.heading: F.30. Sūrat al-Rūm
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read ṯumma ʾilayhi yurǧaʿūna with yāʾ, and the rest read it with tāʾ (i.e., turǧaʿūna).

statements.heading: F.30. Sūrat al-Rūm
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-ka-ḏālika taḫruǧūna and in al-Ǧāṯiyah (Q45:35) fa-lyawma lā yaḫruǧūna minhā with fatḥah on the tāʾ here and the yāʾ there, and with ḍammah on the rāʾ. Al-Naqqāš, transmitting from al-ʾAḫfaš, said it was like that too but only for the variant here. The rest read it with ḍammah on the yāʾ and tāʾ, and with fatḥah on the rāʾ (i.e., tuḫraǧūna, yuḫraǧūna). There is no disagreement on the second occurrence of this word in this sūrah (Q30:25, all read taḫruǧūna).

statements.heading: F.30. Sūrat al-Rūm
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads li-l-ʿālimīna with kasrah on the lām and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., li-l-ʿālamīna).

statements.heading: F.30. Sūrat al-Rūm
statements.text: fāraqū/farraqū,[272] yaqni/uṭūna (Q30:36),[273] and wa-mā ʾā̆taytum(ū) min rabban (Q30:39)[274] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.30. Sūrat al-Rūm
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads li-turbū with a tāʾ that carries a ḍammah and without vowel on the wāw. The rest read it with a yāʾ that carries a fatḥah and with naṣb of the wāw (i.e., yarbuwa).

statements.heading: F.30. Sūrat al-Rūm
statements.text: ʿammā t/yušrikūna has already been mentioned.[275]

statements.heading: F.30. Sūrat al-Rūm
statements.text: Qunbul reads li-nuḏīqahumū with nūn and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., li-yuḏīqahum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.30. Sūrat al-Rūm
statements.text: yursilu r-rīḥa/r-riyāḥa has already been mentioned.[276] Ibn ʿĀmir, with some disagreement in the transmission of Hišām, reads kasfan with no vowel on the sīn, and the rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., kasafan).

statements.heading: F.30. Sūrat al-Rūm
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾilā ʾāṯāri with ʾalif as a plural, and the rest read it without ʾalif as a singular (i.e., ʾaṯari).

statements.heading: F.30. Sūrat al-Rūm
statements.text: wa-lā yusmiʿu/tasmaʿu ṣ-ṣumma[277] and wa-mā ʾanti yahdi/bi-hādi l-ʿumya/i[278] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.30. Sūrat al-Rūm
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr and Ḥamzah read min ḍaʿfin in all three cases (in this verse) with fatḥah on the ḍād (i.e., ḍaʿfin, ḍaʿfin, ḍaʿfan). This is likewise transmitted by Ḥafṣ transmitting from ʿĀṣim for these, except that he abandoned this practice and chose the ḍammah instead, following a report that al-Fuḍayl b. Marzūq reported from ʿAṭiyyah al-ʿAwfī from ʿAbd Aḷḷāh b. ʿUmar that the Prophet (s) taught to recite that with ḍammah, and he recited it back to him with fatḥ and (the Prophet) rejected it. But ʿAṭiyyah is regarded as weak. What Ḥafṣ transmitting from ʿĀṣim transmitted from his teachers (ḍaʿfin, etc.) is sounder. I adopt both options in his transmission in order to follow ʿĀṣim in his reading and to agree with Ḥafṣ in his preference. The rest read it with ḍammah on the ḍād of all three (i.e., ḍuʿfin, ḍuʿfin, ḍuʿfan).

statements.heading: F.30. Sūrat al-Rūm
statements.text: The Kufans read here lā yanfaʿu llaḏīna with a yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tanfaʿu). There are no yāʾs at all.

statements.heading: F.31. Sūrat Luqmān (s)
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads hudan wa-raḥmatun with rafʿ and the rest with naṣb (i.e., raḥmatan).

statements.heading: F.31. Sūrat Luqmān (s)
statements.text: li-yaḍilla/li-yuḍilla[279] and fī ʾuḏ(u)nayhi[280] have already been mentioned. Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-yattaḫiḏahā with naṣb and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., wa-yattaḫiḏuhā).

statements.heading: F.31. Sūrat Luqmān (s)
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads yā bunay lā tušrik with no vowel on the yāʾ, and that is (only) for the first attestation (in this sūrah). Qunbul reads yā bunay ʾaqim iṣ-ṣalāta (Q31:17) with no vowel on the yāʾ and that is the last one. Ḥafṣ reads both of these and the middle one (Q31:16) with fatḥah on the yāʾ (i.e., yā bunayya), and al-Bazzī does similarly for the last one.[281] The rest read all three with kasrah on the yāʾ (i.e., yā bunayyi).

footnotes.text: Al-Bazzī thus has three different pronunciations for the three:: yā bunay (Q31:13), yā bunayyi (Q31:16) and yā bunayya (Q31:17).

statements.heading: F.31. Sūrat Luqmān (s)
statements.text: miṯqālu ḥibbatin has already been mentioned.[282]

statements.heading: F.31. Sūrat Luqmān (s)
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read wa-lā tuṣaʿʿir ḫaddaka with gemination of the ʿayn and without ʾalif. The rest read it with ʿalif and without gemination of the ʿayn (i.e., tuṣāʿir).

statements.heading: F.31. Sūrat Luqmān (s)
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ read ʿalaykum niʿamahū in the plural and with a masculine (pronoun). The rest read it in the singular and feminine (i.e., niʿmatan).

statements.heading: F.31. Sūrat Luqmān (s)
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads wa-l-baḥra yamudduhū with naṣb of the rāʾ and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., wa-l-baḥru).

statements.heading: F.31. Sūrat Luqmān (s)
statements.text: wa-ʾanna mā y/tadʿūna has already been mentioned.[283]

statements.heading: F.31. Sūrat Luqmān (s)
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read yunazzilu l-ġayṯa here and in al-Šūrā (Q42:28) with gemination. The rest read it without gemination (i.e., yunzilu l-ġayṯa) and that has already been mentioned.[284]

statements.heading: F.32. Sūrat al-Saǧdah
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū ʿAmr read kulla šayʾin ḫalqahū with no vowel on the lām, and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., ḫalaqahū).

statements.heading: F.32. Sūrat al-Saǧdah
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads mā ʾuḫfī lahum with no vowel on the yāʾ and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., ʾuḫfiya).

statements.heading: F.32. Sūrat al-Saǧdah
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read limā ṣabarū with kasrah on the lām and without gemination of the mīm. The rest read it with fatḥah on the lām and gemination of the mīm (i.e., lammā).

statements.heading: F.33. Sūrat al-ʾAḥzāb
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads bi-mā yaʿmalūna ḫabīran and bi-mā yaʿmalūna baṣīran (Q33:9) with yāʾ on both. The rest read it with tāʾ (i.e., taʿmalūna).

statements.heading: F.33. Sūrat al-ʾAḥzāb
statements.text: [285] Qālūn and Qunbul read allāʾi here, in al-Muǧādalah (Q68:2) and al-Ṭalāq (Q65:4) with hamzah and without yāʾ. Warš reads it with a yāʾ carrying an ultrashort kasrah[286] in place of the hamzah (i.e., allā.i).[287] If he pauses on it, he articulates the yāʾ without vowel (i.e., allāy#). Al-Bazzī and ʾAbū ʿAmr read it with a yāʾ not carrying a vowel that replaces the hamzah in connected speech and pause (i.e., allāy(#)). The rest read it with hamzah and with yāʾ after the hamzah in connected speech and pause (i.e., allāʾī). Ḥamzah, however, when he pauses, makes the hamzah pronounced in between in accordance with his general principle[288] (i.e., allā.ī#). Whoever pronounces the hamzah among them or does not pronounce it, they pronounce fully the strength of the ʾalif in connected speech and pause (i.e., allâʾī or allây), except for Warš. For him both an overlong vowel and a vowel of regular length are allowed in his practice (i.e., allâ.i and allā.i), as we have already mentioned in the chapter of two hamzahs.[289] ʿĀṣim reads tuḏ̣āhirūna with ḍammah on the tāʾ, without gemination of the ḏ̣āʾ, with ʾalif after it and with kasrah on the hāʾ. Ibn ʿĀmir reads it with fatḥah on the tāʾ and hāʾ, and with gemination of the ḏ̣āʾ with ʾalif after it (i.e., taḏ̣ḏ̣āharūna). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read it like that except that they did not geminate the ḏ̣āʾ (i.e., taḏ̣āharūna). The rest read it with fatḥah on the tāʾ and gemination of the ḏ̣āʾ and hāʾ without ʾalif (i.e., taḏ̣ḏ̣ahharūna).

footnotes.text: Pretzl erroneously marks this as verse 7 (al-Dānī 2008a, 60).
The literal reading of this description points to allāyĭ. In modern recitation this is understood to be allā.i (described as such by Ibn al-Ǧazarī 2018, §1522).
See U.11.2. While al-Dānī discusses the option of pronouncing the vowel as not overlong in that section, he does not explicitly attribute it to Warš as he seems to do here.

statements.heading: F.33. Sūrat al-ʾAḥzāb
statements.text: Ḥamzah and ʾAbū ʿAmr read aḏ̣-ḏ̣unūna, ar-rasūla (Q33:66) and as-sabīla (Q33:67) with the removal of the ʾalif in connected speech and pause. Ibn Kaṯīr, Ḥafṣ and al-Kisāʾī with removal in connected speech only (i.e., aḏ̣-ḏ̣unūna, aḏ̣-ḏ̣unūnā#; ar-rasūla, ar-rasūlā#; as-sabīla, as-sabīlā#). The rest read it with retention of the ʾalif in connected speech and pause (i.e., aḏ̣-ḏ̣unūnā, aḏ̣-ḏ̣unūnā#; ar-rasūlā, ar-rasūlā#; as-sabīlā, as-sabīlā#).

statements.heading: F.33. Sūrat al-ʾAḥzāb
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads lā muqāma lakum with ḍammah on the (first) mīm and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., maqāma).

statements.heading: F.33. Sūrat al-ʾAḥzāb
statements.text: The two of the holy cities read la-ʾatawhā short, and the rest with length (i.e., la-ʾātawhā).

statements.heading: F.33. Sūrat al-ʾAḥzāb
statements.text: ʿĀṣim reads ʾuswatun here and in two places in al-Mumtaḥanah (Q60:4, 6) with ḍammah on the hamzah. The rest read it with kasrah (i.e., ʾiswatun).

statements.heading: F.33. Sūrat al-ʾAḥzāb
statements.text: ar-ruʿ(u)ba[290] and mubayya/inatin (Q33:30)[291] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.33. Sūrat al-ʾAḥzāb
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read nuḍaʿʿif lahā with nūn, with kasrah on the ʿayn with gemination and without ʾalif, and al-ʿaḏāba with naṣb. The rest read it with yāʾ, fatḥah on the ʿayn and with rafʿ of al-ʿaḏābu. ʾAbū ʿAmr geminated the ʿayn and removed the ʾalif that is before it (i.e., yuḍaʿʿaf lahà l-ʿaḏābu). The rest made it ungeminated and retained the ʾalif (i.e., yuḍāʿaf lahà l-ʿaḏābu).

statements.heading: F.33. Sūrat al-ʾAḥzāb
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-yaʿmal ṣāliḥan yuʾtihā ʾaǧrahā with yāʾ on both. The rest read it with tāʾ on the first and nūn on the second (i.e., wa-taʿmal ṣāliḥan nuʾtihā).

statements.heading: F.33. Sūrat al-ʾAḥzāb
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim read wa-qarna with fatḥah on the qāf and the rest with kasrah (i.e., qirna).

statements.heading: F.33. Sūrat al-ʾAḥzāb
statements.text: The Kufans and Hišām read ʾan yakūna lahum with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., takūna).

statements.heading: F.33. Sūrat al-ʾAḥzāb
statements.text: ʿĀṣim reads wa-ḫātama n-nabiyyīna with fatḥah on the tāʾ and the rest with kasrah (i.e., ḫātima).

statements.heading: F.33. Sūrat al-ʾAḥzāb
statements.text: ʾan tamā̆ssūhunna,[292] turǧī/turǧiʾu (Q33:51)[293] and ʾinā/ēhu (Q33:53)[294] have al-ready been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.33. Sūrat al-ʾAḥzāb
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads lā taḥillu laka with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaḥillu).

statements.heading: F.33. Sūrat al-ʾAḥzāb
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads sādātinā in the plural with kasrah on the tāʾ and the rest in the singular with naṣb of the tāʾ (i.e., sādatanā).

statements.heading: F.33. Sūrat al-ʾAḥzāb
statements.text: ʿĀṣim reads laʿnan kabīran with bāʾ and the rest with ṯāʾ (i.e., kaṯīran). There are no yāʾs at all.

statements.heading: F.34. Sūrat al-Sabaʾ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʿallāmi l-ġaybi with ʾalif after the lām and with ḫafḍ of the mīm in the pattern faʿʿāl. The rest read ʿālimu/i l-ġaybi with ʾalif after the ʿayn in the pattern fāʿil. Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir applied rafʿ to it (i.e., ʿālimu) and the rest applied ḫafḍ (i.e., ʿālimi). lā yaʿzi/ubu,[295] and muʿāǧizīna/muʿaǧǧizīna in two places (Q34:5, 38)[296] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.34. Sūrat al-Sabaʾ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and Ḥafṣ read min riǧzin ʾalīmun here and in al-Ǧāṯiyah (Q45:11) with rafʿ of the mīm and the rest with ǧarr (i.e., ʾalīmin).

statements.heading: F.34. Sūrat al-Sabaʾ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾin yašaʾ yaḫsif and ʾaw yusqiṭ with yāʾ for all three, and al-Kisāʾī assimilated the fāʾ to the bāʾ (i.e., yaḫsib⸗bihumu l-ʾaṛda). The rest read nūn of those (i.e., našaʾ, naḫsif, nusqiṭ). kis(a)fan has already been mentioned.[297]

statements.heading: F.34. Sūrat al-Sabaʾ
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads wa-li-sulaymāna r-rīḥu with rafʿ and the rest with naṣb (i.e., ar-rīḥa).

statements.heading: F.34. Sūrat al-Sabaʾ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr read minsātahū with an unvocalised ʾalif replacing the hamzah; the replacement is received by audition (as it is irregular and cannot be defended on other grounds). Ibn Ḏakwān reads it with an unvowelled hamzah (i.e., minsaʾtahū). Similar forms occur on occasion in poetry to fit the metre, as al-ʾAḫfaš al-Dimašqī recited (the verse): The rest read it with a hamzah that carries a fatḥah (i.e., minsaʾatahū). But when Ḥamzah pauses, he makes (the hamzah) in between in accordance with his general principle (i.e., minsa.atah#).[298]

statements.heading: F.34. Sūrat al-Sabaʾ
statements.text: li-sabaʾin/a has already been mentioned.[299] Ḥafṣ and Ḥamzah read fī maskanihim with no vowel on the sīn and fatḥah on the kāf. Al-Kisāʾī reads likewise, except he has kasrah on the kāf (maskinihim). The rest read it with fatḥah on the sīn, kasrah on the kāf and with an ʾalif between them (i.e., masākinihim).

statements.heading: F.34. Sūrat al-Sabaʾ
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads ḏawātay ʾukuli ḫamṭin without tanwīn on the lām and the rest with tanwīn (i.e., ʾuk(u)lin ḫamtin). The lack of pronunciation of an extra vowel of al-ʾukl here by the two of the holy cities has already been mentioned.[300]

statements.heading: F.34. Sūrat al-Sabaʾ
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-hal nuǧāzī with nūn and with kasrah on the zāy, and ʾillā kafūra with naṣb. The rest read it with yāʾ, fatḥah on the zāy and with rafʿ (i.e., hal yuǧāza/ǟ ʾillā kafūru).

statements.heading: F.34. Sūrat al-Sabaʾ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Hišām read rabbanā baʿʿid bayna with gemination of the ʿayn without ʾalif. The rest read it with ʿalif and without gemination (i.e., bāʿid).

statements.heading: F.34. Sūrat al-Sabaʾ
statements.text: The Kufans read wa-la-qad ṣaddaqa with gemination of the dāl and the rest without gemination (i.e., ṣadaqa).

statements.heading: F.34. Sūrat al-Sabaʾ
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read li-man ʾuḏina lahū with ḍammah on the hamzah and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., ʾaḏina). Ibn ʿĀmir reads ḥattā ʾiḏā fazzaʿa with fatḥah on the fāʾ and the zāy. The rest read it with ḍammah on the fāʾ and kasrah on the zāy (i.e., fuzziʿa).

statements.heading: F.34. Sūrat al-Sabaʾ
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads fì l-ġurufati without ʾalif as a singular and the rest with ʾalif as a plural (i.e., al-ġurufāti).

statements.heading: F.34. Sūrat al-Sabaʾ
statements.text: wa-yawma yaḥšuruhum … ṯumma yaqūlu has already been mentioned.[301]

statements.heading: F.34. Sūrat al-Sabaʾ
statements.text: The two of the holy cities, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read at-tanāwušu with ḍammah on the wāw and the rest read it with hamzah (i.e., at-tanāʾušu). When Ḥamzah pauses on it, he makes it in between (i.e., at-tanā.uš#)[302] because it is from an-naʾiš which means al-ḥarakah fì l-ʾibṭāʾ (‘moving slowly’), so its root has a hamzah. But it is also conceivable to interpret it as coming from an-nawš which means at-tanāwul (‘to accept’). In this case, its root has a wāw and it is subsequently given a hamzah because of the ḍammah requiring it.[303] In effect the pausing on the ḍammah with a wāw returns it to its original form.

footnotes.text: In Classical Arabic the sequence wu is frequently shifted to ʾu, although it is never quite regular. Sībawayh (1988, IV:331) reports ʾulida and ʾuǧūh for wulida and wuǧūh. In the Qurʾān this phenomenon is found in yet another place, namely Q77:11, where اقتتis read as ʾuqittat by the majority of the readers but as wuqqitat by ʾAbū ʿAmr (F.77:11.).

statements.heading: F.34. Sūrat al-Sabaʾ
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read wa-ḥǖla baynahum and in al-Zumar (Q39:71, 73) sǖqa llaḏīna with ʾišmām of the ḍamm to the ḥāʾ and sīn and the rest read it with pure kasrah (i.e., ḥīla, sīqa).

statements.heading: F.34.1. [Yāʾs of Q34]
statements.text: There are three yāʾs: 1. ʿibādi š-šakūru (Q34:13) with no vowel (on the yāʾ) by Ḥamzah. 2. ʾin ʾaǧrī ʾillā (Q34:47) with no vowel by Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī. 3. rabbiya ʾinnahu samīʿun (Q34:50) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr.

statements.heading: F.34.2. [Removed yāʾs of Q34]
statements.text: There are two removed ones: 1. ka-l-ǧawābī (Q34:13) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr, and with retention in connected speech by Warš and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 2. kāna nakīrī (Q34:45) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Warš.

statements.heading: F.35. Sūrat al-Fāṭir
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ġayri llāhi with ḫafḍ of the rāʾ and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., ġayru ḷḷāhi).

statements.heading: F.35. Sūrat al-Fāṭir
statements.text: ʾarsala r-riyāḥa/r-rīḥa[304] and ʾilā baladin may(yi)tin[305] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.35. Sūrat al-Fāṭir
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads yudḫalūnahā with ḍammah on the yāʾ and fatḥah on the ḫāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ and ḍammah on the ḫāʾ (i.e., yadḫulūnahā). wa-luʾluʾin/an has already been mentioned.[306]

statements.heading: F.35. Sūrat al-Fāṭir
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads ka-ḏālika yuǧzā with a yāʾ that carries a ḍammah and with fatḥah on the zāy, and kullu kafūrin with rafʿ. The rest read it with a nūn that carries a fatḥah, with kasrah on the zāy and with naṣb (i.e., ka-ḏālika yaǧzī kulla kafūrin).

statements.heading: F.35. Sūrat al-Fāṭir
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʾAbū Bakr and al-Kisāʾī read ʿalā bayyinātin with ʾalif, in the plural, and the rest without ʾalif, in the singular (i.e., bayyinatin).

statements.heading: F.35. Sūrat al-Fāṭir
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads wa-makra s-sayyiʾ with no vowel on the hamzah in connected speech; due to the succession of vowels, it is pronounced without the final vowel (i.e., as-sayyiʾi wa-lā would contain four open syllables in a row), just like how ʾAbū ʿAmr places no vowel on the hamzah of bāriʾkum,[307] and what it is like that when he pauses on it. He replaces (the hamzah) with a quiescent yāʾ (i.e., as-sayyī#). The rest give it ḫafḍ in connected speech (i.e., as-sayyiʾi) and allow rawm (i.e., as-sayyiʾĭ#) or no vowel in pause (i.e., as-sayyiʾ#).

footnotes.text: See F.2:54. The explanation that this is due to the succession of vowels (tawālì l-ḥarakāt) is an old one: al-Farrāʾ uses the same argument in Luġāt al-Qurʾān (al-Farrāʾ 2014, 30).

statements.heading: F.35.1. [Removed yāʾ of Q35]
statements.text: There is a removed one: it is kāna nakīrī (Q35:26) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Warš.

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read yē-sīn with ʾimālah of the fatḥah of the yāʾ and the rest read it with a pure fatḥah (i.e., yā-sīn). Warš, ʾAbū Bakr, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī assimilated the nūn of the letters to the wāw but retained nasalisation (i.e., yā/ē-sīw̃⸗wa-lqurʾāni). It is like that in nūw̃-wa-l-qalami (Q68:1) except for most people of the oral tradition among the Egyptians. They adopt the nūn, in the tradition of Warš, there (i.e., Q68:1) with clear pronunciation (i.e., nūn wa-l-qalami). The rest pronounces the nūn clearly in both sūrahs (i.e., yā/ē-sīn wa-l-qur(ʾ)ān, nūn wa-l-qalami).

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read tanzīla l-ʿazīzi with naṣb of the lām and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., tanzīlu l-ʿazīzi).

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read saddan in both cases (in this verse) with fatḥah on the sīn and the rest with ḍammah (i.e., suddan).

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads fa-ʿazaznā without gemination of the zāy and the rest with gemination (i.e., fa-ʿazzaznā).

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: lammā/lamā ǧamīʿun,[308] al-ʾarḍu l-may(yi)tatu (Q36:33),[309] min ṯamarihī (Q36:35)[310] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-mā ʿamilat ʾaydīhim without hāʾ and the rest with hāʾ (i.e., ʿamilathū̆).[311]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 141).

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read wa-l-qamara qaddarnāhu with naṣb of the rāʾ and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., wa-l-qamaru).

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read ḏurriyyātihim in the plural with kasrah on the tāʾ and the rest read it in the singular with fatḥah on the tāʾ (i.e., ḏurriyatahum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Warš and Hišām read yaḫaṣṣimūna with fatḥah on the ḫāʾ and gemination on the ṣād. Qālūn and ʾAbū ʿAmr read it with ultrashort fatḥah on the ḫāʾ and gemination of the ṣād (i.e., yaḫăṣṣimūna); the written transmission from Qālūn is without a vowel (i.e., yaḫṣṣimūna).[312] Ḥamzah reads it with no vowel on the ḫāʾ and no gemination of the ṣād. The rest—that is, ʿĀṣim, Ibn Ḏakwān and al-Kisāʾī—read it with kasrah on the ḫāʾ and gemination of the ṣād (i.e., yaḫiṣṣimūna).

footnotes.text: Qālūn is said to have authored a book on his transmission of Nāfiʿ which he recited to his students (al-Dānī 2007, 292).

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: min marqadinā has already been mentioned.[313]

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: The two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr read fī šuġlin with no vowel on the ġayn and the rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., šuġulin).

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read fī ḏ̣ulalin with ḍammah on the ḏ̣āʾ without ʾalif. The rest read it with kasrah and ʾalif (i.e., ḏ̣ilālin).

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim read ǧibillan kaṯīran with kasrah on the ǧīm and bāʾ and gemination of the lām. ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with ḍammah on the ǧīm, no vowel on the bāʾ and no gemination on the lām (i.e., ǧublan). The rest read it like that except that they place a ḍammah on the bāʾ (i.e., ǧubulan).

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: ʿalā makānā̆tihim has already been mentioned.[314]

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read nunakkishu fì l-ḫalqi with ḍammah on the first nūn, fatḥah on the second and kasrah on the kāf with gemination. The rest read it with fatḥah on the first nūn, no vowel on the second and ḍammah on an ungeminated kāf (i.e., nankushū̆). Nāfiʿ and Ibn Ḏakwān read ʾa-fa-lā taʿqilūna here with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaʿqilūna).

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read li-tunḏira man kāna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., li-yunḏira).

statements.heading: F.36. Sūrat Yā-Sīn
statements.text: wa-mašā/ēribu[315] and fa-yakūnu/a (Q38:82)[316] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.36.1. [Yāʾs of Q36]
statements.text: There are three yāʾs: 1. wa-mā lī lā ʾaʿbudu (Q36:22) with no vowel by Ḥamzah. 2. ʾinniya ʾiḏān lafī (Q36:24) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 3. ʾinniya ʾāmantu (Q36:25) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr.

statements.heading: F.36.2. [Removed yāʾ of Q36]
statements.text: There is a removed one: wa-lā yunqiḏūnī (Q36:23) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Warš.

statements.heading: F.37. Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads aṣ-ṣāffāṣ⸗ṣaffan (Q37:1), fa-zāǧirāz⸗zaǧran (Q37:2), fa-ttāliyāḏ⸗ḏikran and likewise wa-ḏ-ḏāriyāḏ⸗ḏirwan (Q51:1) with assimilation of the tāʾ to what comes after it without hinting (at the vowel through rawm or ʾišmām) in all four. ʾAbū al-Fatḥ taught me to recite in the transmission of Ḫallād fa-l-muqliyāḏ⸗ḏikran, fa-l-muġīrāṣ⸗ṣubḥan in al-Mursalāt (Q77:5) and al-ʿĀdiyāt (Q100:3) with assimilation also, without hinting (at the vowel through rawm or ʾišmām). The rest placed kasrah on the tāʾ in all these cases without assimilation except what occurs in the manner of ʾAbū ʿAmr when he applies major assimilation. We have explained that previously.[317]

statements.heading: F.37. Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt
statements.text: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read bi-zayyinatin with tanwīn and the rest without tanwīn (i.e., bi-zayyinati). ʾAbū Bakr reads al-kawākiba with naṣb and the rest with ḫafḍ (i.e., al-kawākibi).

statements.heading: F.37. Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read lā yassammaʿūna with gemination of both the sīn and mīm. The rest read it without vowel on the sīn and no gemination of the mīm (i.e., yasmaʿūna).

statements.heading: F.37. Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī bal ʿaǧibtu with ḍammah on the tāʾ and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., ʿaǧibta).

statements.heading: F.37. Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt
statements.text: Qālūn and Ibn ʿĀmir read ʾaw ʾābāʾunā here and in al-Wāqiʿah (Q56:48) with no vowel on the wāw. The rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., ʾa-wa-ʾābāʾunā).[318] al-muḫli/aṣīna and all that is said about it[319] and qul naʿa/im (Q37:18)[320] have already been mentioned.

footnotes.text: This is a difference of interpretation of the same rasm اواٮاونا which has ambiguous word division.

statements.heading: F.37. Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʿanhā yunzifūna with kasrah on the zāy here and the rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., yunzafūna). There is no disagreement on the ḍammah on the yāʾ.

statements.heading: F.37. Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads ʾilayhi yuziffūna with ḍammah on the yāʾ and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., yaziffūna).

statements.heading: F.37. Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt
statements.text: yā bunayyi/a ʾinnī[321] and yā ʾabat/h#[322] have already been mentioned. Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read mā-ḏā turī with ḍammah on the tāʾ, kasrah on the rāʾ and the kasrah is pure (i.e., not ʾimālah), making it a verb of four letters (i.e., an ʾafʿala verb rather than a faʿala verb). The rest place fatḥah on both, making it a verb of three letters (i.e., a faʿala verb), ʾAbū ʿAmr applies ʾimālah to the fatḥah of the rāʾ (i.e., tarē) and Warš makes it in between (i.e., tarǟ), in accordance with their general principles.[323] The rest read it with pure fatḥah (i.e., tarā).

statements.heading: F.37. Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt
statements.text: Ibn Ḏakwān reads, according to my recitation to [ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz b. Ǧaʿfar] al-Fārisī, transmitting from al-Naqqāš from al-ʾAḫfaš from him, wa-ʾinna l-yāsa with removal of the hamzah (and in other paths it is transmitted like the rest). The rest pronounces it (i.e., wa-ʾinna ʾilyāsa). That is also how I recite it for Ibn Ḏakwān in the path of the Syrians.[324] But Ibn Ḏakwān says in his book, “It is without hamzah.” God knows best what he meant.[325]

footnotes.text: The Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān is more specific, “… from a group of Syrians from al-ʾAḫfaš.” There are indeed several readers that transmit through al-ʾAḫfaš (al-Dānī 2007, 334–36, 1527)

This comment does not make much sense in the context that the Taysīr gives us. However, on examining the discussion in al-Dānī’s Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān, it becomes clear that many (including al-Dānī) think that the wording in Ibn Ḏakwān’s book was not to indicate the presence of an ʾalif al-waṣl, but rather to prevent the reader from reading ʾilyaʾsa (al-Dānī 2007, 1527–28).

statements.heading: F.37. Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read aḷḷāha rabbakum wa-rabba with naṣb of the three nouns and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., aḷḷāhu rabbukum(ū) wa-rabbu).

statements.heading: F.37. Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read ʿalā ʾāli yāsīn as separate words like ʾāli muḥammadin. The rest read it with kasrah on the hamzah and no vowel on the lām connecting the words (i.e., ʾilyāsīn).[326]

footnotes.text: The rasm of this phrase ال  ياسഽن obviously favours the former reading as two separate words.

statements.heading: F.37.1. [Yāʾs of Q37]
statements.text: There are three yāʾs: 1. ʾinniya ʾarā/ē fì l-manāmi, and 2. ʾanniya ʾaḏbaḥuka (Q37:102) with fatḥah of both by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 3. sa-taǧiduniya ʾin šāʾa ḷḷāhu (Q37:103) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ.

statements.heading: F.37.2. [Removed yāʾ of Q37]
statements.text: There is a removed one: la-turdīnī wa-law-lā (Q37:56–7) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Warš.

statements.heading: F.38. Sūrat Ṣād
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read min fuwāqin with ḍammah on the fāʾ and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., fawāqin).

statements.heading: F.38. Sūrat Ṣād
statements.text: ʾaṣḥābu l(ʾ)aykati/a[327] and bi-s-sūqi/bi-s-suʾqi/bi-s-suʾūqi (Q38:33)[328] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.38. Sūrat Ṣād
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads wa-ḏkur ʿabdanā ʾibrāhīma in the singular and the rest in the plural (i.e., ʿibādanā).

statements.heading: F.38. Sūrat Ṣād
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Hišām read bi-ḫāliṣati without tanwīn and the rest with tanwīn (i.e., bi-ḫāliṣatin).

statements.heading: F.38. Sūrat Ṣād
statements.text: wa-l-yasaʿa/wa-l-laysaʿa has already been mentioned.[329]

statements.heading: F.38. Sūrat Ṣād
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read hāḏā mā yūʿadūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tūʿadūna).

statements.heading: F.38. Sūrat Ṣād
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-ġassāqun and in al-Nabaʾ (Q78:25) wa-ġassāqan with gemination of the sīn for both. The rest read it without gemination (i.e., wa-ġasāqun, wa-ġasāqan).

statements.heading: F.38. Sūrat Ṣād
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads wa-ʾuḫaru min šaklihī with ḍammah on the hamzah in the plural. The rest read it with fatḥah and an ʾalif after it in the singular (i.e., wa-ʾāḫaru).

statements.heading: F.38. Sūrat Ṣād
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read min al-ʾašrā/ēri // ttaḫaḏnāhum with ʾalif al-waṣl and with kasrah when they start on it (i.e., #ittaḫaḏnāhum). The rest read it with ʾalif al-qaṭʿ in both connected speech and when starting on it (i.e., (#)ʾa-ttaḫaḏnāhum). su/iḫriyyan has already been mentioned.[330]

statements.heading: F.38. Sūrat Ṣād
statements.text: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read qāla fa-l-ḥaqqu with rafʿ and the rest with naṣb (i.e., fa-lḥaqqa). There is no disagreement on the second instance (of the word) before ʾaqūlu (i.e., all read wa-l-ḥaqqa ʾaqūlu). al-muḫli/aṣīn (Q28:83) has already been mentioned.[331]

statements.heading: F.38.1. [Yāʾs of Q38]
statements.text: There are six yāʾs: 1. wa-liya naʿǧatun (Q38:23) and 2. mā kāna liya min ʿilmin (Q38:69) both with fatḥah by Ḥafṣ. 3. ʾinniya ʾaḥbabtu (Q38:32) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 4. min baʿdiya ʾinnaka (Q38:35) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 5. massani š-šayṭānu (Q38:41) with no vowel by Ḥamzah. 6. laʿnatiya ʾilā (Q38:78) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ.

statements.heading: F.39. Sūrat al-Zumar
statements.text: I have already mentioned fī buṭūni ʾi/umma/ihātikum(ū).[332]

statements.heading: F.39. Sūrat al-Zumar
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah and Hišām, (the last one of the four) with some disagreement, read yarḍahu lakum with shortness of the ḍammah on the hāʾ.[333] Hišām in my recitation to ʾAbū al-Fatḥ, ʾAbū Šuʿayb [as-Sūsī], ʾAbū ʿUmar [al-Dūrī][334] and others transmitting from al-Yazīdī read it without a vowel (i.e., yarḍah). However, I recited it to [ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz b. Ǧaʿfar] al-Fārisī and the other (ʾAbū al-Fatḥ) via the people of Iraq [= al-Dūrī and others] with ṣilah of the wāw. This is the transmission of ʾAbū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [Ibn al-Yazīdī] and ʾAbū Ḥamdūn[335] and others from al-Yazīdī (i.e., yarḍahū).[336] The rest read it with ṣilah of the wāw (i.e., yarḍahū).

footnotes.text: Shortness translates iḫtilās here. This normally means ‘ultrashort’, but it is technically a relative term. Since underlying form of the vowel is long (-hū), its shortening just yields -hu not -hŭ.
Neither Ibn al-Yazīdī nor ʾAbū Ḥamdūn are present in the ʾisnāds section U.4.3. but they are mentioned in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 327, 328–29).

This complex paragraph highlights a conflict between what al-Dānī has received through tilāwah (yarḍah for Hišām and yarḍahū for al-Sūsī and al-Dūrī), and riwāyah (yarḍahu for Hišām and yarḍah for al-Sūsī and al-Dūrī). The riwāyah transmission reported is indeed exactly as it appears in Ibn Muǧāhid’s Kitāb al-sabʿah where al-Dānī gets his riwāyah transmission from, through Muḥammad b. ʾAḥmad (Ibn Muǧāhid 1972, 560–61).

statements.heading: F.39. Sūrat al-Zumar
statements.text: li-yaḍilla/li-yuḍilla has already been mentioned.[337]

statements.heading: F.39. Sūrat al-Zumar
statements.text: The two of the holy cities and Ḥamzah read ʾa-man huwa without gemination of the mīm and the rest with gemination (i.e., ʾam-man).

statements.heading: F.39. Sūrat al-Zumar
statements.text: ʾAbū Šuʿayb [al-Sūsī] reads fa-baššir ʿibādiya // llaḏīna with a yāʾ that carries a fatḥah in connected speech and with no vowel in pause (i.e., ʿibādī#). ʾAbū Ḥamdūn[338] and others transmitting from al-Yazīdī say that it is with fatḥah (on the yāʾ) in connected speech but with removal (of the yāʾ) in pause (i.e., ʿibād#). To me this is an analogy (qiyās) with the opinion of ʾAbū ʿAmr to follow what is written in pause.[339] The rest removes (the yāʾ) in both connected speech and pause (i.e., ʿibādi, ʿibād#).

footnotes.text: ʾAbū Ḥamdūn is not present in U.4.3. But he is mentioned in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 328–29).
The rasm here lacks the final yāʾ, i.e.,  عباد.

statements.heading: F.39. Sūrat al-Zumar
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read wa-raǧulan sāliman with ʾalif after the sīn and kasrah on the lām. The rest read it with fatḥah on the lām without ʾalif (i.e., salaman).

statements.heading: F.39. Sūrat al-Zumar
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read bi-kāfin ʿibādahū with ʾalif as a plural and the rest without ʾalif as a singular (i.e., ʿabdahū).

statements.heading: F.39. Sūrat al-Zumar
statements.text: ʿalā makānā̆tikum(ū) has already been mentioned.[340]

statements.heading: F.39. Sūrat al-Zumar
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads kāšifātun ḍurrahū and mumsikātun raḥmatahū with tanwīn on both and with naṣb of ḍurrahū and raḥmatahū. The rest read it without tanwīn and with ḫafḍ of ḍurrihī and raḥmatihī (i.e., kāšifatu ḍurrihī, mumsikātu raḥmatihī).

statements.heading: F.39. Sūrat al-Zumar
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read allatī quḍiya ʿalayhā with ḍammah on the qāf, kasrah on the ḍād and fatḥah on the yāʾ, and al-mawtu with rafʿ. The rest read it with fatḥah on both the qāf and ḍād, with an ʾalif after it in pronunciation (as opposed to its spelling with a yāʾ) and al-mawta with naṣb (i.e., allatī qaḍā/ǟ ʿalayhà l-mawta).

statements.heading: F.39. Sūrat al-Zumar
statements.text: lā taqni/aṭū has already been mentioned.[341]

statements.heading: F.39. Sūrat al-Zumar
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read bi-mafāzātihim with ʾalif as a plural and the rest without ʾalif as a singular (i.e., bi-mafāzatihim(ū)).

statements.heading: F.39. Sūrat al-Zumar
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads taʾmurūnanī ʾaʿbudu with two nūns, the first one carrying a fatḥah. Nāfiʿ reads it with one ungeminated nūn (i.e., taʾ/āmurūnī) and the rest read it with a single geminated nūn (i.e., taʾ/āmurūnnī).[342]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 147).

statements.heading: F.39. Sūrat al-Zumar
statements.text: wa-ǧǖ/īʾa and wa-sǖ/īqa (Q39:71, 73) have already been mentioned.[343]

statements.heading: F.39. Sūrat al-Zumar
statements.text: The Kufans read futiḥat ʾabwābuhā in two places here (Q39:71, 73) and in al-Nabaʾ (Q78:19) without gemination of the tāʾ. The rest read it with gemination (i.e., futtiḥat).

statements.heading: F.39.1. [Yāʾs of Q39]
statements.text: There are six yāʾs: 1. ʾinniya ʾumirtu (Q39:11) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ. 2. ʾinniya ʾaḫāfu (Q39:13) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 3. ʾin ʾarādani llāhu (Q39:38) with no vowel by Ḥamzah. 4. qul yā ʿibādi llaḏīna ʾasrafū (Q39:53) with no vowel in pause (i.e., yā ʿibād#), and removal (of the yāʾ) in continued speech by ʾAbū ʿAmr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī in accordance to what we have mentioned in al-ʿAnkabūt (Q29:56).[344] The rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., yā ʿibādiya). 5. taʾ/āmurūn(n)iya (Q39:64) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities. 6. fa-baššir ʿibādī (Q39:17): we have discussed the disagreement previously.[345]

statements.heading: F.40. Sūrat al-Muʾmin
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Qālūn, Ḥafṣ and Hišām read ḥā-mīm with fatḥah on the ḥāʾ in all of the Ḥāwāmīm (Q40:1; Q41:1; Q42:1; Q43:1; Q44:1; Q45:1; Q46:1). Warš and ʾAbū ʿAmr pronounce it in between (i.e., ḥǟ-mīm) and the rest read it with ʾimālah (i.e., ḥē-mīm).

statements.heading: F.40. Sūrat al-Muʾmin
statements.text: kalimā̆tu rabbika has already been mentioned.[346]

statements.heading: F.40. Sūrat al-Muʾmin
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Hišām read wa-llaḏīna tadʿūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yadʿūna).

statements.heading: F.40. Sūrat al-Muʾmin
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads ʾašaddu minkum with kāf and the rest with hāʾ (i.e., minhum(ū)).[347]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 141).

statements.heading: F.40. Sūrat al-Muʾmin
statements.text: The Kufans read ʾaw ʾan with the addition of ʾalif before the wāw and without vowel on the wāw. The rest read it with fatḥah on the wāw and without ʾalif (i.e., wa-ʾan).[348] Nāfiʿ, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ read yuḏ̣hira with ḍammah on the yāʾ and kasrah on the hāʾ, and fì l-ʾarḍi l-fasāda with naṣb. The rest read it with fatḥah on both the yāʾ and the hāʾ, and with rafʿ of al-fasādu (i.e., yaḏ̣hara fì l-ʾarḍi l-fasādu).

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 141).

statements.heading: F.40. Sūrat al-Muʾmin
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ibn Ḏakwān read ʿalā kulli qalbin with tanwīn and the rest without tanwīn (i.e., ʿalā kulli qalbi).

statements.heading: F.40. Sūrat al-Muʾmin
statements.text: wa-ṣa/udda ʿani s-sabīli has already been mentioned.[349] Ḥafṣ reads fa-ʾaṭṭaliʿa with naṣb of the ʿayn and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., fa-ʾaṭṭaliʿu).

statements.heading: F.40. Sūrat al-Muʾmin
statements.text: yadḫulūna l-ǧannata has already been mentioned.[350]

statements.heading: F.40. Sūrat al-Muʾmin
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʾAbū ʿAmr and ʾAbū Bakr read as-sāʿatu dḫulū with ʾalif al-waṣl and ḍammah on the ḫāʾ, but with ḍammah (on the ʾalif) when starting on it (i.e., #ʾudḫulū).
