The rest read it with ʾalif al-qaṭʿ both when starting on it and in connected speech (fī l-ḥālayn) and with kasrah on the ḫāʾ (i.e., ʾadḫilū).

statements.heading: F.40. Sūrat al-Muʾmin
statements.text: The Kufans and Nāfiʿ read yawma lā yanfaʿu with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tanfaʿu).

statements.heading: F.40. Sūrat al-Muʾmin
statements.text: The Kufans read qalīlan mā tataḏakkarūna with two tāʾs. The rest read it with yāʾ and tāʾ (i.e., yataḏakkarūna).

statements.heading: F.40. Sūrat al-Muʾmin
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū Bakr read sa-yudḫalūna ǧahannama with ḍammah on the yāʾ and fatḥah on the ḫāʾ. The rest with fatḥah on the yāʾ and ḍammah on the ḫāʾ (i.e., sa-yadḫulūna).

statements.heading: F.40. Sūrat al-Muʾmin
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, ʾAbū ʿAmr, Ḥafṣ and Hišām read šuyūḫan with ḍammah on the šīn and the rest read it with kasrah (i.e., šiyūḫan). kun fa-yakūna/u has already been mentioned.[351]

statements.heading: F.40.1. [Yāʾs of Q40]
statements.text: There are eight yāʾs: 1. ʾinniya ʾaḫāfu in three places (Q40:26, 2. Q40:30, 3. Q40:32) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 4. ḏarūniya ʾaqtul (Q40:26) and 5. ʾadʿūniya ʾastaǧib lakumū (Q40:60) with fatḥah by Ibn Kaṯīr. 6. laʿallī ʾabluġu (Q40:36) with no vowel by the Kufans. 7. mā lī ʾadʿūkum (Q40:41) with no vowel by the Kufans and Ibn Ḏakwān. 8. ʾamriya ʾilà ḷḷāhi (Q40:44) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr.

statements.heading: F.40.2. [Removed yāʾs of Q40]
statements.text: There are three removed ones: 1. at-talāqī (Q40:15) and 2. at-tunādī (Q40:32) with retention (of the yāʾ) both in connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr. With retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Warš and there is disagreement in transmission from Qālūn. I recited them for him in both ways (i.e., at-talāqi/at-talāqī, at-tunādi/at-tunādī). 3. ittabiʿūnī ʾahdikum(ū) (Q40:38) with retention (of the yāʾ) both in connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr. With retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Qālūn and ʾAbū ʿAmr.

statements.heading: F.41. Sūrat Fuṣṣilat
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read naḥisātin with kasrah on the ḥāʾ. Al-Fārisī transmitted to me from ʾAbū Ṭāhir from his companions from ʾAbū al-Ḥāriṯ[352] that he applies ʾimālah to fatḥah on the sīn (i.e., naḥisētin), but I do not recite it like that because I think that it is a mistake. The rest read it without vowel on the ḥāʾ (i.e., naḥsātin).

footnotes.text: This ʾisnād to ʾAbū al-Ḥāriṯ is not mentioned in U.4.7.2., nor is it mentioned in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān.

statements.heading: F.41. Sūrat Fuṣṣilat
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads wa-yawma naḥšuru with a nūn that carries a fatḥah and with ḍammah on the šīn, and ʾaʿdāʾa ḷḷāhi with naṣb. The rest read it with a yāʾ that carries a ḍammah and with fatḥah on the šīn, and ʾaʿdāʾu ḷḷāhi with rafʿ (i.e., yuḥšaru ʾaʿdāʾu ḷḷāhi).

statements.heading: F.41. Sūrat Fuṣṣilat
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʾAbū Bakr and ʾAbū Šuʿayb [al-Sūsī] read rabbanā ʾarnā without a vowel on the rāʾ here only. ʾAbū ʿUmar [al-Dūrī], transmitting from al-Yazīdī, reads it with an ultrashort kasrah (i.e., ʾarĭnā). The rest read it with a full vowel (i.e., ʾarinā).

statements.heading: F.41. Sūrat Fuṣṣilat
statements.text: allaḏīna yalḥadūna/yulḥidūna has already been mentioned.[353]

statements.heading: F.41. Sūrat Fuṣṣilat
statements.text: Hišām reads ʾaʿǧamiyyun with a single hamzah without length as a declarative. The rest read it as an interrogative. ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī pronounce both hamzahs (i.e., ʾa-ʾaʿǧamiyyun). The rest read it with hamzah and length. Qālūn and ʾAbū ʿAmr pronounce it with full length because in their opinion the ʾalif is inserted between the hamzah pronounced strongly and the one pronounced softly (i.e., ʾā-.aʿǧamiyyun). Warš, in accordance with his general principle,[354] replaces the second hamzah with an ʾalif without insertion (of ā) between them (i.e., ʾāʿǧamiyyun). Ibn Kaṯīr, likewise in accordance with his general principles, makes the second hamzah in between without insertion (of ā) between them (i.e., ʾa-.aʿǧamiyyun). This is the same for what Ḥafṣ and Ibn Ḏakwān say, by analogy, (so they also recite ʾa-.aʿǧamiyyun), because their (regular) practice is to pronounce both hamzahs without insertion (of ā) between them. However, there are some people of oral tradition among my teachers who adopt for Ibn Ḏakwān the full pronunciation of the length (i.e., ʾā-.aʿǧamiyyun) here and in Nūn wa-l-Qalam in His speech ʾā-.an kāna ḏā mālin (Q68:14) analogous to the practice of Hišām. But this is not the right consideration nor is it proper from the point of view of analogy. This is because Ibn Ḏakwān, since he does not insert a separation with ʾalif between two hamzahs even when he pronounces them fully, despite the heaviness of their meeting, it should be understood that introducing (ā) between them in the case of softening one of the two while this is (even) lighter, is incorrect for his practice. Considering that al-ʾAḫfaš, transmitting from him, already said in his book[355] that it is with full pronunciation of the first and softening of the second without mentioning insertion (of ā) between them in these two places, that is clearly in line with what we have said.

footnotes.text: Al-ʾAḫfaš had a book describing the transmission of Ibn Ḏakwān (Hamdan 2018, 75).

statements.heading: F.41. Sūrat Fuṣṣilat
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read min ṯamarātin in the plural and the rest in the singular (i.e., min ṯamaratin). wa-na/eʾā/ē/ǟ bi-ǧānibihī/wa-nāʾa bi-ǧānibihī (Q41:51) has already been mentioned.[356]

statements.heading: F.41.1. [Yāʾs of Q41]
statements.text: There are two yāʾs: 1. ʾayna šurukāʾiya qālū (Q41:47) with fatḥah by Ibn Ḏakwān. 2. ʾilā rabbiya ʾinna (Q41:50) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ, with disagreement in the transmission from Qālūn, and ʾAbū ʿAmr.

statements.heading: F.42. Sūrat al-Šūrā
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads ka-ḏālika yūḥā ʾilayka with fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and the rest with kasrah (i.e., yūḥī).

statements.heading: F.42. Sūrat al-Šūrā
statements.text: y/takādu s-samāwātu has already been mentioned.[357] ʾAbū Bakr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read yanfaṭirna here with nūn and kasrah on the ṭāʾ. The rest read it with tāʾ and fatḥah on the ṭāʾ (i.e., yatafaṭṭarna).

statements.heading: F.42. Sūrat al-Šūrā
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read yubašširu with ḍammah on the yāʾ, fatḥah on the bāʾ and kasrah on a geminate šīn. The rest read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ, without a vowel on the bāʾ and with ḍammah on an ungeminated šīn (i.e., yabšuru).

statements.heading: F.42. Sūrat al-Šūrā
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-yaʿlamu mā tafʿalūna with tāʾ. The rest read it with yāʾ (i.e., yafʿalūna).

statements.heading: F.42. Sūrat al-Šūrā
statements.text: yunzilu/yunazzilu l-ġayṯa has already been mentioned.[358]

statements.heading: F.42. Sūrat al-Šūrā
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read bi-mā kasabat without fāʾ and the rest read fa-bi-mā with fāʾ.[359]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 141).

statements.heading: F.42. Sūrat al-Šūrā
statements.text: ar-rīḥa/ar-riyāḥa has already been mentioned.[360]

statements.heading: F.42. Sūrat al-Šūrā
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read yaʿlamu llaḏīna with rafʿ of the mīm and the rest with naṣb (i.e., yaʿlama).

statements.heading: F.42. Sūrat al-Šūrā
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read kabīra l-ʾiṯmi here and in al-Naǧm (Q53:32) with kasrah on the bāʾ without ʾalif or hamzah. The rest read it with fatḥah on the bāʾ, and with ʾalif and hamzah after it (i.e., kabāʾira).

statements.heading: F.42. Sūrat al-Šūrā
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads ʾaw yursilu with rafʿ of the lām and fa-yūḥī bi-ʾiḏnihī with no vowel on the yāʾ. The rest read both with naṣb (i.e., yursila, fa-yūḥiya).

statements.heading: F.42.1. [Removed yāʾ of Q42]
statements.text: There is a removed one: it is al-ǧawārī fì l-baḥri (Q42:32) with retention (of the yāʾ) both in connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr, and with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech only by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr.

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: I have already mentioned fī ʾu/immi l-kitābi.[361]

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ṣafḥan ʾin kuntum with kasrah on the hamzah and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., ʾan).

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: al-ʾarḍa mahdan/mihādan,[362] ka-ḏālika tuḫraǧūna (Q43:11),[363] ǧuz(u)ʾan (Q43:15)[364] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾa-wa-man yunaššaʾu with ḍammah on the yāʾ, fatḥah on the nūn and gemination of the šīn. The rest read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ, no vowel on the nūn and no gemination of the šīn (i.e., yanšaʾu).

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: The two of the holy cities and Ibn ʿĀmir read ʿinda r-raḥmāni with a nūn that does not carry a vowel and with fatḥah on the dāl. The rest read it with a bāʾ that carries a fatḥah, with ʾalif after it and with ḍammah on the dāl (i.e., ʿibādu r-raḥmāni). Nāfiʿ reads ʾa.ušhidū with two hamzahs, the second carrying a ḍammah with softening, so that it is between the hamzah and the wāw. Qālūn, in the transmission of ʾAbū Našīṭ, with some disagreement, introduces an ʾalif before it (i.e., ʾā.ušhidū) and the šīn does not carry a vowel. The rest read ʾa-šahidū with a single hamzah that carries a fatḥah and with fatḥah on the šīn.

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read qāla ʾulū with an ʾalif and the rest read qul without ʾalif.

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read saqfan with fatḥah on the sīn and without a vowel on the qāf as a singular. The rest read it with ḍammah on both as a plural (i.e., suqufan).

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah and Hišām, with some disagreement, here read lammā matāʿu with gemination of the mīm and the rest read it without gemination (i.e., la-mā).

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: The two of the holy cities, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū Bakr read ʾiḏā ǧāʾānā with ʾalif as a dual, and the rest read it without ʾalif as a singular (i.e., ǧāʾanā).

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: yā ʾayyuha/u s-sāḥiru has already been mentioned.[365]

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads ʿalayhi ʾaswiratun without a vowel on the sīn and without ʾalif. The rest read it with fatḥah on it and with ʾalif after it (i.e., ʾasāwiratun).

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read fa-ǧaʿalnāhum sulufan with ḍammah on both the sīn and the lām. The rest read it with fatḥah on both (i.e., salafan).

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read yaṣuddūna with ḍammah on the ṣād and the rest read it with kasrah (i.e., yaṣiddūna).

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: The Kufans read ʾa-ʾālihatunā ḫayrun with full pronunciation of the two hamzahs and with an ʾalif after it. The rest read it with softening of the second (hamzah) and with ʾalif after it (i.e., ʾa-.ālihatunā). None of them introduces an ʾalif between a hamzah pronounced fully and another pronounced softened, as we have already mentioned in Sūrat al-ʾAʿrāf.[366]

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read taštahīhi l-ʾanfusu with two hāʾs and the rest read it with one (i.e., taštahī).[367]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 141).

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: li-r-raḥmāni waladun/wuldun has already been mentioned.[368]

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-ʾilayhi yurǧaʿūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ.

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read waqīlihī with ḫafḍ of the lām and with kasrah on the hāʾ. The rest read it with naṣb of the lām and with ḍammah on the hāʾ (i.e., waqīlahū).

statements.heading: F.43. Sūrat al-Zuḫruf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read fa-sawfa taʿmalūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaʿmalūna).

statements.heading: F.43.1. [Yāʾs of Q43]
statements.text: There are two yāʾs: 1. min taḥtiya ʾa-fa-lā (Q43:51) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ, al-Bazzī and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 2. yā ʿibādiya lā ḫawfun (Q43:68) with fatḥah by ʾAbū Bakr in connected speech, without a vowel in both connected speech and pause by Nāfiʿ, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir (i.e., yā ʿibādī, yā ʿibādī#). The rest read it with removal (of the yāʾ) in both connected speech and pause (i.e., yā ʿibādi, yā ʿibād#).[369]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 141).

statements.heading: F.43.2. [Removed yāʾ of Q43]
statements.text: There is a removed one: wa-ttabiʿūnī hāḏā (Q43:61) with addition in connected speech by ʾAbū ʿAmr.

statements.heading: F.44. Sūrat al-Duḫān
statements.text: The Kufans read rabbi s-samāwāti with ḫafḍ and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., rabbu).

statements.heading: F.44. Sūrat al-Duḫān
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and Ḥafṣ read yaġlī fì l-buṭūni with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taġlī).

statements.heading: F.44. Sūrat al-Duḫān
statements.text: The two of the holy cities and Ibn ʿĀmir read fa-ʿtulūhu with ḍammah on the tāʾ and the rest with kasrah (i.e., fa-ʿtilūhu).

statements.heading: F.44. Sūrat al-Duḫān
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads ḏuq ʾannaka with fatḥah on the hamzah and the rest with kasrah (i.e., ʾinnaka).

statements.heading: F.44. Sūrat al-Duḫān
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read fī muqāmin with ḍammah on the mīm and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., maqāmin).

statements.heading: F.44.1. [Yāʾs of Q44]
statements.text: There are two yāʾs: 1. ʾinniya ʾātikum(ū) (Q44:19) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 2. liya fa-ʿtazilūni (Q44:21) with fatḥah by Warš.

statements.heading: F.44.2. [Removed yāʾs of Q44]
statements.text: There are two removed ones: 1. ʾan tarǧumūnī (Q44:20) and 2. fa-ʿtazilūnī (Q44:21) with retention (of the yāʾ) of both in connected speech by Warš.

statements.heading: F.45. Sūrat al-Ǧāṯiyah
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read taṣrīfi r-rīḥi ʾāyātin (Q45:5) and min dābbatin ʾāyātin (Q45:4) with ar-rīḥi in the singular and with kasrah on the tāʾ of both words. The rest read it in the plural and with rafʿ of the tāʾ (i.e., taṣrīfi r-riyāḥi ʾāyātun, min dābbatin ʾāyātun).

statements.heading: F.45. Sūrat al-Ǧāṯiyah
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī wa-ʾāyātihī tuʾimūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yuʾ/ūminūna).

statements.heading: F.45. Sūrat al-Ǧāṯiyah
statements.text: min riǧzin ʾalīmu/in has already been mentioned.[370]

statements.heading: F.45. Sūrat al-Ǧāṯiyah
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read li-naǧziya qawman with nūn and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaǧziya).

statements.heading: F.45. Sūrat al-Ǧāṯiyah
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read sawāʾan maḥyā/ēhum with naṣb and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., sawāʾun).

statements.heading: F.45. Sūrat al-Ǧāṯiyah
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ġašwatan with fatḥah on the ġayn and no vowel on the šīn. The rest read it with kasrah on the ġayn, fatḥah on the šīn and with ʾalif after it (i.e., ġišāwatan).

statements.heading: F.45. Sūrat al-Ǧāṯiyah
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads wa-s-sāʿata lā rayba fīhā with naṣb and the rest with rafʿ.

statements.heading: F.45. Sūrat al-Ǧāṯiyah
statements.text: lā yuḫraǧūna/yaḫruǧūna has already been mentioned.[371] There are no yāʾs at all.

statements.heading: F.46. Sūrat al-ʾAḥqāf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, al-Bazzī, with some disagreement, and Ibn ʿĀmir read li-tunḏira llaḏīna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., li-yunḏira).

statements.heading: F.46. Sūrat al-ʾAḥqāf
statements.text: The Kufans read bi-wālidayhi ʾiḥsānan with a hamzah that carries a kasrah, without vowel on the ḥāʾ, with fatḥah on the sīn and with an ʾalif after it. The rest read ḥusnan with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and no vowel on the sīn without ʾalif.[372] The Kufans and Ibn Ḏakwān read kurhan in two places (in this verse) with ḍammah on the kāf and the rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., karhan).

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 142).

statements.heading: F.46. Sūrat al-ʾAḥqāf
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read nataqabbalu ʿanhum ʾaḥsana mā ʿamilū wa-nataǧāwazu with nūn on both, with both carrying a fatḥah and with naṣb of the nūn of ʾaḥsana. The rest read it with yāʾ that carries a ḍammah on both words and with rafʿ of the nūn of ʾaḥsanu (i.e., yutaqabbalu ʿanhum(ū) ʾaḥsanu mā ʿamilū wa-yutaǧāwazu).

statements.heading: F.46. Sūrat al-ʾAḥqāf
statements.text: ʾuffu/i/a(n) lakumā has already been mentioned.[373] Hišām reads ʾa-taʿidānnī with a single geminated nūn and the rest with two nūns, both carrying a kasrah (i.e., ʾa-taʿidāninī).

statements.heading: F.46. Sūrat al-ʾAḥqāf
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and Hišām read wa-li-yuwaffiyahum(ū) with yāʾ and the rest read it with nūn (i.e., wa-li-nuwaffiyahum).

statements.heading: F.46. Sūrat al-ʾAḥqāf
statements.text: Ibn Ḏakwān reads ʾa-ʾaḏhabtum with two fully pronounced hamzahs without length. Ibn Kaṯīr and Hišām read it with hamzah and length, and Hišām stretches it in terms of length (i.e., Ibn Kaṯīr ʾa-.aḏhabtumū, Hišām ʾā-.aḏhabtum) according to his general principle.[374] The rest read it with a single hamzah without length as a declarative (i.e., ʾaḏhabtum).

footnotes.text: With the reference to the general principle, it seems clear that the intention of madd ‘length’ in this description refers to the bayna bayn realisation of hamzah rather than ʾā. See U.11.1. for the description.

statements.heading: F.46. Sūrat al-ʾAḥqāf
statements.text: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read lā yurā/ē with a yāʾ that carries a ḍammah and ʾillā masākinuhum with rafʿ. The rest read it with a tāʾ that carries a fatḥah and with naṣb (i.e., lā yarā/ē/ǟ ʾillā masākinahum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.46. Sūrat al-ʾAḥqāf
statements.text: wa-ʾuballiġukum(ū)/ʾubliġukum has already been mentioned.[375]

statements.heading: F.46.1. [Yāʾs of Q46]
statements.text: There are four yāʾs: 1. ʾawziʿniya ʾan ʾaškura (Q46:15) with fatḥah by Warš and al-Bazzī. 2. ʾa-taʿidāniniya ʾan (Q46:17) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities. 3. ʾinniya ʾaḫāfu (Q46:21) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 4. wa-lākinniya ʾarā/ēkum(ū) (Q46:23) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ, al-Bazzī and ʾAbū ʿAmr.

statements.heading: F.47. Sūrat Muḥammad (s)
statements.text: Ḥafṣ and ʾAbū ʿAmr read wa-llaḏīna qutilū with ḍammah on the qāf and kasrah on the tāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on both, with an ʾalif between them (i.e., qātalū).

statements.heading: F.47. Sūrat Muḥammad (s)
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads ʾasinin with shortness and the rest with length (i.e., ʾāsinin).

statements.heading: F.47. Sūrat Muḥammad (s)
statements.text: Muḥammad b. ʾAḥmad b. ʿAlī al-Baġdādī related to us, saying that Ibn Muǧāhid related to us, saying that Muḍar b. Muḥammad related to us from al-Bazzī with his ʾisnād back to Ibn Kaṯīr that he said ʾanifan with shortness, and this is how I recited it in the transmission of ʾAbū Rabīʿah from him to ʾAbū al-Fatḥ.[376] But I read it to [ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz b. Ǧaʿfar] al-Fārisī in his (ʾAbū Rabīʿah’s) transmission with length (i.e., ʾānifan). I recited it likewise in the transmission of al-Ḫuzāʿī[377] and others from him, and this is what I adopt.

footnotes.text: This tilāwah ʾisnād is not mentioned in U.4.2.2. but it is present in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān and indeed also reported by Ibn Muǧāhid via Muḍar b. Muḥammad. In the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān Muḍar is not mentioned, and the variant ʾanifan is attributed to an imprecision in the wording in a book by al-Bazzī on the reading of Ibn Kaṯīr (al-Dānī 2007, 308, 1591; Ibn Muǧāhid 1972, 600).
This transmission does not occur in the ʾisnād section, but it is mentioned in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 309–10).

statements.heading: F.47. Sūrat Muḥammad (s)
statements.text: fa-hal ʿasaytum(ū)/ʿasītum has already been mentioned.[378]

statements.heading: F.47. Sūrat Muḥammad (s)
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr recites wa-ʾumliya lahum with ḍammah on the hamzah, kasrah on the lām and fatḥah on the yāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the hamzah and the lām (i.e., wa-ʾamlā/ē/ǟ).

statements.heading: F.47. Sūrat Muḥammad (s)
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾisrārahum with kasrah on the hamzah and the rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., ʾasrārahum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.47. Sūrat Muḥammad (s)
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads wa-li-yabluwannakum ḥattā yaʿlama and yabluwa with yāʾ for all three; the rest read them with nūn (i.e., wa-li-nabluwannakum(ū) ḥattā naʿlama, nabluwa).

statements.heading: F.47. Sūrat Muḥammad (s)
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr and Ḥamzah said wa-tadʿū ʾilà s-silmi with kasrah on the sīn and the rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., as-salmi).

statements.heading: F.48. Sūrat al-Fatḥ
statements.text: I have already mentioned dāʾiratu s-sūʾi/sawʾi[379] and ʿalayhu ḷḷāhu/ʿalayhi llāhu (Q48:10).[380]

statements.heading: F.48. Sūrat al-Fatḥ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read li-yuʾ/ūminū bi-llāhi wa-rasūlihī wa-yuʿazzirūhu wa-yuwaqqirūhu wa-yusabbiḥūhu with yāʾ in all four and the rest read them with tāʾ (i.e., li-tuʾ/ūminū bi-llāhi wa-rasūlihī wa-tuʿazzirūhu wa-tuwaqqirūhu wa-tusabbiḥūhu).

statements.heading: F.48. Sūrat al-Fatḥ
statements.text: The two of the holy cities and Ibn ʿĀmir read fa-sa-nuʾ/ūtīhi with nūn and the rest read it with yāʾ (i.e., fa-sa-yuʾ/ūtīhī̆).

statements.heading: F.48. Sūrat al-Fatḥ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read bikum ḍurran with ḍammah on the ḍād and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., ḍarran).

statements.heading: F.48. Sūrat al-Fatḥ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read kalima ḷḷāhi with kasrah on the lām; the rest read it with fatḥah and an ʾalif after it (i.e., kalāma).

statements.heading: F.48. Sūrat al-Fatḥ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read nudḫilhu and nuʿaḏḏibhu with nūn on both. The rest read them with yāʾ (i.e., yudḫilhū̆, yuʿaḏḏibhū̆).

statements.heading: F.48. Sūrat al-Fatḥ
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads bimā yaʿlamūna baṣīran with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taʿlamūna).

statements.heading: F.48. Sūrat al-Fatḥ
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and Ibn Ḏakwān read šaṭaʾahū with vowel on the ṭāʾ and the rest without a vowel (i.e., šaṭʾahū). Ibn Ḏakwān reads fa-ʾazarahū with shortness and the rest with length (i.e., fa-ʾāzarahū). ʿalā suʾqihī/suʾūqihī/sūqihī has already been mentioned.[381]

statements.heading: F.49. Sūrat al-Ḥuǧurāt
statements.text: fa-taṯabbatū/fa-tabayyanū,[382] laḥma ʾaḫīhī̆ may(yi)tan (Q49:12)[383] and the tāʾs of al-Bazzī (Q49:11, 12, 13)[384] have already been mentioned before.

statements.heading: F.49. Sūrat al-Ḥuǧurāt
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads yaʾlitkum with hamzah without a vowel after the yāʾ and, when he softens it, he replaces it with ʾalif (i.e., yālitkum). The rest read it without hamzah or ʾalif (i.e., yalitkum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.49. Sūrat al-Ḥuǧurāt
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads baṣīrun bimā yaʿlamūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taʿlamūna).

statements.heading: F.50. Sūrat Qāf
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū Bakr read yawma yaqūlu with yāʾ and the rest read it with nūn (i.e., naqūlu).

statements.heading: F.50. Sūrat Qāf
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads hāḏā mā yūʿadūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tūʿadūna).

statements.heading: F.50. Sūrat Qāf
statements.text: The two of the holy cities and Ḥamzah read wa-ʾidbāra s-suǧūdi with kasrah on the hamzah and the rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., wa-ʾadbāra).

statements.heading: F.50. Sūrat Qāf
statements.text: yawma taš(š)aqqaqu l-(ʾ)arḍu has already been mentioned.[385]

statements.heading: F.50.1. [Removed yāʾs of Q50]
statements.text: There are three removed ones:[386] 1. waʿīdī // ʾa-faʿī ʾa-faʿayīnā (Q50:14–15) and 2. man yaḫāfu waʿīdī (Q50:45) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Warš. 3. al-munādī min (Q50:41) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr, and retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 4. Al-Naqqāš, transmitting from ʾAbū Rabīʿah from al-Bazzī, and Ibn Muǧāhid, transmitting from Qunbul, say that yunādī# (Q50:41) is read with yāʾ in pause. The rest pause on it without yāʾ (yunād#).

footnotes.text: Despite the text clearly saying there are three removed yāʾs, al-Dānī lists four.

statements.heading: F.51. Sūrat Wa-l-Ḏāriyāt
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read miṯlu mā ʾannakum with rafʿ of the lām and the rest with naṣb (i.e., miṯla).

statements.heading: F.51. Sūrat Wa-l-Ḏāriyāt
statements.text: qāla salāmun/silmun has already been mentioned.[387]

statements.heading: F.51. Sūrat Wa-l-Ḏāriyāt
statements.text: [388] Al-Kisāʾī reads fa-ʾaḫaḏathumu ṣ-ṣaʿqatun without a vowel on the ʿayn and without ʾalif. The rest read it with ʾalif and kasrah on the ʿayn (i.e., ṣ-ṣāʿiqatun).

footnotes.text: Pretzl has 45; this is a mistake.

statements.heading: F.51. Sūrat Wa-l-Ḏāriyāt
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-qawmi nūḥin with ḫafḍ and the rest with naṣb (i.e., wa-qawma).

statements.heading: F.52. Sūrat al-Ṭūr
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads wa-ʾatbaʿnāhum with ʾalif al-qaṭʿ and without a vowel on both the tāʾ and the ʿayn, and with nūn and an ʾalif after the nūn. The rest read it with ʾalif al-waṣl with fatḥah on both the tāʾ and the ʿayn, and with tāʾ without a vowel after the ʿayn (i.e., wa-ttabaʿathum(ū)). Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū ʿAmr read ḏurriyyātu/ihu/im bi-ʾīmāni in the plural. Ibn ʿĀmir places ḍammah on the tāʾ (i.e., ḏurriyyātuhum) and ʾAbū ʿAmr places kasrah on it (i.e., ḏurriyyātihim). The rest read it in the singular with rafʿ of the tāʾ (i.e., ḏurriyyatuhum(ū)). Ibn Kaṯīr reads wa-mā ʾa-litnāhumū with kasrah on the lām and the rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., ʾa-latnāhūm).

statements.heading: F.52. Sūrat al-Ṭūr
statements.text: lā laġwun/a fīhā wa-lā taʾṯīmun has already been mentioned.[389]

statements.heading: F.52. Sūrat al-Ṭūr
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read ʾannahū huwa l-barru with fatḥah on the hamzah and the rest with kasrah (i.e., ʾinnahū).

statements.heading: F.52. Sūrat al-Ṭūr
statements.text: Qunbul, Ḥafṣ, with some disagreement, and Hišām read al-musayṭirūna with sīn. Ḥamzah, with disagreement in the transmission of Ḫallād, reads it between the ṣād and the zāy (i.e., al-muẓayṭirūna). The rest read it with pure ṣād (i.e., al-muṣayṭirūna).

statements.heading: F.52. Sūrat al-Ṭūr
statements.text: ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read fīhi yuṣʿaqūna with ḍammah on the yāʾ and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., yaṣʿaqūna).

statements.heading: F.53. Sūrat al-Naǧm
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read the ends of the verses of this sūrah from His speech ʾiḏā hawē (Q53:1) up until His speech min an-nuḏuri l-ʾūlē (Q53:50) with ʾimālah. ʾAbū ʿAmr applies ʾimālah to whichever of these has rāʾ in it (e.g., al-ʾuḫrē Q53:47), and what remains in between (e.g., al-ʾūlǟ Q53:50). Warš made all of them in between (i.e., hawǟ, al‿uḫrǟ, al‿ūlǟ). The rest pronounced it with pure fatḥah (i.e., hawā, al-ʾuḫrā etc.).

statements.heading: F.53. Sūrat al-Naǧm
statements.text: Hišām reads mā kaḏḏaba l-fuʾādu with gemination of the ḏāl and the rest without gemination (i.e., kaḏaba).

statements.heading: F.53. Sūrat al-Naǧm
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ʾa-fa-tamrūnahū with fatḥah on the tāʾ and without a vowel on the mīm. The rest read it with ḍammah on the tāʾ, fatḥah on the mīm and with ʾalif after it (i.e., ʾa-fa-tumārūnahū).

statements.heading: F.53. Sūrat al-Naǧm
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads wa-manâʾata with length and hamzah. The rest read it without length and without hamzah (i.e., wa-manāta).

statements.heading: F.53. Sūrat al-Naǧm
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads wa-ḍiʾzā with hamzah and the rest without hamzah (i.e., wa-ḍīzā/ē/ǟ).

statements.heading: F.53. Sūrat al-Naǧm
statements.text: kabīra/kabāʾira l-ʾiṯmi,[390] fī buṭūni ʾu/immi/ahātikum(ū),[391] an-naš(ā)ʾata (Q53:47)[392] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.53. Sūrat al-Naǧm
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr read ʿādal⸗lū/uʾlā/ǟ with ḍammah on the lām, for the vowel of the hamzah (which has been dropped) and assimilation of the nūn to it (i.e., ʿādal⸗lūlǟ). For Qālūn, after the ḍammah of the lām comes a hamzah without vowel in place of the wāw (i.e., ʿādal⸗luʾlā). The rest applies kasrah to the tanwīn, no vowel to the lām and fully pronounce the hamzah after it (i.e., ʿādan il-ʾūlā/ē). Upon starting on the word al-ʾūlǟ, three options are allowed for ʾAbū ʿAmr. The first of these is #ʾalūlǟ with retention of the hamzat al-waṣl with ḍammah on the lām after it. The second is lūlǟ with ḍammah on the lām with removal of the hamzat al-waṣl before it, as there is no need for this (epenthetic) vowel. These two options are both allowed and this is similar in the manner of Warš. The third option is #al-ʾūlǟ with the addition of hamzat al-waṣl, no vowel on the lām and pronunciation of the hamzah as the first root letter after it. In the manner of Qālūn there are also three options: #ʾaluʾlā with ḍammah on the lām and retention of the hamzat al-waṣl and with hamzah without vowel in place of the wāw, #luʾlā with ḍammah on the lām, removal of the hamzat al-waṣl and hamzah on the wāw, and #ʾal-ʾūlā like the third option of ʾAbū ʿAmr. To me this is the best of these options and the most regular in their manners. I explain the reason why that is the case in Kitāb al-tamhīd.[393]

footnotes.text: This work by al-Dānī is known by its full title, Kitāb al-tamhīd fī qirāʾat Nāfiʿ, but it has not yet been published (al-Dānī 1995, 16).

statements.heading: F.53. Sūrat al-Naǧm
statements.text: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read wa-ṯamūda fa-mā without tanwīn and when pausing upon it without ʾalif (i.e., wa-ṯamūd#). The rest read it with tanwīn (i.e., wa-ṯamūdan) and when pausing on it with ʾalif (i.e., wa-ṯamūdā#).

statements.heading: F.54. Sūrat al-Qamar
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads ʾilā šayʾin nukrin with no vowel on the kāf and the rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., nukurin).

statements.heading: F.54. Sūrat al-Qamar
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ḫāšiʿan with fatḥah on the ḫāʾ, with ʾalif after it and with kasrah on the šīn. The rest read it with ḍammah on the ḫāʾ and fatḥah on a geminate šīn (i.e., ḫuššaʿan).

statements.heading: F.54. Sūrat al-Qamar
statements.text: fa-fat(t)aḥnā has already been mentioned.[394]

statements.heading: F.54. Sūrat al-Qamar
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamzah read sa-taʿlamūna ġadan with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., sa-yaʿlamūna).

statements.heading: F.54.1. [Removed yāʾs of Q54]
statements.text: There are eight removed ones: 1. yadʿu d-dāʿī (Q54:6) with retention (of the yāʾ) in both connected speech and pause by al-Bazzī, and with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Warš and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 2. ʾilà d-dāʿī (Q54:8) with retention in both connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr, and with retention in connected speech by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 3. ʿaḏābī wa-nuḏurī in six places (Q54:16, 4. 18, 5. 21, 6. 30, 7. 37, 8. 39) with retention in connected speech by Warš alone.

statements.heading: F.55. Sūrat al-Raḥmān
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads wa-l-ḥabba ḏà l-ʿaṣfi wa-r-rayḥāna with naṣb of the three nouns. Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-r-rayḥāni with ḫafḍ and what remains with rafʿ (i.e., wa-l-ḥabbu ḏù l-ʿaṣfi wa-r-rayḥāni). The rest read all three with rafʿ (i.e., wa-l-ḥabbu ḏù l-ʿaṣfi wa-rrayḥānu).[395]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 142).

statements.heading: F.55. Sūrat al-Raḥmān
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr read yuḫraǧu minhumā with ḍammah on the yāʾ and fatḥah on the rāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ and ḍammah on the rāʾ (i.e., yaḫruǧu).

statements.heading: F.55. Sūrat al-Raḥmān
statements.text: Ḥamzah and ʾAbū Bakr, with some disagreement, read al-munšiʾātu with kasrah on the šīn, and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., al-munšaʾātu).[396]

footnotes.text: Spelled اঐঔنشاتin modern print editions, but in early Qurʾānic manuscripts consistently spelled as اঐঔنشيت, a spelling that supports the minority reading better than the majority reading (van Putten 2022a, 315).

statements.heading: F.55. Sūrat al-Raḥmān
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read sa-yafruġu with yāʿ, and the rest with nūn (i.e., sa-nafruġu). ʾayyuha/u ṯ-ṯaqalāni has already been mentioned.[397]

statements.heading: F.55. Sūrat al-Raḥmān
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads šiwāḏ̣un with kasrah on the šīn and the rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., šuwāḏ̣un). Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read wa-nuḥāsin with ḫafḍ, and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., wa-nuḥāsun).

statements.heading: F.55. Sūrat al-Raḥmān
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿUmar [al-Dūrī], transmitting from al-Kisāʾī, reads lam yaṭmuṯhunna in the first attestation with ḍammah on the mīm and ʾAbū al-Ḥāriṯ transmitting from him (al-Kisāʾī) for the second (Q55:74), and that is my recitation. But what ʾAbū al-Ḥāriṯ transmits textually is like the transmission of al-Dūrī.[398] The rest read it with kasrah on the mīm for both (i.e., yaṭmiṯhunna).

footnotes.text: This opinion is transmitted through a riwāyah ʾisnād for ʾAbū al-Ḥāriṯ that is absent in the Taysīr; see Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 1622).

statements.heading: F.55. Sūrat al-Raḥmān
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads ḏù l-ǧalāli at the end (i.e., as opposed to the one at Q55:27) with wāw and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., ḏì l-ǧalāli).[399]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 142).

statements.heading: F.56. Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah
statements.text: The Kufans read wa-lā yunzifūna with kasrah on the zāy and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., yunzafūna).

statements.heading: F.56. Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-ḥūrin ʿīnin with ḫafḍ of both and the rest read it with rafʿ of both (i.e., wa-ḥūrun ʿīnun).

statements.heading: F.56. Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr and Ḥamzah read ʿurban with no vowel on the rāʾ and the rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., ʿuruban).

statements.heading: F.56. Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah
statements.text: The two interrogatives have already been mentioned in al-Raʿd,[400] except that Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read the first of the two as an interrogative and the second as a declarative. The rest read both as interrogatives, and they follow their principles in terms of pronouncing fully (the hamzah) or softening it. ʾaw(a) ʾābāʾunā has already been mentioned.[401]

statements.heading: F.56. Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read šurba l-hīmi with ḍammah on the šīn and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., šarba).

statements.heading: F.56. Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads naḥnu qadarnā without gemination of the dāl and the rest with gemination (i.e., qaddarnā).

statements.heading: F.56. Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah
statements.text: an-naš(ā)ʾata had already been mentioned.[402]

statements.heading: F.56. Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads ʾaʾinnā la-muġrimūna with two hamzahs and the rest with a single hamzah that carries a kasrah (i.e., ʾinnā).

statements.heading: F.56. Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read bi-mawqiʿi with no vowel on the wāw without ʾalif. The rest read it with fatḥah on the wāw and the ʾalif after it (i.e., bi-mawāqiʿi).

statements.heading: F.57. Sūrat al-Ḥadīd
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads wa-qad ʾuḫiḏa with ḍammah on the hamzah, kasrah on the ḫāʾ, and mīṯāqukum with rafʿ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the hamzah, with ḫāʾ and with naṣb (i.e., wa-qad ʾaḫaḏā mīṯāqakum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.57. Sūrat al-Ḥadīd
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads wa-kullun waʿada ḷḷāhu with rafʿ. The rest read it with naṣb (i.e., kullan).[403]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 147).

statements.heading: F.57. Sūrat al-Ḥadīd
statements.text: fa-yuḍāʿifahū/fa-yuḍaʿʿifahū has already been mentioned.[404]

statements.heading: F.57. Sūrat al-Ḥadīd
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads li-llaḏīna ʾāmanū ʾanḏ̣irūnā with hamzat al-qaṭʿ and fatḥah both when starting on it and in connected speech (fì l-ḥālayn), and kasrah on the ḏ̣āʾ. The rest read it with ʾalif al-waṣl and, if they start on it, with ḍammah and with ḍammah on the ḏ̣āʾ (i.e., unḏ̣urūnā).

statements.heading: F.57. Sūrat al-Ḥadīd
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads lā tuʾḫaḏu with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yuʾ/ūḫaḏu).

statements.heading: F.57. Sūrat al-Ḥadīd
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ read wa-mā nazala without gemination and the rest with gemination (i.e., nazzala).

statements.heading: F.57. Sūrat al-Ḥadīd
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū Bakr read al-muṣaddaqīna wa-l-muṣaddaqāti without gemination of the ṣād of both and the rest read them with gemination of both (i.e., al-muṣṣaddaqīna wa-l-muṣṣaddaqāti).

statements.heading: F.57. Sūrat al-Ḥadīd
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads bi-mā ʾatākum with shortness and the rest with length (i.e., ʾātā/ē/ǟkum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.57. Sūrat al-Ḥadīd
statements.text: bi-l-buḫli/baḫal[405] and ri/uḍwāni (Q57:27)[406] have already been mentioned. Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read fa-ʾinna ḷḷāha l-ġaniyyu without huwa, and the rest read it with the addition of huwa (i.e., fa-ʾinna ḷḷāha huwa l-ġaniyyu).[407]

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 142).

statements.heading: F.58. Sūrat al-Muǧādalah
statements.text: ʿĀṣim reads yuḏ̣āhirūna in two places (here and in Q58:3) with ḍammah, without gemination of the ḏ̣āʾ, with ʾalif after it and kasrah on the hāʾ. Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ and the hāʾ, and gemination of the ḏ̣āʾ with ʾalif after it (i.e., yaḏ̣ḏ̣āharūna). The rest read it with gemination of the ḏ̣āʾ and the hāʾ, with fatḥah on the yāʾ and without ʾalif (i.e., yaḏ̣ḏ̣ahharūna).

statements.heading: F.58. Sūrat al-Muǧādalah
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads wa-yantaǧūna with a nūn that does not carry a vowel after the yāʾ and with ḍammah on the ǧīm. The rest read it with a tāʾ that carries a fatḥah between the yāʾ and the nūn, with ʾalif after the nūn and fatḥah on the ǧīm (i.e., yatanāǧawna).

statements.heading: F.58. Sūrat al-Muǧādalah
statements.text: ʿĀṣim reads fì l-maǧālisi with ʾalif in the plural and the rest without ʾalif in the singular (i.e., al-maǧlisi). Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim, with disagreement in transmission from ʾAbū Bakr, read unšuzū fa-nšuzū with ḍammah on the šīn for both and, when starting on it, with ḍammah on the ʾalif (i.e., #unšuzū). The rest read it with kasrah on the šīn and, when starting on it, with kasrah on the ʾalif (i.e., #inšizū, fa-nšizū). I have recited it with this option for ʾAbū Bakr in the path of al-Ṣarīfīnī transmitting from Yaḥyā [b. ʾĀdam] from him for both (words).[408]

footnotes.text: This is the tilāwah ʾisnād listed in U.4.5.1. But the reading unšuzū fa-nšuzū is not transmitted along the riwāyah ʾisnād listed in that section; see Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 1632).

statements.heading: F.58.1. [Yāʾ of Q58]
statements.text: There is one yāʾ: wa-rusuliya ʾinna ḷḷāha (Q58:21) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir.

statements.heading: F.59. Sūrat al-Ḥašr
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads yuḫarribūna with gemination and the rest without gemination (i.e., yuḫribūna). ar-ruʿ(u)ba has already been mentioned.[409]

statements.heading: F.59. Sūrat al-Ḥašr
statements.text: Hišām reads kay lā takūna with tāʾ—it was also transmitted from him with yāʾ (i.e., kay lā yakūna)—and dūlatun with rafʿ (with both options). The rest read it with yāʾ and with naṣb (i.e., kay lā yakūna dūlatan).

statements.heading: F.59. Sūrat al-Ḥašr
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read ǧidā/ērin with kasra on the ǧīm and ʾalif after the dāl, and ʾAbū ʿAmr applies ʾimālah to the fatḥah of the dāl (i.e., ǧidērin).[410] The rest read ǧudurin with ḍammah on the ǧīm and dāl.

footnotes.text: In accordance with his general principle, see U.13.4.

statements.heading: F.59. Sūrat al-Ḥašr
statements.text: al-bā/ēriʾu has already been mentioned in (the chapter on) ʾimālah.[411]

statements.heading: F.59.1. [Yāʾ of Q59]
statements.text: There is one yāʾ: ʾinnī ʾaḫāfu (Q59:16) with no vowel by the Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir.

statements.heading: F.60. Sūrat al-Muttaḥanah
statements.text: ʿĀṣim reads yafṣilu baynakum with fatḥah on the yāʾ, no vowel on the fāʾ and kasrah on ungeminated ṣād. Ibn ʿĀmir reads yufaṣṣalu with ḍammah on the yāʾ, fatḥah on the fāʾ and geminated ṣād. Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read it like that except that they place kasrah on the ṣād (i.e., yufaṣṣilu). The rest read it with ḍammah on the yāʾ, no vowel on the fāʾ and fatḥah on ungeminated ṣād (i.e., yufṣalu).

statements.heading: F.60. Sūrat al-Muttaḥanah
statements.text: ʾu/iswatun ḥasanatun in two places has already been mentioned.[412]

statements.heading: F.60. Sūrat al-Muttaḥanah
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads lā tumassikū with gemination and the rest without gemination (i.e., lā tumsikū).

statements.heading: F.61. Sūrat al-Ṣaff
statements.text: I have already mentioned hāḏā sāḥirun/siḥrun.[413]

statements.heading: F.61. Sūrat al-Ṣaff
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read mutimmu without tanwīn and nūrihī with ḫafḍ. The rest read it with tanwīn and naṣb (i.e., mutimmun nūrahū).

statements.heading: F.61. Sūrat al-Ṣaff
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads tunaǧǧīkum with gemination and the rest without gemination (i.e., tunǧīkum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.61. Sūrat al-Ṣaff
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read ʾanṣāra ḷḷāhi without tanwīn and without lām. The rest read it with tanwīn and with a lām that carries a kasrah at the beginning of the name of God Almighty (i.e., ʾanṣāran li-llāhi).[414]

footnotes.text: This represents a reanalysis of the position of the word boundary, which is ambiguous in the Arabic script, where originally the space between words and between non-connected letters was identical ჭጅانصارال.

statements.heading: F.61.1. [Yāʾs of Q61]
statements.text: There are two yāʾs: 1. min baʿdì smuhū (Q61:6) without a vowel by Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī. 2. min ʾanṣāriya ʾilà ḷḷāhi (Q61:14) with fatḥah by Nāfiʿ.

statements.heading: F.62. There Is No Disagreement in Sūrat al-Ǧumuʿah
statements.text: Except for what has preceded about ʾimālah and such.

statements.heading: F.63. Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn
statements.text: Qunbul, ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read ḫušbun with no vowel on the šīn and the rest read it with ḍammah (i.e., ḫušubun).

statements.heading: F.63. Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads lawaw with no gemination of the wāw and the rest with gemination (i.e., lawwaw).

statements.heading: F.63. Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads wa-ʾakūna with wāw and naṣb of the nūn. The rest read it without wāw and with ǧazm of the nūn (i.e., wa-ʾakun).[415]

footnotes.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr’s reading disagrees with the rasm اكن.

statements.heading: F.63. Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads bi-mā yaʿmalūna at the end (i.e., not the one at Q63:2) with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taʿmalūna).

statements.heading: F.64. Sūrat al-Taġābun
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read nukaffir ʿanhu and wa-nudḫilhu with nūn in both and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yukaffir ʿanhū̆ and wa-yudḫilhū̆).

statements.heading: F.64. Sūrat al-Taġābun
statements.text: We have already mentioned yuḍāʿifhu/yuḍaʿʿifhu.[416]

statements.heading: F.65. Sūrat al-Ṭalāq
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads bāliġu without tanwīn and ʾamrihī with ḫafḍ. The rest read it with tanwīn and naṣb of ʾamrahū (i.e., bāliġun ʾamrahū).

statements.heading: F.65. Sūrat al-Ṭalāq
statements.text: mubayyinatin,[417] wa-llāʾī (Q65:4),[418] nuk(u)ran (Q65:8),[419] mubayyinātin (Q65:11)[420] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.65. Sūrat al-Ṭalāq
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read nudḫilhu with nūn, and the rest read it with yāʾ (i.e., yudḫilhū̆).

statements.heading: F.66. Sūrat al-Taḥrīm
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads ʿarafa baʿḍahū without gemination of the rāʾ and the rest with gemination (i.e., ʿarrafa).

statements.heading: F.66. Sūrat al-Taḥrīm
statements.text: wa-ʾin taḏ̣(ḏ̣)āharā,[421] ǧibrīlu/ǧabrīlu/ǧabraʾilu/ǧabraʾīlu,[422] yubdilahū/yubaddilahū[423] (Q66:5) have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.66. Sūrat al-Taḥrīm
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr reads nuṣūḥan with ḍammah on the nūn and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., naṣūḥan).

statements.heading: F.66. Sūrat al-Taḥrīm
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ read wa-kutubihī in the plural and the rest in the singular (i.e., wa-kitābihī).

statements.heading: F.67. Sūrat al-Mulk
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read min tafawwutin with gemination of the wāw without ʾalif. The rest read it with ʾalif and without gemination of the wāw (i.e., tafāwutin).

statements.heading: F.67. Sūrat al-Mulk
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads fa-suḥuqan with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and the rest without a vowel (i.e., fa-suḥqan).

statements.heading: F.67. Sūrat al-Mulk
statements.text: Qunbul reads an-nušūru // wa-.amintumū with replacement of the hamzah of the interrogative with a wāw that carries a fatḥah in connected speech, and he lengthens what comes after with length equivalent to an ʾalif (i.e., pronounced bayna bayn). When he starts on it, he pronounces the hamzah fully (i.e., ʾa-.amintumū). The Kūfans and Ibn Ḏakwān pronounce the two hamzahs fully (i.e., ʾa-ʾamintum), and the rest soften the second (i.e., ʾa-.amintum). Al-Bazzī, in accordance with his general principle, does not introduce an ʾalif before it (i.e., ʾa-.amintumū), and this is likewise for Warš in accordance with his principle (i.e., ʾāmintum or ʾa-.amintum). The rest read it in accordance with their principles (i.e., ʾā-.amintum).[424]

statements.heading: F.67. Sūrat al-Mulk
statements.text: sī/ǖʾat has already been mentioned.[425]

statements.heading: F.67. Sūrat al-Mulk
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads fa-sa-yaʿlamūna man huwa with yāʾ and this is the last one (that occurs in this sūrah). The rest read it with tāʾ (i.e., fa-sa-taʿlamūna). There is no disagreement on the first (Q67:17, all read it fa-sa-taʿlamūna).

statements.heading: F.67.1. [Yāʾs of Q67]
statements.text: There are two yāʾs: 1. ʾin ʾahlaknì llāhu (Q67:28) without a vowel by Ḥamzah. 2. wa-man maʿī ʾaw (Q67:28) without a vowel by ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī.

statements.heading: F.67.2. [Removed yāʾs of Q67]
statements.text: There are two removed ones: 1. naḏīrī (Q67:17) and 2. nakīrī (Q67:18) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Warš.

statements.heading: F.68. Sūrat Nūn al-Qalam
statements.text: We have already mentioned the non-assimilation and assimilation of nūn wa-l-qalami/nūw̃⸗wa-l-qalami.[426]

statements.heading: F.68. Sūrat Nūn al-Qalam
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr and Ḥamzah read ʾa-ʾan kāna with two hamzahs pronounced fully. Ibn ʿĀmir reads it with hamzah and length (i.e., ʾā̆-.an kāna). Ibn Ḏakwān is different from Hišām in terms of lengthening and that is why we have mentioned it in Fuṣṣilat[427] (i.e., Ibn Ḏakwān: ʾā-.an kāna and Hišām: ʾa-.an kāna). The rest read it with a single hamzah that carries a fatḥah, as a declarative (i.e., ʾan).

statements.heading: F.68. Sūrat Nūn al-Qalam
statements.text: ʾan yubdilanā/yubaddilanā has already been mentioned.[428]

statements.heading: F.68. Sūrat Nūn al-Qalam
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads la-yazliqūnaka with fatḥah and the rest with ḍammah (i.e., yuzliqūnaka).

statements.heading: F.69. Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah
statements.text: [429] ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read wa-man qibalahū with kasrah on the qāf and fatḥah on the bāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the qāf and no vowel on the bāʾ (i.e., qablahū).

statements.heading: F.69. Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah
statements.text: ʾuḏ(u)nun wāʿiyatun has already been mentioned.[430] All of them read wa-taʿiyahā with kasrah on the ʿayn, fatḥah on the yāʾ and no gemination. However, some reports from Ibn Kaṯīr, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah about that are incorrect.[431]

footnotes.text: While not explicit, the incorrect readings al-Dānī is referring to are taʿyahā (Ibn Kaṯīr), taʿiyyahā (ʿĀṣim) and taʿĭyahā (Ḥamzah) (al-Dānī 2007, 1652–54).

statements.heading: F.69. Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read lā yaḫfē minkum with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taḫfā/ǟ).

statements.heading: F.69. Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads ʿannī māliya and ʿannī sulṭāniya with removal of the hāʾ in connected speech, and the rest read it with retention in both connected speech and pause (i.e., māliyah(#), sulṭāniyah(#)).

statements.heading: F.69. Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read both qalīlan mā yuʾminūna and qalīlan mā yaḏḏakkarūna with yāʾ. The rest read it with tāʾ (i.e., tuʾ/ūminūna, ta(ḏ)ḏakkarūna), and al-Naqqāš said it was transmitted from al-ʾAḫfaš from Ibn Ḏakwān like that (i.e., with tāʾ).

statements.heading: F.70. Sūrat al-Maʿāriǧ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read sāla with ʾalif without a vowel replacing the hamzah and the replacement is received by audition (as it is irregular, the regular form would be sa.ala).[432] The rest read it with hamzah (i.e., saʾala). Ḥamzah makes it in between in pause (i.e., sa.al#).

footnotes.text: Cf. the similar wording in F.34:14. for the similarly irregular shift of aʾa → ā, rather than the regular softening aʾa → a.a.

statements.heading: F.70. Sūrat al-Maʿāriǧ
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads yaʿruǧu with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., taʿruǧu).

statements.heading: F.70. Sūrat al-Maʿāriǧ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read min ʿaḏābi yawmaʾiḏin with fatḥah on the mīm and the rest with ḫafḍ (i.e., min ʿaḏābi yawmiʾiḏīn).

statements.heading: F.70. Sūrat al-Maʿāriǧ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī apply ʾimālah to laḏ̣ē, li-š-šawē (Q70:16), wa-tawallē (Q70:17) and fa-ʾawʿē (Q70:18) in accordance with their general principles.[433] Warš and ʾAbū ʿAmr read it in between (i.e., laḏ̣ǟ, etc.) and the rest read it with the pure pronunciation of the fatḥah (i.e., laḏ̣ā, etc.).

statements.heading: F.70. Sūrat al-Maʿāriǧ
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads nazzāʿatan with naṣb and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., nazzāʿatun).

statements.heading: F.70. Sūrat al-Maʿāriǧ
statements.text: li-ʾamāna/ātihim has already been mentioned.[434]

statements.heading: F.70. Sūrat al-Maʿāriǧ
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads bi-šahādātihim with ʾalif as a plural and the rest without ʾalif (i.e., bi-šahādatihim(ū)).

statements.heading: F.70. Sūrat al-Maʿāriǧ
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read ʾilā nuṣubin with ḍammah on the nūn and the ṣād. The rest read it with fatḥah on the nūn and no vowel on the ṣād (i.e., naṣbin).

statements.heading: F.71. Sūrat Nūḥ (s)
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read wa-waladuhū with fatḥah on the wāw and the lām. The rest read it with ḍammah on the wāw and no vowel on the lām (i.e., wa-wulduhū).

statements.heading: F.71. Sūrat Nūḥ (s)
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads wuddan with ḍammah on the wāw and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., waddan).

statements.heading: F.71. Sūrat Nūḥ (s)
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads mimmā ḫaṭāyāhum like the word qaḍāyāhum and the rest read it with yāʾ, tāʾ and hamzah (i.e., ḫaṭīʾātihim(ū)).

statements.heading: F.71.1. [Yāʾs of Q71]
statements.text: There are three yāʾs: 1. duʿāʾī ʾillā (Q71:6) without vowel by the Kufans. 2. ṯumma ʾinnī ʾaʿlantu (Q71:9) without vowel by the Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir. 3. baytiya muʾminan (Q71:28) with fatḥah by Ḥafṣ and Hišām.

statements.heading: F.72. Sūrat al-Ǧinn
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read fatḥah on the hamzah of wa-ʾannahū, wa-ʾannā, wa-ʾannahum from the words of the Almighty wa-ʾannahū taʿālē/ā ǧaddu rabbinā (Q72:4) up until His words wa-ʾannā minnà l-muslimūna, at the beginning of each verse. The rest read them with kasrah (i.e., wa-ʾinnahū, wa-ʾinnā and wa-ʾinnahum(ū)).

statements.heading: F.72. Sūrat al-Ǧinn
statements.text: The Kufans read yaslukhu with yāʾ and the rest with nūn (i.e., naslukhū̆).

statements.heading: F.72. Sūrat al-Ǧinn
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū Bakr read wa-ʾinnahū lammā with kasrah on the hamzah and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., wa-ʾannahū). Hišām reads ʿalayhi lubadan with ḍammah on the lām and the rest with kasrah (i.e., libadan).

statements.heading: F.72. Sūrat al-Ǧinn
statements.text: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read qul ʾinnamā ʾadʿū without ʾalif and the rest read qāla with ʾalif.

statements.heading: F.72.1. [Yāʾ of Q72]
statements.text: There is one yāʾ: rabbiya ʾamadan (Q72:25) with fatḥah by the two of the holy cities and ʾAbū ʿAmr.

statements.heading: F.73. Sūrat al-Muzzammil
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read ʾašaddu wiṭâʾan with kasrah on the wāw and fatḥah on the ṭāʾ with length. The rest read it with faṭhah on the wāw and no vowel on the ṭāʾ (i.e., waṭʾan).

statements.heading: F.73. Sūrat al-Muzzammil
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read rabbi l-mašriqi with ḫafḍ of the bāʾ and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., rabbu).

statements.heading: F.73. Sūrat al-Muzzammil
statements.text: Hišām reads min ṯulṯay il-layli without vowel on the lām and the rest with ḍammah (i.e., ṯuluṯay). The Kufans and Ibn Kaṯīr read wa-niṣfahū wa-ṯuluṯahū with naṣb of the fāʾ and the ṯāʾ. The rest read it with ḫafḍ of both (i.e., wa-niṣfihī wa-ṯuluṯihī).

statements.heading: F.74. Sūrat al-Muddaṯṯir
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads wa-r-ruǧza with ḍammah on the rāʾ and the rest with kasrah (i.e., wa-rriǧza).

statements.heading: F.74. Sūrat al-Muddaṯṯir
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ḥafṣ and Ḥamzah wa-l-layli ʾiḏ with no vowel on the ḏāl and ʾadbara in the pattern ʾafʿala. The rest read ʾiḏā with ʾalif after the ḏāl and dabara in the pattern faʿala (i.e., ʾiḏā dabara).[435]

footnotes.text: This represents two different interpretations of the rasm ޻ޙاذاد, where the place of the word boundary is ambiguous. In historical Arabic scripts the space between non-connected letters and word boundaries is identical.

statements.heading: F.74. Sūrat al-Muddaṯṯir
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read mustanfaratun with fatḥah on the fāʾ and the rest with kasrah (i.e., mustanfiratun).

statements.heading: F.74. Sūrat al-Muddaṯṯir
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads wa-mā taḏkurūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yaḏkurūna).

statements.heading: F.75. Sūrat al-Qiyāmah
statements.text: Qunbul reads la-ʾuqsimu bi-yawmi without ʾalif, and al-Naqqāš transmits it like that from ʾAbū Rabīʿah from al-Bazzī. The rest read it with ʾalif (i.e., lā ʾuqsimu).[436] There is no disagreement on the second (Q75:2, all read it wa-lā ʾuqsimu).

footnotes.text: This is the result of an unusual ancient orthographic practice of early Islamic Arabic where the asseverative la- may be written with a জগ before a word that starts with a hamzah. Other cases of this are attested throughout the Qurʾān (see Q27:21 গজاذ๷චنه la-ʾaḏbaḥannahū). For a discussion on more

statements.heading: F.75. Sūrat al-Qiyāmah
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads fa-ʾiḏā baraqa with fatḥah on the rāʾ and the rest read it with kasrah (i.e., bariqa).

statements.heading: F.75. Sūrat al-Qiyāmah
statements.text: The Kufans and Nāfiʿ read bal tuḥibbūna and wa-taḏarūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yuḥibbūna, yaḏarūna).

statements.heading: F.75. Sūrat al-Qiyāmah
statements.text: man rāqin[437] and sudan (sudē/ǟ/ā# Q75:36)[438] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.75. Sūrat al-Qiyāmah
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads min maniyyin yumnā with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tumnā/ē/ǟ). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī applied ʾimālah to all the ends of the verses of this sūrah from His speech wa-lā ṣallē (Q75:31) up until the end. Warš and ʾAbū ʿAmr pronounced it in between (wa-lā ṣallǟ, etc.). The rest read it with pure fatḥah.

statements.heading: F.76. Sūrat al-ʾInsān
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī, ʾAbū Bakr and Hišām read salāsilan with tanwīn and pause on it with an ʿalif replacing it (i.e., salāsilā#). The rest read it without tanwīn (i.e., salāsila). Ḥamzah, Qunbul and Ḥafṣ, in my recitation to ʾAbū al-Fatḥ,[439] pause on it without ʾalif (i.e., salāsil#). Al-Naqqāš says it is like that, transmitting from ʾAbū Rabīʿah from al-Bazzī and transmitting from al-ʾAḫfaš from Ibn Ḏakwān, and I recited it like that in their tradition to al-Fārisī. The rest pause upon it with the addition of an ʾalif to the fatḥah (i.e., salāsilā#).[440]

footnotes.text: This transmission path is not included in U.4.5.2. It is present in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān (al-Dānī 2007, 360–62).
The rasm of this word is ௌேسلس, as if the noun were a triptote.

statements.heading: F.76. Sūrat al-ʾInsān
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī and ʾAbū Bakr read qawārīran // qawārīran both with tanwīn and, when they pause on either of these two, they do so with an ʾalif (i.e., qawārīrā#). Ibn Kaṯīr reads the first with tanwīn and pauses upon it with ʾalif (i.e., Q76:15 qawārīran/qawārīrā#) and he reads the second without ʾalif and pauses upon it without ʾalif (i.e., Q76:16 qawārīra/qawārīr#). The rest read it without tanwīn on either (i.e., qawārīra) and Ḥamzah pauses on both without ʾalif (i.e., qawārīr#). Ḥišām pauses upon them with a ṣilah of the ʾalif to the fatḥah (i.e., qawārīrā#). The rest—they are ʾAbū ʿAmr, Ḥafṣ, Ibn Ḏakwān—pause on the first one with ʾalif (i.e., Q76:15 qawārīrā#) and on the second without ʾalif (i.e., Q76:16 qawārīr#).[441] So, one can surmise from this that whoever does not apply tanwīn pauses on the first with ʾalif except Ḥamzah and (whoever does not apply tanwīn pauses) on the second without ʾalif except Hišām.

footnotes.text: Similar to the case in the previous footnote, the rasm of these words ( )قوارޒ޻اunexpectedly suggests a triptotic reading. Some reports on regional rasm variants suggest that the second instance is spelled without ʾalif, i.e., ޻ޒقوار. This seems to explain the differential treatment of the two verses in pause found with Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr, Ḥafṣ and Ibn Ḏakwān (Sidky 2020, 176–77).

statements.heading: F.76. Sūrat al-ʾInsān
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ḥamzah read ʿālīhim without a vowel on the yāʾ and with kasrah on the hāʾ. The rest read it with fatḥah on the yāʾ and ḍammah on the hāʾ (i.e., ʿāliyahum(ū)). Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ read both ḫuḍrun wa-ʾistabraqun with rafʿ. Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū Bakr read the first with ḫafḍ and the second with rafʿ (i.e., ḫuḍrin wa-ʾistabraqun). Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū ʿAmr read the first with rafʿ and the second with ḫafḍ (i.e., ḫuḍrun wa-ʾistabraqin). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read both with ḫafḍ (i.e., ḫuḍrin wa-ʾistabraqin).

statements.heading: F.76. Sūrat al-ʾInsān
statements.text: The Kufans and Nāfiʿ read wa-mā tašāʾūna with tāʾ and the rest with yāʾ (i.e., yašāʾūna).

statements.heading: F.77. Sūrat al-Mursalāt
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḫallād read fa-l-mulqiyāḏ⸗ḏikran and likewise fa-l-muġīraṣ⸗ṣubḥan (Q100:3) with assimilation and it has already been mentioned.[442]

statements.heading: F.77. Sūrat al-Mursalāt
statements.text: The two of the holy cities, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʾAbū Bakr read wa-nuḏuran with ḍammah on the ḏāl and the rest read it without vowel (i.e., wa-nuḏran).

statements.heading: F.77. Sūrat al-Mursalāt
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads wuqqitat with wāw and the rest with hamzah (i.e., ʾuqqitat).[443]

footnotes.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr’s reading disagrees with the rasm اقتت.

statements.heading: F.77. Sūrat al-Mursalāt
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read fa-qaddarnā with gemination of the dāl and the rest without gemination (i.e., fa-qadarnā).

statements.heading: F.77. Sūrat al-Mursalāt
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ǧimālatun in the singular without ʾalif and the rest read it with ʾalif (i.e., ǧimālātun).

statements.heading: F.78.–F.89. From Sūrat al-Nabaʾ to Sūrat al-Balad [F.78. Al-Nabaʾ]
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads labiṯīna fīhā without ʾalif, the rest with ʾalif (i.e., lābiṯīna).

statements.heading: F.78.–F.89. From Sūrat al-Nabaʾ to Sūrat al-Balad [F.78. Al-Nabaʾ]
statements.text: wa-fut(t)iḥat is-samāʾu[444] and ġas(s)āqan (Q78:25)[445] have already been mentioned.

statements.heading: F.78.–F.89. From Sūrat al-Nabaʾ to Sūrat al-Balad [F.78. Al-Nabaʾ]
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads wa-lā kiḏāban without gemination of the ḏāl and the rest with gemination (i.e., kiḏḏāban). There is no disagreement on the first attestation (Q78:28, all read kiḏḏāban).

statements.heading: F.78.–F.89. From Sūrat al-Nabaʾ to Sūrat al-Balad [F.78. Al-Nabaʾ]
statements.text: The Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir read rabbi s-samāwāti with ḫafḍ. ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read wa-mā baynahumà r-raḥmāni with ḫafḍ. The rest read the two nouns with rafʿ (i.e., rabbu, r-raḥmānu).

statements.heading: F.79. Wa-l-Nāziʿāti
statements.text: I have already mentioned about the two interrogatives in (the discussion in) al-Raʿd[446] that Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read the first of these two as an interrogative and the second as a declarative (i.e., ʾā̆ʾ/.innā … // ʾiḏā), while the rest read both as an interrogative (ʾā̆.innā … // ʾā̆.iḏā). They followed their manners in pronouncing strongly or weakly (of the hamzah).[447] ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read nāḫiratan with ʾalif and the rest without ʾalif (i.e., naḫiratan).

statements.heading: F.79. Wa-l-Nāziʿāti
statements.text: ṭuwà // ḏhab/ṭuwan // iḏhab have already been mentioned.[448]

statements.heading: F.79. Wa-l-Nāziʿāti
statements.text: The two of the holy cities read ʾan tazzakkā/ǟ with gemination of the zāy and the rest without gemination (i.e., tazakkā/ǟ/ē). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī apply ʾimālah to the ends of the verses of this sūrah starting from His word hal ʾatēka ḥadīṯu mūsē (Q79:15) up until the end, except in His speech ḍaḥā/ēhā (Q79:3) to which Ḥamzah applied pure fatḥah. Warš reads all of those which have the hāʾ and ʾalif (i.e., -hā) with pure fatḥah except in His speech ḏikrǟhā (Q79:43). He reads that in between because of the rāʾ. ʾAbū ʿAmr reads all that has rāʾ in it with ʾimālah (i.e., Q79:20, 34 al-kubrē; Q79:36 yarē; Q79:43 ḏikrēhā) and whatever remains in between (i.e., Q79:15 mūsǟhā; Q79:44 muntahǟhā, etc.). The rest read it with pure fatḥah for all (i.e., mūsā, muntahāhā, al-kubrā, yarā, ḏikrāhā, etc.).

statements.heading: F.80. ʿAbasa
statements.text: ʿĀṣim reads fa-tanfaʿahū with naṣb of the ʿayn, and the rest read it with rafʿ (i.e., fa-tanfaʿuhū).

statements.heading: F.80. ʿAbasa
statements.text: The two of the holy cities read lahū taṣṣaddā/ǟ with gemination of the ṣād and the rest without gemination (i.e., taṣaddā/ē/ǟ).

statements.heading: F.80. ʿAbasa
statements.text: The Kufans read ʾannā ṣababnā with fatḥah on the hamzah and the rest with kasrah (i.e., ʾinnā). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī apply ʾimālah to the ends of the verses of this sūrah from the beginning up until His speech talahhē (Q80:10). ʾAbū ʿAmr applies ʾimālah to aḏ-ḏikrē (Q80:4) and what remains he pronounces in between (i.e., talahhǟ, etc.). Warš pronounces all of them in between (i.e., talahhǟ, aḏ-ḏikrǟ, etc.). The rest pronounce them with pure fatḥ (i.e., talahhā, aḏ-ḏikrā, etc.).

statements.heading: F.81. Al-Takwīr
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read suǧirat without gemination of the ǧīm and the rest with gemination (i.e., suǧǧirat).

statements.heading: F.81. Al-Takwīr
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, Ḥafṣ and Ibn Ḏakwān read suʿʿirat with gemination and the rest without gemination (i.e., suʿirat).

statements.heading: F.81. Al-Takwīr
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read bi-ḏ̣anīnin with ḏ̣āʾ and the rest read it with ḍād (i.e., bi-ḍanīnin).[449]

footnotes.text: The reading bi-ḏ̣anīnin contradicts the rasm بضنഽن.

statements.heading: F.82. Al-Infiṭār
statements.text: The Kufans read fa-ʿadalaka without gemination and the rest read it with gemination (i.e., fa-ʿaddalaka).

statements.heading: F.82. Al-Infiṭār
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read yawmu lā tamliku with rafʿ of the mīm and the rest with naṣb (i.e., yawma).

statements.heading: F.83. Al-Taṭfīf
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read bal rēna with ʾimālah of the fatḥah of the rāʾ. The rest read it with a back vowel (i.e., ṛāna). Ḥafṣ introduces a short silence on the lām of bal, as we have already mentioned.[450]

statements.heading: F.83. Al-Taṭfīf
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads ḫātimuhū with ʾalif after the ḫāʾ. The rest read it with kasrah on the ḫāʾ and ʾalif after the tāʾ (i.e., ḫitāmuhū).

statements.heading: F.83. Al-Taṭfīf
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads fakihīna here (i.e., not at Q44:27 or Q52:18) without ʾalif and the rest with ʾalif (i.e., fākihīna).

statements.heading: F.84. Al-Inšiqāq
statements.text: ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah and ʾAbū ʿAmr read wa-yaṣlā/ē saʿīran with fatḥah on the yāʾ, without a vowel on the ṣād and without gemination. The rest read it with ḍammah on the yāʾ, fatḥah on a ṣād and with gemination of the lām (i.e., yuṣallā/ē/ǟ).

statements.heading: F.84. Al-Inšiqāq
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read la-tarkabanna with fatḥah on the bāʾ and the rest with ḍammah (i.e., la-tarkabunna).

statements.heading: F.85. Al-Burūǧ
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ḏù l-ʿarši l-maǧīdi with ḫafḍ of the dāl and the rest with rafʿ (i.e., ḏù l-ʿarši l-maǧīdu).

statements.heading: F.85. Al-Burūǧ
statements.text: Nāfiʿ reads maḥfūḏ̣un with rafʿ of the ḏ̣āʾ and the rest with ḫafḍ (i.e., maḥfūḏ̣in).

statements.heading: F.86. Al-Ṭāriq
statements.text: ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamzah read lammā ʿalayhā with gemination of the mīm. The rest read it without gemination (i.e., lamā ʿalayhā); this has already been mentioned.[451]

statements.heading: F.87. Al-ʾAʿlā Almighty
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads wa-llaḏī qadara without gemination of the dāl and the rest read it with gemination (i.e., qaddara).

statements.heading: F.87. Al-ʾAʿlā Almighty
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads bal yuʾ/ūṯirūna with yāʾ and the rest with tāʾ (i.e., tuʾ/ūṯirūna). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī apply ʾimālah to the end of the verses of this complete sūrah (al-ʾaʿlē, etc.). Warš pronounces them in between (i.e., al‿aʿlǟ, etc.). ʾAbū ʿAmr applies ʾimālah to aḏ-ḏikrē (Q87:9), li-l-yusrē (Q87:8) and al-kubrē (Q87:12), and what remains he pronounces in between (i.e., al-ʾaʿlǟ, etc.). The rest pronounce it with pure fatḥ (i.e., al-ʾaʿlā, etc.).

statements.heading: F.88. Al-Ġāšiyah
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read tuṣlā nāran with ḍammah on the tāʾ and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., taṣlā/ē/ǟ).

statements.heading: F.88. Al-Ġāšiyah
statements.text: min ʿaynin ʾē/āniyatin is mentioned in the chapter on ʾimālah.[452]

statements.heading: F.88. Al-Ġāšiyah
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr and ʾAbū ʿAmr read lā yusmaʿu with yāʾ that carries ḍammah and lāġiyatun with rafʿ. Nāfiʿ reads it similarly, but he reads it with tāʾ (i.e., lā tusmaʿu lāġiyatun). The rest read it with a tāʾ that carries a fatḥah and lāġiyatan with naṣb (i.e., lā tasmaʿu lāġiyatan).

statements.heading: F.88. Al-Ġāšiyah
statements.text: Hišām reads bi-musayṭirin with sīn.[453] Ḥamzah, with disagreement in transmission from him through Ḫallād, reads it in between the ṣād and the zāy (bi-muẓayṭirin). The rest read it with pure ṣād (i.e., muṣayṭirin).

statements.heading: F.89. Al-Faǧr
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read wa-l-witri with kasrah on the wāw and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., wa-l-watri).

statements.heading: F.89. Al-Faǧr
statements.text: ʾAbū ʿAmr reads lā yukrimūna, lā yaḥuḍḍūna (Q89:18), wa-yaʾ/ākulūna (Q89:19) and wa-yuḥibbūna (Q89:20) with yāʾ of all four. The rest read it with tāʾ (i.e., lā tukrimūna, lā taḥu/āḍḍūna, wa-taʾ/ākulūna, wa-tuḥibbūna). The Kufans read wa-lā taḥāḍḍūna with ʾalif and the rest without ʾalif (i.e., y/taḥuḍḍūna).

statements.heading: F.89. Al-Faǧr
statements.text: wa-ǧǖ/īʾa yawmaʾiḏin has already been mentioned.[454]

statements.heading: F.89. Al-Faǧr
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads lā yuʿaḏḏabu (Q89:25) and wa-lā yūṯaqu (Q89:26) with fatḥah on the ḏāl and ṯāʾ. The rest read it with kasrah (i.e., yuʿaḏḏibu and yūṯiqu).

statements.heading: F.89.1. [Yāʾs of Q89]
statements.text: There are two yāʾs: 1. rabbī ʾakramani (Q89:15) and 2. rabbī ʾahānani (Q89:16) with no vowel on both by the Kufans and Ibn ʿĀmir.

statements.heading: F.89.2. [Removed yāʾs of Q89]
statements.text: There are four removed ones: 1. ʾiḏā yasrī (Q89:4) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech and pause by Ibn Kaṯīr and retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Nāfiʿ and ʾAbū ʿAmr. 2. bi-l-wāḏī (Q89:9) with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech and pause by al-Bazzī and retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Warš and Qunbul. It has also been transmitted from Qunbul with retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech and pause. 3. ʾakramanī (Q89:15) and 4. ʾahānanī (Q89:16) with retention (of the yāʾ) in both connected speech and pause by al-Bazzī and retention (of the yāʾ) in connected speech by Nāfiʿ. ʾAbū ʿAmr gave the choice (to either retain or remove the yāʾ) for these two (i.e., ʾakramanī/i and ʾahānanī/i). His regular treatment is that at the ends of the verse he removes (the yāʾ) (i.e., ʾahānani and ʾarkamanani). This is what I recited it and adopt.

statements.heading: F.90.–F.114. From Sūrat al-Balad up to the End of the Qurʾān [F.90. Al-Balad]
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr, ʾAbū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read fakka with fatḥah on the kāf, raqabatan with naṣb and ʾaw ʾaṭʿama with fatḥah on the hamzah, removal of the ʾalif after the ʿayn and fatḥah on the mīm without tanwīn (i.e., fakka raqabatan // ʾaw ʾaṭʿama). The rest read it with rafʿ of the kāf (i.e., fakku), ḫafḍ (of raqabatin) and kasrah on the hamzah, ʾalif after the ʿayn and rafʿ of the mīm with tanwīn (i.e., fakku raqabatin // (ʾ)aw (ʾ)iṭʿāmun).

statements.heading: F.90.–F.114. From Sūrat al-Balad up to the End of the Qurʾān [F.90. Al-Balad]
statements.text: Ḥafṣ, ʾAbū ʿAmr and Ḥamzah read muʾṣadatun here and in al-Humazah (Q104:8) with hamzah. Ḥamzah, when he pauses on it, replaces it with wāw (i.e., mūṣadah#). The rest read it without hamzah (i.e., mūṣadatun).

statements.heading: F.91. Al-Šams
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read fa-lā yaḫāfu with fāʾ and the rest with wāw.[455] Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī apply ʾimālah to all the ends of the verses of this sūrah except for His speech talāhā (Q91:2) and ṭaḥāhā (Q91:6). Ḥamzah applies (pure) fatḥah to those. ʾAbū ʿAmr pronounces all of these in between (i.e., wa-ḍuḥǟhā, talǟhā) and the rest pronounce it with pure fatḥ (i.e., wa-ḍuḥāhā, talāhā).

footnotes.text: This is a regional rasm variant (Sidky 2020, 142).

statements.heading: F.92.–F.93. Al-Layl ʾIḏā Yaġšā and al-Ḍuḥā
statements.text: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī apply ʾimālah to the ends of the verses of both (sūrahs) except for His speech saǧā (Q93:2), as Ḥamzah applied (pure) fatḥah to it (and al-Kisāʾī ʾimālah, i.e., saǧē). ʾAbū ʿAmr applies ʾimālah to li-l-yusrē (Q92:7) and li-l-ʿusrē (Q92:10), and he pronounces what remains in between (i.e., yaġšǟ, aḍ-ḍuḥǟ, saǧǟ). Warš pronounces all of that in between (i.e., also li-l-yusrǟ and li-l-ʿusrǟ). The rest pronounce it with pure fatḥ (i.e., yaġšā, aḍ-ḍuḥā and saǧā).

statements.heading: F.94.–F.95. There is No Disagreement in ʾA-Lam Našraḥ and Wa-l-Tīn
statements.text: Except what has already preceded in the general principles.

statements.heading: F.96. Al-ʿAlaq
statements.text: Qunbul reads ʾan raʾahū with shortness of the hamzah and the rest with length (i.e., raʾāhū̆). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī apply ʾimālah to the ends of the verses of this sūrah from His speech la-yaṭġē (Q96:6) up until His speech bi-ʾanna ḷḷāha yarē (Q96:14). As for ʾAbū ʿAmr, (he applies ʾimālah to) yarē only and he pronounces what remains in between (i.e., la-yaṭġǟ, etc.). Warš pronounces all of that in between (i.e., la-yaṭġǟ, yarǟ, etc.). The rest pronounce it with pure fatḥ (i.e., la-yaṭġā, yarā, etc.).

statements.heading: F.97. Al-Qadr
statements.text: Al-Kisāʾī reads ḥattā maṭliʿa l-faǧri with kasrah on the lām and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., maṭlaʿa).

statements.heading: F.98. Al-Barīʾah[456]
statements.text: Nāfiʿ and Ibn Ḏakwān read al-barīʾati in the two places with hamzah and the rest read it without hamzah and with gemination of the yāʾ for both (i.e., al-bariyyati).

footnotes.text: This is an alternative name for Sūrat al-Bayyinah (Kandil 1992, 54).

statements.heading: F.99. Al-Zalzalah
statements.text: Hišām reads ḫayran yarah and šarran yarah without a vowel on the hāʾ. The rest pronounce it with ṣilah (of the wāw) (i.e., yarahū).

statements.heading: F.100. Wa-l-ʿĀdiyāt
statements.text: I have already mentioned the manner of ʾAbū ʿAmr in assimilating wa-l-ʿādiyāḍ⸗ḍabḥan. His manner and the manner of Ḫallād in assimilation fa-l-muġīrāṣ⸗ṣabḥan (has been discussed) earlier.[457]

statements.heading: F.101. Al-Qāriʿah
statements.text: Ḥamzah reads mā hiya without hāʾ in connected speech. The rest retains it in connected speech and pause (i.e., mā hiyah(#)).

statements.heading: F.102. ʾAlhākum[458]
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read la-turawunna with ḍammah on the tāʾ and the rest with fatḥah (i.e., la-tarawunna). There is no disagreement in His speech ṯumma la-tarawunnahā (Q102:7).

footnotes.text: This is an alternative name for Sūrat al-Takāṯur (Kandil 1992, 54).

statements.heading: F.104. Al-Humazah
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ǧammaʿa mālan with gemination of the mīm and the rest read it without gemination (i.e., ǧamaʿa).

statements.heading: F.104. Al-Humazah
statements.text: ʾAbū Bakr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read fī ʿumudin with two ḍammahs and the rest read it with two fatḥahs (i.e., ʿamadin).

statements.heading: F.106. Qurayš
statements.text: Ibn ʿĀmir reads li-ʾilāfi without yāʾ after the hamzah and the rest read it with yāʾ.[459] They all agree on the addition of the yāʾ in the word despite (its absence in) the writing after the hamzah in ʾīlāfihim(ū) (Q106:2).[460]

statements.heading: F.109. Al-Kāfirūna
statements.text: Hišām reads ʿēbidūna, ʿēbidun and ʿēbidūna with ʾimālah and the rest with fatḥ (i.e., ʿābidūna, ʿābidun, ʿābidūna). It has already been mentioned.[461]

statements.heading: F.109. Al-Kāfirūna
statements.text: Nāfiʿ, al-Bazzī with some disagreement, Ḥafṣ and Hišām read wa-liya dīni with fatḥah on the yāʾ and the rest read it without a vowel (i.e., wa-lī). This is what is well-known for al-Bazzī and I adopt it.

statements.heading: F.111. Al-Masad
statements.text: Ibn Kaṯīr reads yadā ʾabī lahbin without a vowel on the hāʾ and the rest read it with fatḥah (i.e., lahabin).

statements.heading: F.111. Al-Masad
statements.text: ʿĀṣim reads ḥammālata l-ḥaṭabi with naṣb of the tāʾ and the rest read it with rafʿ (i.e., ḥammālatu).

statements.heading: F.112. Al-ʾIḫlāṣ
statements.text: Ḥafṣ reads kufuwan with dammah on the fāʾ and fatḥah on the wāw without hamzah. Ḥamzah reads it with no vowel on the fāʾ with hamzah in connected speech (i.e., kufʾan) and when he pauses, he replaces the hamzah with a wāw that carries a fatḥah following what is written (i.e., kufwā#).[462] The regular rule (qiyās) is to place the vowel (of the hamzah) on the fāʾ (i.e., kufā#). The rest reads it with ḍammah on the fāʾ and with hamzah (i.e., kufuʾan).

statements.heading: F.113.–F.114. There Is No Disagreement in al-Falaq and al-Nās
statements.text: Except what has preceded in the general principles in the main body of the book. Success comes from God.

statements.heading: F.115. The Chapter That Mentions the takbīr in the Reading of Ibn Kaṯīr
statements.text: Know—May God support you—that al-Bazzī transmitted from Ibn Kaṯīr along his ʾisnād that he used to say the takbīr (aḷḷāhu ʾakbar) from the end of Wa-l-Ḍuḥā (Q93) on completing each sūrah up until the end of qul ʾaʿūḏu bi-rabbi n-nās (Q114), and he connects the takbīr (without pause following it) at the end of the sūrah. If the reciter wants to pause to draw breath (he does so after saying the takbīr), then he starts at the tasmiyah (i.e., saying #bi-smi llāhi r-raḥmāni r-raḥīmi), connecting it to the beginning of the sūrah that comes after it (i.e., wa-ʾammā bi-niʿmati rabbika fa-ḥaddiṯ illāhu ʾakbar# bi-smi llāhi r-raḥmāni r-raḥīmi ʾa-lam našraḥ laka ṣadrak#). If he wishes, he can connect the takbīr to the tasmiyah and connect the tasmiyah to the beginning of the sūrah but it is not allowed to draw breath on the tasmiyah if the takbīr is connected (i.e., wa-ʾammā bi-niʿmati rabbika fa-ḥaddiṯ illāhu ʾakbaru bi-smi llāhi r-raḥmāni rraḥīmi ʾa-lam našraḥ laka ṣadrak#, not wa-ʾammā bi-niʿmati rabbika fa-ḥaddiṯ illāhu ʾakbaru bi-smi llāhi r-raḥmāni r-raḥīm# ʾa-lam našraḥ laka ṣadrak#). Some of the people of oral tradition draw breath at the end of the sūrahs and then begin with the takbīr connecting it (without drawing breath) to the tasmiyah (i.e., wa-ʾammā bi-niʿmati rabbika fa-ḥaddiṯ# ʾaḷḷāhu ʾakbaru bi-smi llāhi r-raḥmāni r-raḥīmi ʾa-lam našraḥ laka ṣadrak#). Al-Naqqāš transmitted it like this from ʾAbū Rabīʿah from al-Bazzī. I recited it like that to [ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz b. Ǧaʿfar] al-Fārisī transmitting from him. The hadiths narrated from the Meccans on the takbīr are indicative of what we start with, because maʿa ‘along with’ is in it, and that points to their closeness and togetherness.[463] After he says the takbīr at the end of Sūrat al-Nās (Q114), he recites Fātiḥat al-Kitāb (Q1) and five verses from the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqarah according to the count of the Kufans up until the speech of the Almighty wa-ʾulāʾika humu l-mufliḥūna (Q2:5) and then he prays the closing prayer. This is called al-ḥāllu al-murtaḥilu ‘one who arrives and sets off anew (lit. the arriver-departer)’. For all of what has come before, there are famous hadiths which the scholars transmitted and which support each other and indicate the soundness of what Ibn Kaṯīr did. We have mentioned these elsewhere. The people of the oral tradition disagreed on the wording of the takbīr. Some of them said it was aḷḷāhu ʾakbar and nothing else. Their evidence for the soundness of this is that all the hadiths transmitted that without anything additional. This is what our master ʾAbū al-Fatḥ narrated to us, saying: ʾAbū al-Ḥasan [Ibn Ġalbūn] the teacher of recitation narrated to us, saying: ʾAḥmad b. Salm narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥasan b. Maḫlad narrated to us, saying: al-Bazzī narrated to us, saying: I recited to ʿIkrimah b. Sulaymān, who said, “I recited to ʾIsmāʿīl b. ʿAbd Aḷḷāh b. Qusṭanṭīn [= b. al-Qusṭ] and I had arrived at Wa-ḍ-Ḍuḥā (Q93) and he said, ‘Pronounce the takbīr when you finish it along with the end of each sūrah’. So I recited it to ʿAbd Aḷḷāh b. Kaṯīr and he ordered me to do so.”[464] Ibn Kaṯīr narrated to me that he had recited to Muǧāhid and he ordered him to do so, and Muǧāhid narrated that he recited to ʿAbd Aḷḷāh b. ʿAbbās and he ordered him to do so, and Ibn ʿAbbās narrated that he recited to ʾUbayy b. Kaʿb and he ordered him to do so, and he narrated that he recited to the messenger of God (ṣ) and he ordered him to do so. There are others that say lā ʾilāha ʾillà ḷḷāhu wa-ḷḷāhu ʾakbar, so they say the tahlīl before the takbīr. They indicate the soundness of that by what Fāris b. ʾAḥmad al-Muqriʾ narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Bāqī b. al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: ʾAḥmad b. Salm al-Ḫuttulī and ʾAḥmad b. Ṣāliḥ[465] narrated to us, and they said: al-Ḥasan al-Ḥubāb narrated to us, saying: “I asked al-Bazzī about the takbīr, ‘How does it go?’ He said to me, ‘lā ʾilāha ʾillà ḷḷāhu wa-ḷḷāhu ʾakbar’.” ʾAbū ʿAmr [al-Dānī] said: This Ibn al-Ḥubāb due to his mastery, precision and soundness of speech, has a status recognised by every scholar of this craft. This is how I recited it to ʾAbū al-Fatḥ. I recited to others what has preceded (i.e., saying only aḷḷāhu ʾakbar). F.115.1. Subsection Know that the reciter, when he attaches the takbīr at the closure of a sūrah that ends in an unvocalised letter, adds a kasrah due to the meeting of two unvocalised letters, for example, fa-ḥaddiṯ illāhu ʾakbaru (Q93:11) and fa-rġab illāhu ʾakbaru (Q94:8). If it is tanwīn that the verse ends in, he applies kasrah to that too. It is like that regardless of whether a letter carries tanwīn with fatḥah, ḍammah or kasrah, for example, in tawwāban illāhu ʾakbaru (Q110), la-ḫabīrun illāhu ʾakbaru (Q100), min masadin illāhu ʾakbaru (Q111) and what is like it. If the end of the sūrah carries a fatḥah, he applies the fatḥah, if it carries a kasrah, he applies the kasrah and if it ends with a ḍammah, he applies the ḍammah, for example, in the speech of the Almighty ʾiḏā ḥasada ḷḷāhu ʾakbar (Q113), wa-n-nāsi llāhu ʾakbar (Q114), al-ʾabtaru ḷḷāhu ʾakbar (Q108) and what is like it. If the end of the sūrah is a pronominal hāʾ with a ṣilah of wāw, one removes this ṣilah due to the meeting of two unvocalised letters, for example, rabbahu ḷḷāhu ʾakbar (Q98) and šarran yarahu ḷḷāhu ʾakbar (Q99). So, the ʾalif al-waṣl that is at the beginning of the name of God Almighty is dropped in all of these, as there is no need for it. So, know that, succeeding upon the path of truth and the manner of correctness. Success comes from God. The book has been completed with praise for God and with his help. May God bless our master Muḥammad, his family and his companions and grant them peace. God is sufficient for us, and He is the best judge. There is no might nor strength except with God, the High and the Mighty. Praise be to God alone. BIBLIOGRAPHY ʾAḫfaš al-ʾAwsaṭ, ʾAbū Ḥasan Saʿīd b. Masʿadah al-. 1990. Maʿānī al-Qurʾān. footnotes.text: The hadith al-Dānī is referring to is paraphrased a few paragraphs below. The crux is in the use of maʿa ‘with’ in fa-lammā balaġtu ḍ-ḍuḥā qāla ‘kabbir ḥattā yaḫtima maʿa ḫātimati kull sūrah’ “When I arrived at al-Ḍuḥā, he said ‘Pronounce the takbīr when you finish it along with (maʿa) the end of each sūrah.’” The hadith is less paraphrased in the Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān. There the wording is attributed to ʾUbayy who said the Prophet ordered him to do so (al-Dānī 2007, 1739).
This ʾisnād is absent in the Taysīr and Ǧāmiʿ al-bayān.
